docs.text: Diagrams Visual overviews of how Crispy Waffle is put together. Each diagram is an SVG file stored in docs/images/diagrams ; click any diagram to open it at full size. Diagram What it shows Package architecture The core package, its facades, and which integration packages plug into which extension point Logging pipeline How a log call reaches every registered provider, and how exceptions are handled Caching The write path (all repositories) and the read path (priority order, promotion to memory) Events and commands One-to-many event dispatch versus one-to-one command dispatch through the service locator Background jobs The CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs pipeline and the job lifecycle with retries Package architecture The core CrispyWaffle package exposes static facades such as LogConsumer , CacheManager and ServiceLocator . Integration packages implement the core extension points ( ILogProvider , ICacheRepository , ITelemetryClient , IExceptionHandler ). Packages that open connections to external services also reference CrispyWaffle.Configuration . Each module and package has its own page under Core Modules and Integration Packages. BackgroundJobs and HttpClient are standalone and build on Microsoft.Extensions.* . Logging pipeline LogConsumer resolves a category from the calling namespace, checks every ILogFilter for each provider, and writes to every registered ILogProvider that passes. Exceptions sent to LogConsumer.Handle go to the configured IExceptionHandler . The default handler records telemetry and writes to its own provider list ( AddLogProvider<T>(ExceptionLogType) ), separate from LogConsumer 's providers. See the Logging guide for usage. Caching CacheManager.SetAsync writes to every repository in parallel. CacheManager.GetAsync tries repositories in priority order and returns the first hit; a value found outside memory is copied into MemoryCacheRepository in the background. See the Caching guide for usage. Events and commands EventsConsumer finds every IEventHandler<TEvent> implementation by scanning the loaded assemblies and calls each one in discovery order. CommandsConsumer resolves exactly one ICommandHandler<TCommand, TResult> and returns its result. Both look up handlers through the ServiceLocator . See the Events , Commands and Service Locator guides for usage. Background jobs JobDispatcher saves a pending job to an IJobStore (in memory or EF Core). BackgroundWorker loops fetch due jobs, find the handler registered under the job's name, and run it in a DI scope. Failed jobs are retried with exponential backoff until MaxAttempt is reached. See the BackgroundJobs package for usage.

docs.text: Getting started This page wires up the most common CrispyWaffle features in a console application: dependency registration, logging, caching, events and commands. Each step links to the module page with the full reference. 1. Install the core package dotnet add package CrispyWaffle Integration packages (Redis, RabbitMQ, ElasticSearch and others) are installed the same way. See Installation for the full list. 2. Register services CrispyWaffle features are exposed as static facades ( LogConsumer , CacheManager , EventsConsumer , CommandsConsumer ). They find their collaborators through the ServiceLocator , so register those first. using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Adapters; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Handlers; ServiceLocator.Register<IConsoleLogAdapter, StandardConsoleLogAdapter>(Lifetime.Singleton); ServiceLocator.Register<IExceptionHandler, NullExceptionHandler>(Lifetime.Singleton); For larger applications, group registrations in a class that implements IBootstrapper and call ServiceLocator.RegisterBootstrapper<TBootstrapper>() . 3. Log Add one or more providers to LogConsumer . Every message goes to every provider. Providers start at LogLevel.Production (fatal, error, warning and info), so raise the level to see trace and debug output. using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Providers; LogConsumer.AddProvider<ConsoleLogProvider>().SetLevel(LogLevel.All); LogConsumer.Info("Application started"); LogConsumer.Debug("Current time: {0:HH:mm:ss}", DateTime.Now); 4. Cache Add one or more repositories to CacheManager . Writes go to every repository; reads return the first hit in priority order. using CrispyWaffle.Cache; CacheManager.AddRepository<MemoryCacheRepository>(); await CacheManager.SetAsync("Crispy Waffle", "app-name"); await CacheManager.SetAsync("cached for 10 minutes", "short-lived", TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10)); var name = await CacheManager.GetAsync<string>("app-name"); 5. Raise events An event is a class implementing IEvent ; every IEventHandler<TEvent> implementation handles it. The ServiceLocator discovers handlers by scanning the loaded assemblies, so they need no explicit registration. See Events . using CrispyWaffle.Events; public sealed class UserCreatedEvent : IEvent { public UserCreatedEvent(string email) => Email = email; public string Email { get; } } public sealed class SendWelcomeEmail : IEventHandler<UserCreatedEvent> { public void Handle(UserCreatedEvent args) => LogConsumer.Info("Sending welcome e-mail to {0}", args.Email); } EventsConsumer.Raise(new UserCreatedEvent("someone@example.com")); 6. Send commands A command has exactly one handler, which returns a result. If a handler with a parameterless constructor is the only implementation, it is resolved automatically; otherwise register it. See Commands . using CrispyWaffle.Commands; public sealed class SumCommand : ICommand { public int A { get; init; } public int B { get; init; } } public sealed class SumCommandHandler : ICommandHandler<SumCommand, int> { public int Handle(SumCommand command) => command.A + command.B; } var total = CommandsConsumer.Raise<SumCommand, int>(new SumCommand { A = 2, B = 3 }); Next steps Browse the core modules and integration packages in the navigation. See how the pieces fit together on the Diagrams page. Look at the test projects for more working examples.

docs.text: Attributes The CrispyWaffle.Attributes namespace contains four small attributes that attach metadata to enum fields and to properties. They do nothing on their own; other parts of the library read them: HumanReadableAttribute and InternalValueAttribute give enum fields a display text and an external code. The enum helpers in EnumExtensions read them (see Extensions ). QueryStringBuilderIgnoreAttribute and QueryStringBuilderKeyNameAttribute control how QueryStringBuilder.AddFromType turns an object into query string parameters (see Utilities ). Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.Attributes How it works Enum attributes Both enum attributes are restricted to fields ( AttributeTargets.Field ), so they are applied to enum members. The core library uses HumanReadable on its own enums, such as Lifetime and LogLevel . Reader in CrispyWaffle.Extensions.EnumExtensions Behavior GetHumanReadableValue(this Enum value, string flagsSeparator = " \| ") Returns the field's HumanReadable text, or null when the field has none. For a [Flags] value with more than one flag set, returns the texts of every set flag joined by flagsSeparator , or "None" when no non-zero flag matches. In that case every set flag must have the attribute, or an IndexOutOfRangeException is thrown. GetEnumByHumanReadableAttribute<T>(string humanReadableValue) Returns the field whose HumanReadable text or field name equals the value, ignoring case. Throws InvalidOperationException when T is not an enum and ArgumentOutOfRangeException when nothing matches. GetInternalValue(this Enum value) Returns the field's InternalValue text, or null when the field has none. GetEnumByInternalValueAttribute<T>(string internalValue) Returns the field whose InternalValue text or field name equals the value, ignoring case. Returns default(T) for null . Throws InvalidOperationException when T is not an enum and ArgumentOutOfRangeException when nothing matches. HumanReadableAttribute is marked [Localizable(true)] and is meant for text shown to users. InternalValueAttribute takes a [Localizable(false)] value and is meant for codes exchanged with other systems (database values, API codes, file formats). Query string attributes Both query string attributes are restricted to properties ( AttributeTargets.Property ). QueryStringBuilder.AddFromType<T>(T instance, bool convertCamelCaseToUnderscore = true) walks the public properties of T : A property marked with QueryStringBuilderIgnore is skipped. The parameter name is the QueryStringBuilderKeyName value when present, otherwise the property name. When convertCamelCaseToUnderscore is true (the default), every upper-case letter after the first character is replaced with _ plus the lower-case letter. This also applies to names set with QueryStringBuilderKeyName , so [QueryStringBuilderKeyName("pageSize")] produces page_size . A name that starts with the type name is rewritten as typename[rest] . The value is the property's ToString() result, or an empty string for null . Getting started using System; using CrispyWaffle.Attributes; using CrispyWaffle.Extensions; var status = OrderStatus.Shipped; Console.WriteLine(status.GetHumanReadableValue()); // Shipped to customer Console.WriteLine(status.GetInternalValue()); // SHP var fromCode = EnumExtensions.GetEnumByInternalValueAttribute<OrderStatus>("pnd"); Console.WriteLine(fromCode); // Pending public enum OrderStatus { [HumanReadable("Waiting for payment")] [InternalValue("PND")] Pending, [HumanReadable("Shipped to customer")] [InternalValue("SHP")] Shipped, } Reference HumanReadableAttribute [AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Field)] public sealed class HumanReadableAttribute : Attribute — the display text of an enum field. Member Description HumanReadableAttribute(string value) Constructor. value is the display text. StringValue The display text passed to the constructor. InternalValueAttribute [AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Field)] public sealed class InternalValueAttribute : Attribute — an internal or external code for an enum field. Member Description InternalValueAttribute(string value) Constructor. value is the code. InternalValue The code passed to the constructor. QueryStringBuilderIgnoreAttribute [AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Property)] public sealed class QueryStringBuilderIgnoreAttribute : Attribute — excludes a property from QueryStringBuilder.AddFromType . It has no members. The presence of the attribute is checked with the PropertyInfo.QueryStringBuilderIgnore() extension method in CrispyWaffle.Extensions.TypeExtensions . QueryStringBuilderKeyNameAttribute [AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Property)] public sealed class QueryStringBuilderKeyNameAttribute : Attribute — sets the parameter name used for a property by QueryStringBuilder.AddFromType . The value is read with the PropertyInfo.GetQueryStringBuilderKeyName() extension method in CrispyWaffle.Extensions.TypeExtensions , which returns null when the attribute is absent. Member Description QueryStringBuilderKeyNameAttribute(string keyName) Constructor. keyName is the parameter name. KeyName The parameter name passed to the constructor. Examples Parse user input into an enum Matching is case-insensitive and also accepts the field name. This pattern comes from the test suite. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Attributes; using CrispyWaffle.Extensions; var a = EnumExtensions.GetEnumByHumanReadableAttribute<TestEnum>("Três"); // TestEnum.Three var b = EnumExtensions.GetEnumByHumanReadableAttribute<TestEnum>("três"); // TestEnum.Three var c = EnumExtensions.GetEnumByHumanReadableAttribute<TestEnum>("Two"); // TestEnum.Two (field name) Console.WriteLine(TestEnum.Two.GetHumanReadableValue()); // Dois public enum TestEnum { [InternalValue("ноль")] [HumanReadable("Zero")] None = 0, [InternalValue("один")] [HumanReadable("Um")] One = 1, [InternalValue("два")] [HumanReadable("Dois")] Two = 2, [InternalValue("три")] [HumanReadable("Três")] Three = 3, } Build a query string from an object Rename one property and skip another. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Attributes; using CrispyWaffle.Utilities; var filter = new SearchFilter { Text = "waffles", Page = 2, CacheKey = "not-sent", }; var query = new QueryStringBuilder().AddFromType(filter).ToString(); Console.WriteLine(query); // ?q=waffles&Page=2 public sealed class SearchFilter { [QueryStringBuilderKeyName("q")] public string Text { get; set; } public int Page { get; set; } [QueryStringBuilderIgnore] public string CacheKey { get; set; } } See also Extensions Utilities Service Locator

docs.text: Caching The caching module gives you one static entry point, CacheManager , in front of one or more cache repositories. Writes go to every registered repository; reads walk the repositories in priority order and return the first hit. Use it when you want a fast in-process cache, a shared distributed cache, or both layered together. The core package ships MemoryCacheRepository . Distributed repositories live in separate packages: RedisCacheRepository in CrispyWaffle.Redis and CouchDBCacheRepository in CrispyWaffle.CouchDB . You can also write your own by implementing ICacheRepository . Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.Cache How it works Registration and priority. CacheManager keeps its repositories in a list sorted by an integer priority. Lower numbers are queried first. AddRepository overloads without a priority use an internal counter that starts at 0 and increments on every such call. When you pass an explicit priority that is already taken, the manager increments it until it finds a free slot, so a call never fails because of a collision. The repository list is static and lives for the life of the process; there is no way to remove a repository once added. Writes. SetAsync calls SetAsync on every repository in parallel and waits for all of them with Task.WhenAll . A repository that throws is logged through LogConsumer.Error and skipped; the others still store the value. Cancellation inside a single repository is swallowed (a message is written to the console) and is not rethrown. SetAsync therefore never reports a partial failure to the caller. SetToAsync writes to exactly one repository, selected by its concrete type. Reads. GetAsync and TryGetAsync query repositories one at a time, in priority order, through each repository's TryGetAsync . The first repository that reports success wins and the rest are not queried. A repository that throws is logged and skipped. When no repository has the key, GetAsync throws InvalidOperationException and TryGetAsync returns a failure result. Promotion to memory. If a MemoryCacheRepository is registered and the hit comes from a different repository, the value is copied into the memory repository in a fire-and-forget background task ( SetToAsync<MemoryCacheRepository, T> ). Subsequent reads are served from memory if the memory repository has a lower priority number than the remote one. Promotion failures are logged and never surface to the caller. Promotion ignores the remote TTL, because the memory repository does not support expiration. Timeouts and cancellation. Every read and remove operation that goes through repositories ( GetAsync , GetFrom , GetFromAsync , TryGetAsync , Remove , RemoveFrom ) runs under a fixed 10-second timeout linked to your CancellationToken . If the timeout fires, the manager throws TimeoutException . If your token is cancelled, the OperationCanceledException is rethrown. The timeout is not configurable. SetAsync , SetToAsync and TTLAsync do not use the timeout. TTL. Expiration is a repository feature. SetAsync(value, key, ttl) passes the TTL to each repository; MemoryCacheRepository ignores it. TTLAsync asks each repository in priority order and returns the first non-zero value, or TimeSpan.Zero if every repository returns zero. Typed selection. SetToAsync , GetFrom , GetFromAsync and RemoveFrom locate the repository whose runtime type is exactly TCacheRepository (not a base type or interface). If none matches they throw InvalidOperationException . If more than one registered repository has that type, SingleOrDefault throws InvalidOperationException as well. Getting started using System.Threading.Tasks; using CrispyWaffle.Cache; public static class Program { public static async Task Main() { CacheManager.AddRepository(new MemoryCacheRepository()); await CacheManager.SetAsync("some string text", "MyKey"); var value = await CacheManager.GetAsync<string>("MyKey"); // "some string text" var (found, cached) = await CacheManager.TryGetAsync<string>("OtherKey"); // found == false, cached == null await CacheManager.Remove("MyKey"); } } Reference CacheManager public static class CacheManager — static facade that fans writes out to all registered ICacheRepository instances and reads from the first one that has the key. All key and subKey arguments are strings. Every method that takes a CancellationToken defaults it to default . Methods check the token on entry and throw OperationCanceledException if it is already cancelled. Registration Member Description AddRepository<TCacheRepository>() Resolves TCacheRepository from ServiceLocator and adds it with the next automatic priority. TCacheRepository must implement ICacheRepository . Returns the resolved repository as ICacheRepository . AddRepository(ICacheRepository repository) Adds an existing instance with the next automatic priority. Returns the same instance. AddRepository<TCacheRepository>(int priority) Resolves TCacheRepository from ServiceLocator and adds it at priority (or the next free slot above it). Returns the resolved repository. AddRepository(ICacheRepository repository, int priority) Adds an instance at priority , incrementing until a free slot is found. Returns the int priority actually used. Writing Member Description SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Stores value under key in every repository, in parallel. Returns ValueTask . Per-repository errors are logged and swallowed. SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same as above, using a key plus sub-key (hash field). SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, TimeSpan ttl, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same as the first overload, passing ttl to each repository. Repositories that do not support expiration ignore it. SetToAsync<TCacheRepository, TValue>(TValue value, string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Stores the value only in the repository whose type is exactly TCacheRepository . Throws InvalidOperationException if that repository is not registered. Errors from the repository itself are logged and swallowed. SetToAsync<TCacheRepository, TValue>(TValue value, string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same, with a sub-key. SetToAsync<TCacheRepository, TValue>(TValue value, string key, TimeSpan ttl, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same, passing ttl to the repository. SetToAsync<TCacheRepository, TValue>(TValue value, string key, string subKey, TimeSpan ttl, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Stores the value with a sub-key in one repository. Note: ttl is currently ignored; the call is forwarded to the sub-key overload without a TTL. Reading Member Description GetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Returns ValueTask<T> with the first value found, querying repositories in priority order and promoting remote hits to memory. Throws InvalidOperationException if no repository has the key, TimeoutException after 10 seconds. GetAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same, for a key plus sub-key. TryGetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Returns ValueTask<(bool Success, T Value)> . Success is false and Value is default(T) when no repository has the key. Same ordering, promotion and timeout as GetAsync . TryGetAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Returns ValueTask<bool> only: true if any repository has the key and sub-key. The value itself is not returned (it is still promoted to memory). Use GetAsync<T>(key, subKey) to read it. GetFrom<TCacheRepository, TValue>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Reads from the single repository whose type is exactly TCacheRepository , via that repository's GetAsync . Returns ValueTask<TValue> . Throws InvalidOperationException if the repository is not registered or (for most repositories) if the key is missing, TimeoutException after 10 seconds. No promotion. GetFromAsync<TCacheRepository, TValue>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same as GetFrom , for a key plus sub-key. Note the Async suffix, which the single-key overload lacks. TTLAsync(string key) Returns Task<TimeSpan> : the first non-zero TTL reported by a repository in priority order, or TimeSpan.Zero . No cancellation token and no timeout. Removing Member Description Remove(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Removes key from every repository, sequentially in priority order. Returns ValueTask . Errors from individual repositories are swallowed without logging. Throws TimeoutException after 10 seconds. Remove(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same, for a key plus sub-key. RemoveFrom<TCacheRepository>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Removes key only from the repository whose type is exactly TCacheRepository . Throws InvalidOperationException if it is not registered; repository errors propagate. RemoveFrom<TCacheRepository>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same, for a key plus sub-key. ICacheRepository public interface ICacheRepository — contract every cache backend implements so it can be registered with CacheManager . Implement this to plug in your own store. CacheManager reads through TryGetAsync , so make sure it returns (false, default) rather than throwing on a miss. Member Description ShouldPropagateExceptions bool , get/set. Whether the implementation should rethrow backend errors instead of swallowing them. Honoring it is up to the implementation. SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, TimeSpan? ttl = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Stores a value. ttl is the optional time to live. Returns ValueTask . SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Stores a value under a key and sub-key. Returns ValueTask . GetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) / GetAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Returns ValueTask<T> . Expected to throw InvalidOperationException when the key does not exist. TryGetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) / TryGetAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Returns ValueTask<(bool Success, T Value)> . RemoveAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) / RemoveAsync(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Removes the entry. Returns Task . TTLAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Returns Task<TimeSpan> : the remaining time to live, or TimeSpan.Zero if expired, missing or unsupported. Clear() Removes every entry. Returns Task . MemoryCacheRepository public class MemoryCacheRepository : ICacheRepository — in-process cache backed by ConcurrentDictionary instances. The backing dictionaries are static , so every MemoryCacheRepository instance in the process shares the same data, and Clear() on one instance clears all of them. Values are stored as object references, not serialized copies: mutating a cached reference type mutates the cached value. There is no expiration and no size limit. Member Description MemoryCacheRepository() Default constructor. ShouldPropagateExceptions Settable, but not used by this implementation. SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, TimeSpan? ttl, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Adds or replaces the value. ttl is ignored. SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Adds or replaces the value in a separate sub-key store, under the composite key "{key}-{subKey}" . GetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Returns the value cast to T . Throws InvalidOperationException if the key is missing, InvalidCastException if the value is not a T . GetAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same, for the sub-key store. TryGetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) / TryGetAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Returns (true, value) when found and castable to T ; (false, default(T)) when missing or of a different type. RemoveAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Removes the key if present. RemoveAsync(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Intended to remove the sub-key entry. docs.text: The caching module gives you one static entry point, CacheManager , in front of one or more cache repositories. Writes go to every registered repository; reads walk the repositories in priority order and return the first hit. Use it when you want a fast in-process cache, a shared distributed cache, or both layered together. The core package ships MemoryCacheRepository . Distributed repositories live in separate packages: RedisCacheRepository in CrispyWaffle.Redis and CouchDBCacheRepository in CrispyWaffle.CouchDB . You can also write your own by implementing ICacheRepository . Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.Cache
docs.title: Caching

docs.text: Registration and priority. CacheManager keeps its repositories in a list sorted by an integer priority. Lower numbers are queried first. AddRepository overloads without a priority use an internal counter that starts at 0 and increments on every such call. When you pass an explicit priority that is already taken, the manager increments it until it finds a free slot, so a call never fails because of a collision. The repository list is static and lives for the life of the process; there is no way to remove a repository once added. Writes. SetAsync calls SetAsync on every repository in parallel and waits for all of them with Task.WhenAll . A repository that throws is logged through LogConsumer.Error and skipped; the others still store the value. Cancellation inside a single repository is swallowed (a message is written to the console) and is not rethrown. SetAsync therefore never reports a partial failure to the caller. SetToAsync writes to exactly one repository, selected by its concrete type. Reads. GetAsync and TryGetAsync query repositories one at a time, in priority order, through each repository's TryGetAsync . The first repository that reports success wins and the rest are not queried. A repository that throws is logged and skipped. When no repository has the key, GetAsync throws InvalidOperationException and TryGetAsync returns a failure result. Promotion to memory. If a MemoryCacheRepository is registered and the hit comes from a different repository, the value is copied into the memory repository in a fire-and-forget background task ( SetToAsync<MemoryCacheRepository, T> ). Subsequent reads are served from memory if the memory repository has a lower priority number than the remote one. Promotion failures are logged and never surface to the caller. Promotion ignores the remote TTL, because the memory repository does not support expiration. Timeouts and cancellation. Every read and remove operation that goes through repositories ( GetAsync , GetFrom , GetFromAsync , TryGetAsync , Remove , RemoveFrom ) runs under a fixed 10-second timeout linked to your CancellationToken . If the timeout fires, the manager throws TimeoutException . If your token is cancelled, the OperationCanceledException is rethrown. The timeout is not configurable. SetAsync , SetToAsync and TTLAsync do not use the timeout. TTL. Expiration is a repository feature. SetAsync(value, key, ttl) passes the TTL to each repository; MemoryCacheRepository ignores it. TTLAsync asks each repository in priority order and returns the first non-zero value, or TimeSpan.Zero if every repository returns zero. Typed selection. SetToAsync , GetFrom , GetFromAsync and RemoveFrom locate the repository whose runtime type is exactly TCacheRepository (not a base type or interface). If none matches they throw InvalidOperationException . If more than one registered repository has that type, SingleOrDefault throws InvalidOperationException as well.

docs.text: public static class CacheManager — static facade that fans writes out to all registered ICacheRepository instances and reads from the first one that has the key. All key and subKey arguments are strings. Every method that takes a CancellationToken defaults it to default . Methods check the token on entry and throw OperationCanceledException if it is already cancelled. Registration Member Description AddRepository<TCacheRepository>() Resolves TCacheRepository from ServiceLocator and adds it with the next automatic priority. TCacheRepository must implement ICacheRepository . Returns the resolved repository as ICacheRepository . AddRepository(ICacheRepository repository) Adds an existing instance with the next automatic priority. Returns the same instance. AddRepository<TCacheRepository>(int priority) Resolves TCacheRepository from ServiceLocator and adds it at priority (or the next free slot above it). Returns the resolved repository. AddRepository(ICacheRepository repository, int priority) Adds an instance at priority , incrementing until a free slot is found. Returns the int priority actually used. Writing Member Description SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Stores value under key in every repository, in parallel. Returns ValueTask . Per-repository errors are logged and swallowed. SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same as above, using a key plus sub-key (hash field). SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, TimeSpan ttl, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same as the first overload, passing ttl to each repository. Repositories that do not support expiration ignore it. SetToAsync<TCacheRepository, TValue>(TValue value, string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Stores the value only in the repository whose type is exactly TCacheRepository . Throws InvalidOperationException if that repository is not registered. Errors from the repository itself are logged and swallowed. SetToAsync<TCacheRepository, TValue>(TValue value, string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same, with a sub-key. SetToAsync<TCacheRepository, TValue>(TValue value, string key, TimeSpan ttl, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same, passing ttl to the repository. SetToAsync<TCacheRepository, TValue>(TValue value, string key, string subKey, TimeSpan ttl, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Stores the value with a sub-key in one repository. Note: ttl is currently ignored; the call is forwarded to the sub-key overload without a TTL. Reading Member Description GetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Returns ValueTask<T> with the first value found, querying repositories in priority order and promoting remote hits to memory. Throws InvalidOperationException if no repository has the key, TimeoutException after 10 seconds. GetAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same, for a key plus sub-key. TryGetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Returns ValueTask<(bool Success, T Value)> . Success is false and Value is default(T) when no repository has the key. Same ordering, promotion and timeout as GetAsync . TryGetAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Returns ValueTask<bool> only: true if any repository has the key and sub-key. The value itself is not returned (it is still promoted to memory). Use GetAsync<T>(key, subKey) to read it. GetFrom<TCacheRepository, TValue>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Reads from the single repository whose type is exactly TCacheRepository , via that repository's GetAsync . Returns ValueTask<TValue> . Throws InvalidOperationException if the repository is not registered or (for most repositories) if the key is missing, TimeoutException after 10 seconds. No promotion. GetFromAsync<TCacheRepository, TValue>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same as GetFrom , for a key plus sub-key. Note the Async suffix, which the single-key overload lacks. TTLAsync(string key) Returns Task<TimeSpan> : the first non-zero TTL reported by a repository in priority order, or TimeSpan.Zero . No cancellation token and no timeout. Removing Member Description Remove(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Removes key from every repository, sequentially in priority order. Returns ValueTask . Errors from individual repositories are swallowed without logging. Throws TimeoutException after 10 seconds. Remove(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same, for a key plus sub-key. RemoveFrom<TCacheRepository>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Removes key only from the repository whose type is exactly TCacheRepository . Throws InvalidOperationException if it is not registered; repository errors propagate. RemoveFrom<TCacheRepository>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Same, for a key plus sub-key.

docs.text: public class MemoryCacheRepository : ICacheRepository — in-process cache backed by ConcurrentDictionary instances. The backing dictionaries are static , so every MemoryCacheRepository instance in the process shares the same data, and Clear() on one instance clears all of them. docs.text: Commands Commands ask the application to do something and return a result. A command is a plain class that implements ICommand . Exactly one handler, implementing ICommandHandler<TCommand, TResult> or ICommandHandlerAsync<TCommand, TResult> , processes it, and CommandsConsumer returns the handler's result to the caller. Use commands for one-to-one requests that produce a value. To notify any number of listeners without a result, use events . Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.Commands How it works CommandsConsumer.Raise<TCommand, TResult>(command) calls ServiceLocator.Resolve<ICommandHandler<TCommand, TResult>>() , writes a trace message through LogConsumer.Trace , and returns the value of Handle(command) . RaiseAsync does the same with ICommandHandlerAsync<TCommand, TResult> and returns the handler's Task<TResult> directly. Both type arguments must be given explicitly, because TResult cannot be inferred. The handler is found by the normal service locator rules: If the handler interface is registered (for example ServiceLocator.Register<ICommandHandler<MyCommand, MyResult>, MyCommandHandler>() ), that registration is used. Register the handler when its constructor takes dependencies. Otherwise the locator auto-registers the only non-abstract class that implements the interface and has a public parameterless constructor. The handler instance is then cached and reused as a singleton. If no handler is found, Raise throws InvalidOperationException ("No registrations for ..."). If more than one candidate is found, it throws TooManyImplementationsException . The handler runs on the calling thread, and exceptions it throws propagate to the caller. Getting started using System; using CrispyWaffle.Commands; public sealed class HelloWorldCommand : ICommand { } public sealed class HelloWorldCommandHandler : ICommandHandler<HelloWorldCommand, string> { public string Handle(HelloWorldCommand command) => "Hello World, this is the result of the triggered command!"; } public static class Program { public static void Main() { var result = CommandsConsumer.Raise<HelloWorldCommand, string>(new HelloWorldCommand()); Console.WriteLine(result); } } Reference CommandsConsumer public static class CommandsConsumer — sends a command to its handler and returns the result. Member Description TResult Raise<TCommand, TResult>(TCommand command) Constraint: TCommand : ICommand . Resolves ICommandHandler<TCommand, TResult> and returns Handle(command) . Throws InvalidOperationException when no handler can be resolved and TooManyImplementationsException when several unregistered candidates exist. Task<TResult> RaiseAsync<TCommand, TResult>(TCommand command) Constraint: TCommand : ICommand . Resolves ICommandHandlerAsync<TCommand, TResult> and returns HandleAsync(command) . Resolution errors are thrown synchronously, before a task is returned. ICommand public interface ICommand — marker interface for command classes. It has no members. Put the command's input in properties of the class. ICommandHandler<TCommand, TResult> public interface ICommandHandler<in TCommand, out TResult> where TCommand : ICommand — handles a command synchronously. Member Description TResult Handle(TCommand command) Processes the command and returns its result. ICommandHandlerAsync<TCommand, TResult> public interface ICommandHandlerAsync<in TCommand, TResult> where TCommand : ICommand — handles a command asynchronously. Member Description Task<TResult> HandleAsync(TCommand command) Processes the command and returns a task with its result. Examples Returning a class as a result The command carries input data and the handler returns a result object. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Commands; using CrispyWaffle.Log; var result = CommandsConsumer.Raise<SomeCommand, SomeCommandResult>(new SomeCommand(10)); Console.WriteLine($"New quantity: {result.Quantity}"); public sealed class SomeCommand(int quantity) : ICommand { public Guid Id { get; } = Guid.NewGuid(); public DateTime Date { get; } = DateTime.Now; public int Quantity { get; } = quantity; } public sealed class SomeCommandResult(int newQuantity) { public int Quantity { get; } = newQuantity; } public sealed class SomeCommandHandler : ICommandHandler<SomeCommand, SomeCommandResult> { public SomeCommandResult Handle(SomeCommand command) { LogConsumer.Warning( "Command 'SomeCommand' handled by 'SomeCommandHandler'. Command Id: {0}", command.Id ); return new SomeCommandResult(command.Quantity * 2); } } Synchronous and asynchronous handling in one class This pattern comes from the test suite. The same class implements both handler interfaces. using System; using System.Threading.Tasks; using CrispyWaffle.Commands; var command = new TestDoneCommand(Guid.NewGuid(), "Sample test"); var result = CommandsConsumer.Raise<TestDoneCommand, TestDoneResultCommand>(command); var resultAsync = await CommandsConsumer.RaiseAsync<TestDoneCommand, TestDoneResultCommand>( command ); public sealed class TestDoneCommand(Guid identifier, string text) : ICommand { public Guid Identifier { get; } = identifier; public string Text { get; } = text; public DateTime CreatedDateTime { get; } = DateTime.UtcNow; } public sealed class TestDoneResultCommand(string text) { public string Text { get; } = text; } public sealed class TestDoneCommandHandler : ICommandHandler<TestDoneCommand, TestDoneResultCommand>, ICommandHandlerAsync<TestDoneCommand, TestDoneResultCommand> { public TestDoneResultCommand Handle(TestDoneCommand command) => new($"Sample done action handled: {command.Identifier} - {command.Text}"); public Task<TestDoneResultCommand> HandleAsync(TestDoneCommand command) => Task.Run(() => new TestDoneResultCommand( $"Sample done action handled: {command.Identifier} - {command.Text}" ) ); } A handler with dependencies Handlers without a parameterless constructor are not auto-registered. Register them explicitly; their dependencies are injected by the service locator. using CrispyWaffle.Commands; using CrispyWaffle.Composition; ServiceLocator.Register<IPriceCatalog, FixedPriceCatalog>(Lifetime.Singleton); ServiceLocator.Register<ICommandHandler<GetPriceCommand, decimal>, GetPriceCommandHandler>(); var price = CommandsConsumer.Raise<GetPriceCommand, decimal>(new GetPriceCommand("SKU-1")); public interface IPriceCatalog { decimal PriceOf(string sku); } public sealed class FixedPriceCatalog : IPriceCatalog { public decimal PriceOf(string sku) => 9.99m; } public sealed class GetPriceCommand(string sku) : ICommand { public string Sku { get; } = sku; } public sealed class GetPriceCommandHandler : ICommandHandler<GetPriceCommand, decimal> { private readonly IPriceCatalog _catalog; public GetPriceCommandHandler(IPriceCatalog catalog) => _catalog = catalog; public decimal Handle(GetPriceCommand command) => _catalog.PriceOf(command.Sku); } See also Events Service Locator Logging Diagrams

docs.text: Cryptography The cryptography module has one static class, Security . It provides symmetric string encryption and decryption (AES-256 in CBC mode, with a key derived from a password) and string hashing with MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2 and, on .NET 8 or later, SHA-3. These helpers exist for compatibility with data produced by earlier versions of the library. Read Security notes before you use them for new data. Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.Cryptography How it works Encryption and decryption Encrypt and Decrypt are extension methods on string . Both take the same three secrets: passwordHash , saltKey and viKey . Step Detail Key derivation new Rfc2898DeriveBytes(passwordHash, Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(saltKey)).GetBytes(32) . This is PBKDF2 with the .NET defaults for this constructor: HMAC-SHA1 and 1,000 iterations. The password is UTF-8 encoded by Rfc2898DeriveBytes ; the salt is ASCII encoded (non-ASCII characters become ? ). The result is a 256-bit key. Initialization vector Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(viKey) , used as is. It must be exactly 16 ASCII characters (one 128-bit block). Any other length throws ArgumentException ("Specified initialization vector (IV) does not match the block size for this algorithm."). Cipher RijndaelManaged with its default 128-bit block size, CipherMode.CBC . With a 256-bit key this is AES-256-CBC. Padding Encrypt uses PaddingMode.Zeros . Decrypt uses PaddingMode.None and then removes all trailing '\0' characters from the decoded text. Plain text encoding UTF-8. Cipher text encoding Base64 of the raw cipher text. The output contains only the cipher text: no salt, IV, version or authentication tag. Encryption is deterministic: the same plain text with the same three secrets always gives the same output. Hashing Security.Hash(value, type) UTF-8 encodes value , computes the hash with the selected algorithm and converts the bytes to a string. The string format depends on the algorithm: Algorithm Output format Md5 Lowercase hexadecimal, two characters per byte (32 characters). This is the usual MD5 hex string. All others Each byte as an unpadded decimal number ( 0 to 255 ), concatenated with no separator. For example, bytes 0x05 0xA0 become "5160" . The non-MD5 format is not the standard hex encoding, so it does not match the output of other tools ( sha256sum , Convert.ToHexString ), and it has variable length. Different hashes can also produce the same string, because the byte boundaries are lost. Compare these values only with other values produced by Security.Hash . The hash algorithm objects are created once, in a static field, and shared by all calls. Getting started using System; using CrispyWaffle.Cryptography; const string password = "123456"; const string salt = "12345678"; const string iv = "HZEM7|Ne2YGS/F41"; // exactly 16 ASCII characters var encrypted = "PlainText".Encrypt(password, salt, iv); // "vBWW26e4f9QMRPjz4pXoEQ==" var decrypted = encrypted.Decrypt(password, salt, iv); // "PlainText" var md5 = Security.Hash("PlainText", HashAlgorithmType.Md5); // "b7ebbf7f254ef646928dd58f62383a85" Console.WriteLine($"{encrypted} {decrypted} {md5}"); Reference Security public static class Security — string encryption, decryption and hashing helpers. Member Description Encrypt(this string plainText, string passwordHash, string saltKey, string viKey) Encrypts plainText with AES-256-CBC and zero padding, as described in How it works . Returns the cipher text as Base64. Throws ArgumentException when viKey is not 16 ASCII bytes. Throws ArgumentNullException when any argument is null . Decrypt(this string encryptedText, string passwordHash, string saltKey, string viKey) Decodes Base64 and decrypts with the same parameters. Returns the UTF-8 text with trailing '\0' characters removed. Throws FormatException for invalid Base64, ArgumentException for an invalid IV length, and CryptographicException when the cipher text length is not a multiple of 16 bytes. Wrong secrets do not throw; they return unreadable text. Hash(string value, HashAlgorithmType type) Returns the hash of value in the format described in Hashing . Throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException ( Invalid algorithm type ) for a type that is not supported on the current target framework. Throws ArgumentNullException when value is null . HashAlgorithmType public enum HashAlgorithmType — algorithm selector for Security.Hash . Value Description Md5 MD5 (128-bit). Output is lowercase hex. Sha1 SHA-1 (160-bit). Sha256 SHA-256. Sha384 SHA-384. Sha512 SHA-512. Sha3_256 SHA3-256. Only defined when the library is compiled for .NET 8 or later. Sha3_384 SHA3-384. Only defined when the library is compiled for .NET 8 or later. Sha3_512 SHA3-512. Only defined when the library is compiled for .NET 8 or later. Examples Hash with each algorithm using System; using CrispyWaffle.Cryptography; foreach (var type in new[] { HashAlgorithmType.Md5, HashAlgorithmType.Sha1, HashAlgorithmType.Sha256 }) { Console.WriteLine($"{type}: {Security.Hash("PlainText", type)}"); } // Md5: b7ebbf7f254ef646928dd58f62383a85 // Sha1: 5022439192242211661341747135888248197192199115101 // Sha256: 43167247186156224140100585014234839723255150225212687216120565623113068401650 Keep secrets out of code Read the three secrets from configuration instead of constants. The IV still has to be 16 ASCII characters. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Cryptography; var password = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("APP_CRYPTO_PASSWORD"); var salt = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("APP_CRYPTO_SALT"); var iv = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("APP_CRYPTO_IV"); var token = "customer-42".Encrypt(password, salt, iv); var original = token.Decrypt(password, salt, iv); Security notes These points come from the code in Security.cs : No integrity protection. The output is unauthenticated AES-CBC. An attacker who can change the cipher text can change the decrypted plain text in predictable ways, and Decrypt will not detect it. Do not use this for data that crosses a trust boundary without a separate MAC or signature. Fixed IV. The IV comes from a caller-supplied string and is reused for every message. Equal plain texts produce equal cipher texts, and messages that share a prefix produce cipher texts that share a prefix. Each message should have a random IV. Fixed salt. The salt is also a caller-supplied constant, so the derived key is the same for every message. Weak key derivation. PBKDF2 uses the Rfc2898DeriveBytes constructor defaults: HMAC-SHA1 with 1,000 iterations, far below current recommendations. Treat passwordHash as a high-entropy secret, not a human password. Zero padding. Plain text that ends with '\0' characters loses them on decryption. Obsolete APIs. RijndaelManaged and the Rfc2898DeriveBytes(string, byte[]) constructor are marked obsolete in recent .NET versions (SYSLIB0022 and SYSLIB0041). Weak hash algorithms. Md5 and Sha1 are broken for collision resistance. Do not use them for signatures or integrity checks. None of the hash options is suitable for password storage: they are fast, unsalted hashes. Use a password hashing function (PBKDF2 with a high iteration count, bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2) for passwords. Thread safety. Hash reuses one HashAlgorithm instance per algorithm, stored in a static dictionary. HashAlgorithm.ComputeHash is not thread-safe, so concurrent calls with the same algorithm can return wrong results or throw. Synchronize calls if you hash from several threads. SHA-3 availability. On .NET 8 or later, the SHA-3 instances are created in the same static initializer as the others. .NET throws PlatformNotSupportedException from SHA3_256.Create() and its siblings on platforms without SHA-3 support, which would surface as a TypeInitializationException the first time Hash runs on such a platform. See also Extensions Utilities

docs.text: Events Events let one part of an application announce that something happened without knowing who reacts to it. An event is a plain class that implements IEvent . Any number of handler classes implement IEventHandler<TEvent> (synchronous) or IEventHandlerAsync<TEvent> (asynchronous), and EventsConsumer delivers the event to all of them. Use events for one-to-many notifications with no return value. When you need exactly one handler and a result, use commands . Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.Events How it works EventsConsumer.Raise(event) calls ServiceLocator.ResolveAll<IEventHandler<TEvent>>() . ResolveAll does not look at registrations to find handlers: it scans every type loaded when the service locator was initialized and creates one instance of each non-abstract class that implements the handler interface. You do not need to register handlers. Handler constructors can take dependencies, which are resolved by the service locator; a handler class that is registered under its own type (for example Register<MyHandler>(Lifetime.Singleton) ) is created through that registration. Handlers are called one after another on the calling thread, in the order their types appear in the loaded assemblies. That order is not the registration order and should not be relied on. Before each call, a trace message is written through LogConsumer.Trace . If a handler throws, the exception propagates to the caller of Raise and the remaining handlers are not called. EventsConsumer.RaiseAsync(event) resolves IEventHandlerAsync<TEvent> handlers the same way, inside Task.Run , and calls HandleAsync on each of them in turn. The returned tasks are not awaited. As a result: The task returned by RaiseAsync completes once every handler has been started, usually before the handlers have finished their asynchronous work. An exception thrown before a handler's first await faults the RaiseAsync task and stops the remaining handlers. An exception thrown after the first await is not observed by the caller. If a handler must finish before you continue, raise the event synchronously, or have the handler signal completion itself. The two handler interfaces are independent: Raise only calls IEventHandler<TEvent> implementations and RaiseAsync only calls IEventHandlerAsync<TEvent> implementations. A class can implement both. Getting started using System; using CrispyWaffle.Events; public sealed class OrderPlacedEvent : IEvent { public OrderPlacedEvent(Guid orderId) => OrderId = orderId; public Guid OrderId { get; } } public sealed class SendConfirmationEmail : IEventHandler<OrderPlacedEvent> { public void Handle(OrderPlacedEvent args) => Console.WriteLine($"Sending confirmation for order {args.OrderId}"); } public static class Program { public static void Main() { // No registration needed: every IEventHandler<OrderPlacedEvent> is found automatically. EventsConsumer.Raise(new OrderPlacedEvent(Guid.NewGuid())); } } Reference EventsConsumer public static class EventsConsumer — raises events and invokes their handlers. Member Description Raise<TEvent>(TEvent @event) Constraint: TEvent : IEvent . Calls Handle on every IEventHandler<TEvent> implementation, synchronously and sequentially. Exceptions from a handler propagate and stop the remaining handlers. Does nothing if there are no handlers. RaiseAsync<TEvent>(TEvent @event) Constraint: TEvent : IEvent . Returns Task . Calls HandleAsync on every IEventHandlerAsync<TEvent> implementation on a thread-pool thread without awaiting the handler tasks. See "How it works" for completion and error behavior. IEvent public interface IEvent — marker interface for event classes. It has no members. Put the data the handlers need in properties of the event class. IEventHandler<TEvent> public interface IEventHandler<in TEvent> where TEvent : IEvent — handles an event synchronously. Member Description void Handle(TEvent args) Called by EventsConsumer.Raise with the raised event. IEventHandlerAsync<TEvent> public interface IEventHandlerAsync<in TEvent> where TEvent : IEvent — handles an event asynchronously. Member Description Task HandleAsync(TEvent args) Called by EventsConsumer.RaiseAsync with the raised event. The returned task is not awaited by the consumer. Examples Several handlers for the same event Each handler class is discovered and called. Handlers can take constructor dependencies. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Events; using CrispyWaffle.Log; // Both handlers run. EventsConsumer.Raise(new SomeEvent("Some text passed to all event handlers")); public sealed class SomeEvent : IEvent { public SomeEvent(string data) { Id = Guid.NewGuid(); Date = DateTime.Now; Data = data; } public Guid Id { get; } public string Data { get; } public DateTime Date { get; } } public sealed class SomeEventHandler : IEventHandler<SomeEvent> { public void Handle(SomeEvent args) => LogConsumer.Warning( "Event 'SomeEvent' handled by 'SomeEventHandler'. Event Id: {0}", args.Id ); } public sealed class AnotherSomeEventHandler : IEventHandler<SomeEvent> { public void Handle(SomeEvent args) => LogConsumer.Warning( "Event 'SomeEvent' handled by 'AnotherSomeEventHandler'. Event Id: {0}", args.Id ); } One class handling an event both ways This pattern comes from the test suite. Raise calls Handle ; RaiseAsync calls HandleAsync . using System; using System.Threading.Tasks; using CrispyWaffle.Events; using CrispyWaffle.Log; var @event = new TestDoneEvent(Guid.NewGuid(), "Sample test"); EventsConsumer.Raise(@event); await EventsConsumer.RaiseAsync(@event); // Returns once LogDoneEvent.HandleAsync has started. public sealed class TestDoneEvent : IEvent { public TestDoneEvent(Guid identifier, string text) { Identifier = identifier; Text = text; CreatedDateTime = DateTime.Now; } public Guid Identifier { get; } public string Text { get; } public DateTime CreatedDateTime { get; } } public sealed class LogDoneEvent : IEventHandler<TestDoneEvent>, IEventHandlerAsync<TestDoneEvent> { public void Handle(TestDoneEvent args) => LogConsumer.Info( "Sample done action handled: {0} - {1} - {2:dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm:ss}", args.Identifier, args.Text, args.CreatedDateTime ); public async Task HandleAsync(TestDoneEvent args) => await Task.Run(() => LogConsumer.Info( "Sample done action handled: {0} - {1} - {2:dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm:ss}", args.Identifier, args.Text, args.CreatedDateTime ) ); } Handling exceptions from a handler An exception thrown by a synchronous handler reaches the caller of Raise . using System; using CrispyWaffle.Events; try { EventsConsumer.Raise(new ExceptionEvent(Guid.NewGuid())); } catch (NotImplementedException e) { Console.WriteLine($"Handler failed: {e.Message}"); } public sealed class ExceptionEvent : IEvent { public ExceptionEvent(Guid identifier) => Identifier = identifier; public Guid Identifier { get; } } public sealed class ThrowExceptionEvent : IEventHandler<ExceptionEvent> { public void Handle(ExceptionEvent args) => throw new NotImplementedException(args.Identifier.ToString()); } See also Commands Service Locator Logging Diagrams

docs.text: An exception thrown by a synchronous handler reaches the caller of Raise . using System; using CrispyWaffle.Events; try { EventsConsumer.Raise(new ExceptionEvent(Guid.NewGuid())); } catch (NotImplementedException e) { Console.WriteLine($"Handler failed: {e.Message}"); } public sealed class ExceptionEvent : IEvent { public ExceptionEvent(Guid identifier) => Identifier = identifier; public Guid Identifier { get; } } public sealed class ThrowExceptionEvent : IEventHandler<ExceptionEvent> { public void Handle(ExceptionEvent args) => throw new NotImplementedException(args.Identifier.ToString()); }

docs.text: Extension methods The CrispyWaffle.Extensions namespace holds a set of static helper classes, mostly extension methods, for common chores: converting strings to numbers and dates, cleaning and reshaping text, reading enum attributes, flattening exception chains, rounding integers, reflecting over types and reading XML. Each class has no state and no dependencies to wire up. Add using CrispyWaffle.Extensions; and the methods appear on the types they extend. Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.Extensions How it works Most methods are forgiving. They return a neutral value ( 0 , string.Empty , the original input, or false ) for null, empty or whitespace input instead of throwing. The exceptions to this rule are listed in each table: for example ToDateTime throws on empty input, and Levenshtein does not check for null. A few methods depend on legacy code pages that .NET (Core) does not load by default: RemoveDiacritics and LevenshteinInvariantCulture use code page 1251. ToSafeUrl uses ISO-8859-8. On .NET Core and .NET 5 or later, register the code pages provider once at startup before you call these methods. The library does not do it for you. using System.Text; Encoding.RegisterProvider(CodePagesEncodingProvider.Instance); Parsing methods ( ToInt32 , ToInt64 , ToDecimal , ToMonetary , TryToDateTime ) use the current culture unless noted. Getting started using System; using CrispyWaffle.Extensions; var quantity = "1,250".ToInt32(); // 1250 under en-US; 0 if parsing fails var due = "tomorrow".ToDateTime(); // DateTime.Today.AddDays(1) var active = "s".ToBoolean(); // true: matches the default "S", case-insensitive var title = "republica federativa do brasil".ToCamelCase(); // "Republica Federativa Do Brasil" var slots = 15.RoundUp(); // 20 var place = 22.ToOrdinal(); // "22nd" Reference ConversionExtensions public static class ConversionExtensions — conversions between strings, numbers, dates, booleans, bytes, JSON and XML. Member Extends Description ToBoolean(string validValueForTrue = "S") string Returns true only when the string equals validValueForTrue (case-insensitive). Any other value, including null, returns false . The default "S" is the Portuguese "Sim". ToString(string trueValue, string falseValue) bool Returns trueValue or falseValue . ToDateTime() string Parses with the same rules as TryToDateTime . Throws ArgumentNullException when the input is null or whitespace, and ArgumentOutOfRangeException when it cannot be parsed. TryToDateTime(out DateTime value) string Accepts the keywords now , today , yesterday and tomorrow (case-insensitive, trimmed), then DateTime.TryParse with the current culture, then the exact format dd/MM/yyyy for 10-character input. Returns false and DateTime.MinValue on failure. ToInt32() / ToInt64() / ToDecimal() string Parses with NumberStyles.Number and the current culture. Returns 0 for null, whitespace or unparseable input. ToBytes() IEnumerable<string> Converts each base-2 string (for example "01000001" ) to a byte. Throws FormatException on non-binary input. ToBinaryString() IEnumerable<byte> Converts each byte to an 8-character base-2 string. ToMonetary(CultureInfo cultureInfo = null) decimal Formats with {0:C} in cultureInfo or the current culture. Returns the literal "No value" for 0 . ToUnixTimeStamp() DateTime Converts to UTC and returns the number of seconds since 1970-01-01 as an int . FromUnixTimeStamp() int Converts an epoch value to a local DateTime . The value is divided by 1000 (and rounded) before it is added as seconds, so it is treated as milliseconds. It is therefore not the inverse of ToUnixTimeStamp . ToPrettyString() string Re-formats a JSON object or array with indentation (Newtonsoft.Json). Returns string.Empty for null or whitespace and returns the input unchanged when IsValidJson is false . ToIdentString() XmlDocument Serializes the document with tab indentation and CRLF line breaks. Returns null for a null document. ToModule10() string Strips non-digits and computes a modulus-10 check digit with alternating weights 2 and 1 from the right (products of 10 or more have their digits summed). Returns 0 – 9 . ToOrdinal() int , long Appends an English ordinal suffix ( 1st , 2nd , 3rd , 11th , 22nd ). Negative numbers are returned without a suffix. DeepClone<T>(bool useNonPublic = true) T Builds a new T by calling its public constructor with the most parameters. Each argument comes from a property with the same name (case-insensitive) and exact type: public properties first, then non-public ones when useNonPublic is true . Property values are passed by reference, so nested objects are shared and the copy is shallow. Returns default when T has no public constructor. If a constructor parameter has no matching property, the argument list is too short and the constructor call throws. StringExtensions public static class StringExtensions — cleaning, formatting, encoding and comparing strings. All methods are marked [Pure] . Member Extends Description RemoveNonNumeric() string Removes every character except 0 – 9 . RemoveNonAlphanumeric() string Removes every character that is not a word character ( \w ), . , @ or - . ReplaceNonAlphanumeric(string replaceWith) string Like RemoveNonAlphanumeric , but replaces each character with replaceWith . RemoveSpaces() string Removes all whitespace. RemoveExcessSpaces() string Replaces each run of two or more whitespace characters with a single space. The pattern is [\t\|\s]{2,} , so runs of \| characters are replaced as well. RemoveDiacritics() string Removes accents by round-tripping through code page 1251 and ASCII. Requires the code pages provider on .NET Core (see How it works ). ReplaceFirst(string search, string replaceWith) string Replaces the first ordinal occurrence of search . Returns the input unchanged when search is not found. Abbreviate(int maxCharacters, bool addEllipsis = true) string Returns the input unchanged when it is shorter than maxCharacters . Otherwise truncates to maxCharacters - 4 characters and appends "..." (or to maxCharacters characters with no ellipsis). Returns string.Empty for null or whitespace. ToCamelCase() string Splits on spaces, lowercases each word and capitalizes its first letter, then joins with single spaces. Despite the name, the result is title case: "hello WORLD" becomes "Hello World" . Returns string.Empty for null or whitespace. ToUcWords() string Lowercases the text, then uppercases each a – z letter at the start of the text or after whitespace, / or a digit. UcWords(string[] toUpper, string[] toLower) string[] Joins the words, each preceded by a space (so the result starts with a space). A word is fully uppercased when its uppercase form is in toUpper , lowercased when its lowercase form is in toLower , and passed to ToCamelCase otherwise. ToSafeUrl() string Builds a URL slug: transcodes through ISO-8859-8, removes - and . , collapses spaces, replaces remaining non-word characters with - and trims - from both ends. Case is preserved. Requires the code pages provider on .NET Core. ToBase64() string Encodes the UTF-8 bytes as Base64. Returns string.Empty for null or whitespace. FromBase64(string encoding = "ISO-8859-1") string Decodes Base64 and reads the bytes with encoding . Because the default is ISO-8859-1 and ToBase64 uses UTF-8, non-ASCII text does not round-trip unless you pass "UTF-8" . FromISO2UTF8() string Encodes the string as ISO-8859-1, converts the bytes to UTF-8 and decodes them. Characters outside ISO-8859-1 become ? . ToValidFileName() string Replaces runs of characters from Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars() , and trailing dots, with _ . Throws ArgumentNullException for null. Levenshtein(string inputToCompare) string Returns the Levenshtein edit distance (case-sensitive). Throws NullReferenceException if either string is null. LevenshteinInvariantCulture(string inputToCompare) string Removes diacritics and lowercases both strings, then calls Levenshtein . Requires the code pages provider on .NET Core. GetPathOrFileName() string Parses an absolute URL. Returns the file name when the path has an extension, otherwise the absolute path. Throws UriFormatException for relative or malformed URLs. GetFileName() Uri Returns Path.GetFileName of the local path, or string.Empty . GetFileExtension() Uri , string Returns the extension including the leading dot (for example .pdf ), or string.Empty . ToCenter(char spacer, int lineSize) string Pads both sides with lineSize - input.Length / 2 copies of spacer (one more on the right for odd lengths). lineSize is effectively half the final width: the result is about 2 * lineSize characters long. IsValidJson() string Returns true when the trimmed string starts and ends with {} or [] and parses with JToken.Parse . Returns false for null, scalars and parse errors. SplitBy(int chunkLength) string Lazily yields chunks of chunkLength characters (the last may be shorter). Yields a single string.Empty for null or whitespace input. Throws ArgumentException when chunkLength < 1 ; because the method is an iterator, the exception surfaces on first enumeration. StripTags() string Removes everything from each < to the next > . Returns string.Empty for null or whitespace. EnumExtensions public static class EnumExtensions — reads and resolves the HumanReadable and InternalValue attributes on enum fields. See Attributes . Member Extends Description GetHumanReadableValue(string flagsSeparator = " \| ") Enum Returns the [HumanReadable] text of the value, or null if the field has none. For a [Flags] enum with more than one bit set, joins the text of each set single-bit flag with flagsSeparator . In that case every set flag must have the attribute, or an IndexOutOfRangeException is thrown. Throws ArgumentNullException when a non-flags value does not match a declared field. GetInternalValue() Enum Returns the [InternalValue] text of the value, or null if the field has none. GetUniqueFlags<T>() Enum Lazily yields each declared single-bit value (as T , usually the enum type) that is set in the value. GetEnumByHumanReadableAttribute<T>(string humanReadableValue) — (static) Returns the field of enum T whose [HumanReadable] text or field name equals humanReadableValue (case-insensitive). Throws InvalidOperationException when T is not an enum or more than one field matches, and ArgumentOutOfRangeException when nothing matches. GetEnumByInternalValueAttribute<T>(string internalValue) — (static) Same as above, using [InternalValue] . Returns default(T) when internalValue is null. ExceptionExtensions public static class ExceptionExtensions — flattens an exception chain and formats it. The logging infrastructure's default exception handler uses these methods; see Logging . Member Extends Description ToQueue(out List<Type> types) Exception Returns a queue holding the exception and all its inner exceptions, with the innermost exception first and the original exception last. types receives the types of the inner exceptions only (not the outer one), ordered from outer to inner. GetMessages(string category, ICollection<ILogProvider> additionalProviders) Queue<Exception> Dequeues every exception (the queue is empty afterwards) and builds one string with each message, the exception type name in brackets, and the stack trace. Entries after the first are prefixed with Exception rethrow at [n]: and a space, where n is the entry's position. For each exception, also calls Error(category, message) on every provider in additionalProviders , which must not be null. MathExtensions public static class MathExtensions — rounds integers to a multiple. Member Extends Description RoundDown(int multipleOf = 10) int Rounds down to the nearest multiple ( 15 becomes 10 ). Negative values round toward zero. RoundUp(int multipleOf = 10, bool forceDifferentValue = false) int Rounds up to the next multiple ( 11 becomes 20 ). An exact multiple is returned unchanged unless forceDifferentValue is true , in which case multipleOf is added. RoundBest(int multipleOf = 10, bool forceDifferentValue = false) int Rounds to the nearest multiple: down when the remainder is less than multipleOf / 2 , up otherwise. A remainder of exactly 1 always rounds down. An exact multiple is returned unchanged even when forceDifferentValue is true . TypeExtensions public static class TypeExtensions — reflection helpers. Member Extends Description Implements<TInterface>() Type Returns true when TInterface is assignable from the type. TInterface must be a reference type. IsSimpleType() Type Returns true for value types, primitives, string , decimal , DateTime , DateTimeOffset , TimeSpan , Guid , and any type whose TypeCode is not Object . IsNumericType() Type Returns true for byte , sbyte , the 16-, 32- and 64-bit signed and unsigned integers, decimal , double and float , and for Nullable<T> of any of these. UpdateValues<T>(T newObject) T : IUpdateable Copies values from newObject into the current object and returns the current object. A property is copied when its new value is non-null and differs from the value on a freshly constructed T , or when newObject has a bool ShouldSerialize<PropertyName>() method that returns true . Simple types are assigned directly; properties whose type implements IUpdateable are merged recursively; other reference types (such as collections) are skipped. T needs a public parameterless constructor and settable properties. GetQueryStringBuilderKeyName() PropertyInfo Returns the key from [QueryStringBuilderKeyName] , or null . Used by QueryStringBuilder.AddFromType . QueryStringBuilderIgnore() PropertyInfo Returns true when the property has [QueryStringBuilderIgnore] . GetCallingMethod(int frame = 1, bool excludeBegin = true) — (static) Returns Namespace.Type.Method for the given stack frame ( 1 is the method that called GetCallingMethod ). With excludeBegin , a leading CrispyWaffle. is removed. Returns "CrispyWaffle" when the frame has no method. XmlExtensions public static class XmlExtensions — helpers for XmlReader , XmlDocument and XmlNode . Member Extends Description DuplicateReaders(out XmlReader cloneOne, out XmlReader cloneTwo) XmlReader Loads the reader into an XmlDocument , writes it to a MemoryStream and creates two readers (with IgnoreWhitespace ) over that stream, then closes the original reader. Both clones share the same stream, so they are not independent: read one to the end before you start the other, and expect problems with documents larger than the reader buffer. GetFirstElementByTagName(string tagName) XmlDocument Returns the first element with the tag name, or null . GetNodeValue(string node) XmlNode Evaluates node as an XPath expression against the node and returns the inner text of the first match, or string.Empty . GetNodeValue(string[] nodes) XmlNode Evaluates each expression and joins the inner texts with a space. Missing nodes contribute an empty string. Examples Parse user input safely ToInt32 and TryToDateTime never throw, so they suit form and CSV input. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Extensions; var page = "abc".ToInt32(); // 0 if ("31/12/2020".TryToDateTime(out var date)) // dd/MM/yyyy fallback { Console.WriteLine(date.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")); // 2020-12-31 } Console.WriteLine(1000m.ToMonetary(new System.Globalization.CultureInfo("en-US"))); // $1,000.00 Map enums to display and storage values using CrispyWaffle.Attributes; using CrispyWaffle.Extensions; var label = OrderStatus.Pending.GetHumanReadableValue(); // "Waiting for payment" var code = OrderStatus.Shipped.GetInternalValue(); // "SH" var status = EnumExtensions.GetEnumByInternalValueAttribute<OrderStatus>("sh"); // OrderStatus.Shipped public enum OrderStatus { [HumanReadable("Waiting for payment")] [InternalValue("WP")] Pending = 0, [HumanReadable("Shipped")] [InternalValue("SH")] Shipped = 1, } Flatten an exception chain using System; using System.Collections.Generic; using CrispyWaffle.Extensions; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Providers; try { throw new InvalidOperationException("Outer", new ArgumentException("Inner")); } catch (Exception ex) { var queue = ex.ToQueue(out var innerTypes); // Inner first, then Outer var text = queue.GetMessages("Orders", new List<ILogProvider>()); Console.WriteLine(text); } Compare strings ignoring accents and case using System.Text; using CrispyWaffle.Extensions; Encoding.RegisterProvider(CodePagesEncodingProvider.Instance); var distance = "Three".LevenshteinInvariantCulture("tree"); // 1 See also Attributes for HumanReadable , InternalValue and the query string attributes Utilities for QueryStringBuilder and IUpdateable Validations for the regular expressions used by the string helpers pt-BR internationalization for Brazilian-specific conversions

docs.text: Good practices The CrispyWaffle.GoodPractices namespace holds a few shared exception contracts. Two interfaces describe exceptions that carry the request and response of a failed remote call, so logging and error-handling code can read them without knowing the concrete exception type. One concrete exception reports an invalid telephone number. Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.GoodPractices How it works IRestException and IXmlServiceException are contracts only: the library does not implement or catch them. Implement one on your own exception class when it wraps an HTTP or XML/SOAP call, and check for the interface where you log or report errors. InvalidTelephoneNumberException is thrown by ParseBrazilianPhoneNumber in the CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr package (see I18n PtBr ). Its message contains the input with every non-digit character removed. Getting started using System; using CrispyWaffle.GoodPractices; try { throw new PaymentGatewayException("POST /payments {\"amount\":10}", "HTTP 502 Bad Gateway"); } catch (Exception e) when (e is IRestException rest) { Console.WriteLine($"Request: {rest.Request}"); Console.WriteLine($"Response: {rest.Response}"); } public sealed class PaymentGatewayException : Exception, IRestException { public PaymentGatewayException(string request, string response) : base("The payment gateway call failed.") { Request = request; Response = response; } public string Request { get; } public string Response { get; } } Reference IRestException public interface IRestException — an exception raised during an HTTP REST request/response cycle. Member Description string Request The request that caused the failure, such as the URL, headers or body. string Response The response received, such as the status code and error body. IXmlServiceException public interface IXmlServiceException — an exception raised during an XML service call. The source file is IXMLServiceException.cs , but the type name is IXmlServiceException . Member Description XmlDocument Request The XML document that was sent. XmlDocument Response The XML document that was received. InvalidTelephoneNumberException [Serializable] public class InvalidTelephoneNumberException : Exception — thrown when a value is not a valid telephone number. The message is "The value '{telephoneNumber}' isn't a valid telephone number.". Member Description InvalidTelephoneNumberException(string telephoneNumber) Creates the exception for the given number. protected InvalidTelephoneNumberException(SerializationInfo info, StreamingContext context) Serialization constructor. Examples Catch an invalid Brazilian phone number ParseBrazilianPhoneNumber throws InvalidTelephoneNumberException with the digits of the input. This pattern comes from the CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr test suite. using System; using CrispyWaffle.GoodPractices; using CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr; try { var phone = "abc123def456".ParseBrazilianPhoneNumber(); } catch (InvalidTelephoneNumberException e) { Console.WriteLine(e.Message); // The value '123456' isn't a valid telephone number. } Report the payloads of a failed XML service call using System; using System.Xml; using CrispyWaffle.GoodPractices; var request = new XmlDocument(); request.LoadXml("ABC"); var response = new XmlDocument(); response.LoadXml("404"); try { throw new QuoteServiceException(request, response); } catch (Exception e) when (e is IXmlServiceException xml) { Console.WriteLine(xml.Request.OuterXml); Console.WriteLine(xml.Response.OuterXml); } public sealed class QuoteServiceException : Exception, IXmlServiceException { public QuoteServiceException(XmlDocument request, XmlDocument response) : base("The quote service returned a fault.") { Request = request; Response = response; } public XmlDocument Request { get; } public XmlDocument Response { get; } } See also I18n PtBr Logging Validations
