docs.text: Infrastructure and constants EnvironmentHelper exposes facts about the running process: application name and version, host name, user, IP addresses, operating system, and process ID. Log providers and connectors use these values to label what they write, so setting the application name and the current operation early in startup makes logs easier to filter. The root Constants class holds values used by the validation helpers. It is internal and is not part of the public API. Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.Infrastructure , CrispyWaffle ( Constants , internal) How it works All values are computed once, in the static constructor, the first time any EnvironmentHelper member is accessed. UserAgent is the only value rebuilt on every access. Value Source ApplicationName Name of the entry assembly (or the calling assembly when there is no entry assembly), with spaces replaced by - and converted to lower case. Can be replaced with SetApplicationName . DisplayApplicationName null until SetDisplayApplicationName is called. Operation null until SetOperation is called. Host Environment.MachineName . UserName Environment.UserName . IpAddress The first IPv4, non-loopback unicast address of a network interface that is up. Empty string when none is found. IpAddressExternal The public IPv4 address returned by https://api.ipify.org . Empty string when the request fails or the response is not an IP address. ExecutionPath Assembly.Location of the same assembly used for ApplicationName . Version ProductVersion of that assembly file, or an empty string when ExecutionPath is empty. VersionDate Last write time of that assembly file, local time, formatted as dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm:ss . OperationalSystemVersion Environment.OSVersion , a hyphen, and x64 or x86 depending on whether the operating system is 64-bit. ProcessId ID of the current process. Keep these points in mind: The first access makes a blocking HTTP request to api.ipify.org to get IpAddressExternal . On machines without internet access, the first use of EnvironmentHelper (often the first log entry) can be slow until that request fails. When the entry assembly has no file location (for example, a single-file published application), ExecutionPath is empty and building VersionDate throws, so the static constructor fails with a TypeInitializationException . The Set* methods only store the value. SetApplicationName does not apply the lower-case and - normalization used for the default name. Values are read by the logging and messaging integrations, among others: RollingTextFileLogAdapter and the Elasticsearch and RabbitMQ log providers include the application name, host, IP addresses, operation, process ID and user agent in each entry. The Redis log provider includes the host and IP addresses. The Elasticsearch and RabbitMQ connectors use ApplicationName (and Version for Elasticsearch) in their default index and exchange names. The Redis propagation strategies publish to channels named after Operation or ProcessId . Getting started using System; using CrispyWaffle.Infrastructure; // Set names before the first log entry is written. EnvironmentHelper.SetApplicationName("orders-api"); EnvironmentHelper.SetDisplayApplicationName("Orders API"); EnvironmentHelper.SetOperation("nightly-import"); Console.WriteLine(EnvironmentHelper.ApplicationName); // orders-api Console.WriteLine(EnvironmentHelper.Host); Console.WriteLine(EnvironmentHelper.UserAgent); // orders-api/1.0.0 (H:MY-HOST|P:1234|T:1) Reference EnvironmentHelper public static class EnvironmentHelper — information about the current application, process and machine. Member Description SetApplicationName(string applicationName) Replaces ApplicationName . SetDisplayApplicationName(string displayApplicationName) Sets DisplayApplicationName . SetOperation(string operation) Sets Operation , a free-form name for the job or operation the process is running. ApplicationName Application name used in logs and default resource names. See the table above for the default. DisplayApplicationName Friendly application name. null until set. Operation Current operation name. null until set. Host Machine name. UserName Name of the user running the process. IpAddress Local IPv4 address, or an empty string. IpAddressExternal Public IPv4 address, or an empty string. ExecutionPath Full path of the entry assembly file. Version Product version of the entry assembly, or an empty string. VersionDate Last write time of the entry assembly, as dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm:ss . OperationalSystemVersion Operating system description and bitness, for example Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.22631.0 - x64 . ProcessId int ID of the current process. UserAgent {ApplicationName}/{Version} (H:{Host}\|P:{ProcessId}\|T:{ManagedThreadId}) , where the thread ID is that of the thread reading the property. Constants internal static class Constants — constants for Brazilian tax document validation. Not accessible from application code; listed here for completeness. Member Value Description _BrazilianCorporateDocumentName "CNPJ" Name of the Brazilian corporate taxpayer document. _BrazilianCorporateDocumentFullLength 14 Number of digits in a CNPJ. _BrazilianPersonDocumentName "CPF" Name of the Brazilian individual taxpayer document. _BrazilianPersonDocumentFullLength 11 Number of digits in a CPF. These values are used by PersonalDataValidation in CrispyWaffle.Validations (see Validations ). Examples Tag log output with the current operation Set the operation at the start of each job so that log entries and the Redis operation channel carry its name. using CrispyWaffle.Infrastructure; using CrispyWaffle.Log; EnvironmentHelper.SetOperation("invoice-export"); LogConsumer.Info("Starting {0} on {1}", EnvironmentHelper.Operation, EnvironmentHelper.Host); Send a user agent with outgoing HTTP requests using System.Net.Http; using CrispyWaffle.Infrastructure; using var client = new HttpClient(); client.DefaultRequestHeaders.TryAddWithoutValidation("User-Agent", EnvironmentHelper.UserAgent); See also Logging Telemetry Validations Redis

docs.text: Logging CrispyWaffle logging is a static facade, LogConsumer , that fans each message out to every registered log provider. Providers decide where messages go (console, rolling text files, Log4Net, Redis, RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch, Windows Event Log). Filters decide which provider receives which message, and an exception handler decides what happens to exceptions passed to LogConsumer.Handle . Use it when you want one logging call site in your code and the freedom to add or swap destinations at startup without touching that code. Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.Log , CrispyWaffle.Log.Adapters , CrispyWaffle.Log.Filters , CrispyWaffle.Log.Handlers , CrispyWaffle.Log.Providers How it works The pipeline has four kinds of parts: LogConsumer is the static entry point. It holds a list of providers, a list of filters and one exception handler. Providers ( ILogProvider ) receive a category and a message for each level. You register them with LogConsumer.AddProvider . Adapters ( ILogAdapter and friends) do the actual writing for the two core providers. ConsoleLogProvider writes through an IConsoleLogAdapter and TextFileLogProvider writes through an ITextFileLogAdapter , both resolved from the service locator . Filters ( ILogFilter ) are checked per provider, per message. Sending a message When you call LogConsumer.Info("...") (or any other level), the consumer: Resolves a category by walking the stack trace. It skips frames whose declaring type is in CrispyWaffle.Log* or is a CrispyWaffle type whose name ends with LogProvider , then uses the declaring type's full name (for example MyApp.Services.OrderService ). A leading CrispyWaffle. prefix is removed. For async methods and lambdas this is the compiler-generated type name (for example MyApp.OrderService+<RunAsync>d__0 ). If no frame qualifies, the category is CrispyWaffle . For each provider, calls every registered filter with the provider's full type name, the level, the category and the message. The provider receives the message only if all filters return true . Calls the matching method on each provider that passed, synchronously and in registration order. LogTo<TLogProvider> and DebugTo<TLogProvider> skip the fan-out and target the one registered provider whose runtime type is exactly TLogProvider . They return false when no such provider is registered or a filter rejects the message. The overloads that take params object[] arguments format the message with string.Format(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, ...) before it reaches the providers. Levels LogLevel is a [Flags] enum. Each provider (through its adapter) keeps its own level and drops messages whose level flag is not set. LogConsumer itself does not check levels. The built-in adapters start at LogLevel.Production (Fatal, Error, Warning, Info), so Trace and Debug messages are dropped until you call SetLevel on the provider: LogConsumer.AddProvider<ConsoleLogProvider>().SetLevel(LogLevel.All); Exceptions LogConsumer.Handle(exception) (and the two event-handler overloads) forward to the current IExceptionHandler . The handler is chosen the first time LogConsumer is used (static constructor): it resolves IExceptionHandler from the service locator and, if that fails, falls back to DefaultExceptionHandler and passes it the resolution error. Without a registration, resolution normally fails because the core package already contains two implementations ( DefaultExceptionHandler and NullExceptionHandler ) and auto-registration refuses to pick one. Register your handler before the first logging call, or replace it later with LogConsumer.SetHandler . DefaultExceptionHandler does not write to the providers registered on LogConsumer . It keeps its own static list of providers, added with AddLogProvider<T>(ExceptionLogType) , TryAddConsoleLogProvider() or TryAddTextFileLogProvider() . When it handles an exception it: Resolves a category from the stack trace, the same way LogConsumer does. Unwraps the exception chain (innermost first) and calls TelemetryAnalytics.TrackException for each inner exception type (see Telemetry ). Calls Error(category, message) on each ExceptionLogType.Message provider once per exception in the chain, with just that exception's Message . Calls Error(category, details) once on each ExceptionLogType.Full provider, where details contains every exception's message, type name and stack trace, with Exception rethrow at [n]: markers between them. With no providers added, DefaultExceptionHandler only tracks telemetry. Integration packages Other CrispyWaffle packages add providers and handlers that plug into the same pipeline: Package Adds Log4Net Log4NetLogProvider EventLog EventLogProvider , EventLogAdapter Redis PubSubRedisLogProvider RabbitMQ RabbitMQLogProvider Elasticsearch ElasticSearchLogProvider Elmah ElmahExceptionHandler Threading LogConsumer holds providers and filters in plain collections with no locking, so register them at startup before logging from multiple threads. StandardConsoleLogAdapter and RollingTextFileLogAdapter lock around each write, so concurrent logging through them is safe. Getting started Register an adapter and an exception handler, add a provider, then log. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Adapters; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Handlers; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Providers; public static class Program { public static void Main() { // Adapter used by ConsoleLogProvider. ServiceLocator.Register<IConsoleLogAdapter, StandardConsoleLogAdapter>(Lifetime.Singleton); // Must be registered before the first LogConsumer call. ServiceLocator.Register<IExceptionHandler, NullExceptionHandler>(Lifetime.Singleton); LogConsumer.AddProvider<ConsoleLogProvider>().SetLevel(LogLevel.All); LogConsumer.Info("Hello world Crispy Waffle"); LogConsumer.Debug("Current time: {0:HH:mm:ss}", DateTime.Now); LogConsumer.Warning("Press any key to close the program!"); Console.ReadKey(); } } Reference LogConsumer public static class LogConsumer — static facade that sends messages to every registered provider and exceptions to the exception handler. Methods without a To suffix return void and write to every provider that passes the filters. The category is resolved from the caller; see How it works . Member Description StorageDirectory public static readonly string . <AppDomain base directory>/Logs . Set by the static constructor; not used by the core library. DebugDirectory public static readonly string . StorageDirectory/Debug . Not used by the core library. AddProvider<TLogProvider>() Resolves TLogProvider from ServiceLocator , adds it and returns it as ILogProvider . Constraint: TLogProvider : ILogProvider . AddProvider(ILogProvider provider) Adds an existing provider instance and returns it. AddFilter(ILogFilter filter) Adds a filter. Every filter must return true for a provider to receive a message. SetHandler(IExceptionHandler handler) Replaces the exception handler used by Handle . LogTo<TLogProvider>(LogLevel level, string message) Logs to the single registered provider whose type is exactly TLogProvider . Returns false if none is registered or a filter rejects it. Throws InvalidOperationException if more than one provider of that type is registered, and ArgumentOutOfRangeException if level is a combined value such as Production . DebugTo<TLogProvider>(string content, string identifier) Sends content with an identifier at Debug level to one provider ( ILogProvider.Debug(category, content, identifier) ). Same return rules as LogTo . DebugTo<TLogProvider, T>(T content, string identifier, SerializerFormat customFormat = SerializerFormat.None) Sends an object at Debug level to one provider for serialization. Constraint: T : class, new() . Filters receive an empty message. Debug(string message) / Debug(string message, params object[] arguments) Logs at Debug level. Debug(string content, string identifier) Sends content with an identifier at Debug level ( ILogProvider.Debug(category, content, identifier) ). Note that Debug("text {0}", "value") binds to this overload, not to the formatting one. Debug<T>(T content, string identifier, SerializerFormat customFormat = SerializerFormat.None) Sends an object at Debug level for serialization. Constraint: T : class, new() . Filters receive an empty message. Trace(string message) / Trace(string message, params object[] arguments) Logs at Trace level. Trace(Exception exception) Logs exception details at Trace level. Filters receive exception.Message . Trace(Exception exception, string message) / Trace(Exception exception, string message, params object[] arguments) Logs a message plus exception details at Trace level. Info(string message) / Info(string message, params object[] arguments) Logs at Info level. Warning(string message) / Warning(string message, params object[] arguments) Logs at Warning level. Error(string message) / Error(string message, params object[] arguments) Logs at Error level. Fatal(string message) / Fatal(string message, params object[] arguments) Logs at Fatal level. Handle(Exception exception) Passes the exception to the current IExceptionHandler . Handle(object sender, UnhandledExceptionEventArgs args) Passes the event to the handler. Matches AppDomain.UnhandledException . Handle(object sender, ThreadExceptionEventArgs args) Passes the event to the handler. Matches Application.ThreadException (WinForms). LogLevel [Flags] public enum LogLevel — severity flags. Each value has a [HumanReadable] name used in log output. Value Description Fatal (1) Fatal errors. Human-readable name Fatal . Error (2) Errors. Error . Warning (4) Warnings. Warning . Info (8) Informational messages. Information . Trace (16) Detailed diagnostic messages and exception traces. Trace . Debug (32) Debug messages and content dumps. Debug . Production Fatal \| Error \| Warning \| Info . Default level of the built-in adapters. Development Production \| Trace . All Development \| Debug . LogMessage [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Json)] public sealed class LogMessage — the record RollingTextFileLogAdapter writes for each entry. Also usable by custom providers. All properties have public getters and setters. Member Description Id string . Unique id of the entry (the rolling adapter uses a new GUID). Level string . Human-readable level name. Application string . Application name. Category string . Log category. ProcessId int . Process id. ThreadId int . Managed thread id. ThreadName string . Thread name. Hostname string . Machine host name. IpAddress string . Local IP address. IpAddressRemote string . External IP address. UserAgent string . User agent. Date DateTime . Local time of the entry. Message string . Message text. MessageIdentifier string . Identifier passed to a Debug(content, identifier) call, otherwise the current log file name. Operation string . Current operation. The rolling adapter fills Application , Hostname , IpAddress , IpAddressRemote , Operation , ProcessId and UserAgent from EnvironmentHelper (see Infrastructure ). ILogProvider public interface ILogProvider — a log destination registered with LogConsumer . Implement it to add your own destination. Member Description SetLevel(LogLevel level) Sets the levels this provider writes. Fatal(string category, string message) Writes at Fatal level. Error(string category, string message) Writes at Error level. Warning(string category, string message) Writes at Warning level. Info(string category, string message) Writes at Info level. Trace(string category, string message) Writes at Trace level. Trace(string category, string message, Exception exception) Writes a message and exception details at Trace level. Trace(string category, Exception exception) Writes exception details at Trace level. Debug(string category, string message) Writes at Debug level. Debug(string category, string content, string identifier) Stores content under an identifier (file name, key, and so on; meaning depends on the implementation) at Debug level. Files are named LogFile-{fileNameSeed}-[{n}].txt (or .json ). On start and on each roll, n is increased until the name does not collide with an existing file. Before each write the adapter checks the current file: when it holds maxMessageCount messages or its length has reached maxFileSize , it closes it and opens the next one, so a file can exceed the size limit by one entry. Writes are serialized with a lock per instance. Use one instance per seed; two instances with the same seed and folder write to different numbers but may race on creating them. Each entry is a LogMessage . In LogFileType.Text files, entries are separated by a ---------- line and each property is written as Name: value ( N.A. for empty values). In LogFileType.Json files, the file is kept as a valid JSON array of entries. Exceptions are written as [MainException][Type]: message followed by one [InnerException][Type]: message line per inner exception, without stack traces. The default category is N.A. . Full The provider receives one Error entry with every message, type name and stack trace in the chain. Examples Rolling text files Write to text files that roll every 100 messages or 10 KB. Register the adapter as a singleton so every resolution of TextFileLogProvider shares the same files. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Adapters; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Handlers; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Providers; ServiceLocator.Register<ITextFileLogAdapter>( () => new RollingTextFileLogAdapter( AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory, // folder, must exist "textFileLogs", // file name seed 100, // max messages per file (Unit.KByte, 10), // max file size LogFileType.Text), Lifetime.Singleton); ServiceLocator.Register<IExceptionHandler, NullExceptionHandler>(Lifetime.Singleton); LogConsumer.AddProvider<TextFileLogProvider>(); LogConsumer.Info("Hello world Crispy Waffle"); LogConsumer.Warning("Warning message!"); Logging unhandled exceptions Use the default handler, write exception messages to the console and full details to text files, and hook process-wide unhandled exceptions. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Adapters; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Handlers; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Providers; ServiceLocator.Register<IConsoleLogAdapter, StandardConsoleLogAdapter>(Lifetime.Singleton); ServiceLocator.Register<ITextFileLogAdapter>( () => new RollingTextFileLogAdapter("Logs", "app", 1000, (Unit.MByte, 5), LogFileType.Json), Lifetime.Singleton); ServiceLocator.Register<IExceptionHandler, DefaultExceptionHandler>(Lifetime.Singleton); DefaultExceptionHandler.TryAddConsoleLogProvider(); DefaultExceptionHandler.TryAddTextFileLogProvider(); AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException += LogConsumer.Handle; try { throw new InvalidOperationException("Something failed"); } catch (Exception e) { LogConsumer.Handle(e); } The Logs folder must exist before the adapter is created. Filtering by category Drop messages from one namespace for the console provider only. using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Filters; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Providers; LogConsumer.AddFilter( new CategoryLogFilter(typeof(ConsoleLogProvider), isExclusive: true) .AddCategory("MyApp.Services.NoisyService")); The category is the caller's full type name, so add one entry per type you want to filter. Dumping an object for debugging Serialize an object to every provider at Debug level. using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Serialization; LogConsumer.Debug(new Order { Id = 1, Total = 9.90m }, "order-1", SerializerFormat.Json); [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Json)] public class Order { public int Id { get; set; } public decimal Total { get; set; } } The provider must have LogLevel.Debug enabled (for example SetLevel(LogLevel.All) ) for the entry to be written. Writing a custom provider Implement ILogProvider and add an instance. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Providers; using CrispyWaffle.Serialization; LogConsumer.AddProvider(new DebugOutputLogProvider()).SetLevel(LogLevel.All); LogConsumer.Info("Custom provider registered"); public sealed class DebugOutputLogProvider : ILogProvider { private LogLevel _level = LogLevel.Production; public void SetLevel(LogLevel level) => _level = level; private void Write(LogLevel level, string category, string message) { if (_level.HasFlag(level)) { System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine($"[{level}] {category}: {message}"); } } public void Fatal(string category, string message) => Write(LogLevel.Fatal, category, message); public void Error(string category, string message) => Write(LogLevel.Error, category, message); public void Warning(string category, string message) => Write(LogLevel.Warning, category, message); public void Info(string category, string message) => Write(LogLevel.Info, category, message); public void Trace(string category, string message) => Write(LogLevel.Trace, category, message); public void Trace(string category, string message, Exception exception) => Write(LogLevel.Trace, category, $"{message}: {exception}"); public void Trace(string category, Exception exception) => Write(LogLevel.Trace, category, exception.ToString()); public void Debug(string category, string message) => Write(LogLevel.Debug, category, message); public void Debug(string category, string content, string identifier) => Write(LogLevel.Debug, category, $"{identifier}: {content}"); public void Debug<T>(string category, T content, string identifier, SerializerFormat customFormat) where T : class, new() => Write(LogLevel.Debug, category, $"{identifier}: {content}"); } See also Service locator Telemetry Serialization Infrastructure Diagrams

docs.text: CrispyWaffle logging is a static facade, LogConsumer , that fans each message out to every registered log provider. Providers decide where messages go (console, rolling text files, Log4Net, Redis, RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch, Windows Event Log). Filters decide which provider receives which message, and an exception handler decides what happens to exceptions passed to LogConsumer.Handle . Use it when you want one logging call site in your code and the freedom to add or swap destinations at startup without touching that code. Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.Log , CrispyWaffle.Log.Adapters , CrispyWaffle.Log.Filters , CrispyWaffle.Log.Handlers , CrispyWaffle.Log.Providers
docs.title: Logging

docs.text: The pipeline has four kinds of parts: LogConsumer is the static entry point. It holds a list of providers, a list of filters and one exception handler. Providers ( ILogProvider ) receive a category and a message for each level. You register them with LogConsumer.AddProvider . Adapters ( ILogAdapter and friends) do the actual writing for the two core providers. ConsoleLogProvider writes through an IConsoleLogAdapter and TextFileLogProvider writes through an ITextFileLogAdapter , both resolved from the service locator . Filters ( ILogFilter ) are checked per provider, per message.
docs.title: How it works

docs.text: When you call LogConsumer.Info("...") (or any other level), the consumer: Resolves a category by walking the stack trace. It skips frames whose declaring type is in CrispyWaffle.Log* or is a CrispyWaffle type whose name ends with LogProvider , then uses the declaring type's full name (for example MyApp.Services.OrderService ). A leading CrispyWaffle. prefix is removed. For async methods and lambdas this is the compiler-generated type name (for example MyApp.OrderService+<RunAsync>d__0 ). If no frame qualifies, the category is CrispyWaffle . For each provider, calls every registered filter with the provider's full type name, the level, the category and the message. The provider receives the message only if all filters return true . Calls the matching method on each provider that passed, synchronously and in registration order. LogTo<TLogProvider> and DebugTo<TLogProvider> skip the fan-out and target the one registered provider whose runtime type is exactly TLogProvider . They return false when no such provider is registered or a filter rejects the message. The overloads that take params object[] arguments format the message with string.Format(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, ...) before it reaches the providers.
docs.title: Sending a message

docs.text: LogLevel is a [Flags] enum. Each provider (through its adapter) keeps its own level and drops messages whose level flag is not set. LogConsumer itself does not check levels. The built-in adapters start at LogLevel.Production (Fatal, Error, Warning, Info), so Trace and Debug messages are dropped until you call SetLevel on the provider: LogConsumer.AddProvider<ConsoleLogProvider>().SetLevel(LogLevel.All);
docs.title: Levels

docs.text: LogConsumer.Handle(exception) (and the two event-handler overloads) forward to the current IExceptionHandler . The handler is chosen the first time LogConsumer is used (static constructor): it resolves IExceptionHandler from the service locator and, if that fails, falls back to DefaultExceptionHandler and passes it the resolution error. Without a registration, resolution normally fails because the core package already contains two implementations ( DefaultExceptionHandler and NullExceptionHandler ) and auto-registration refuses to pick one. Register your handler before the first logging call, or replace it later with LogConsumer.SetHandler . DefaultExceptionHandler does not write to the providers registered on LogConsumer . It keeps its own static list of providers, added with AddLogProvider<T>(ExceptionLogType) , TryAddConsoleLogProvider() or TryAddTextFileLogProvider() . When it handles an exception it: Resolves a category from the stack trace, the same way LogConsumer does. Unwraps the exception chain (innermost first) and calls TelemetryAnalytics.TrackException for each inner exception type (see Telemetry ). Calls Error(category, message) on each ExceptionLogType.Message provider once per exception in the chain, with just that exception's Message . Calls Error(category, details) once on each ExceptionLogType.Full provider, where details contains every exception's message, type name and stack trace, with Exception rethrow at [n]: markers between them. With no providers added, DefaultExceptionHandler only tracks telemetry.

docs.text: LogConsumer holds providers and filters in plain collections with no locking, so register them at startup before logging from multiple threads. StandardConsoleLogAdapter and RollingTextFileLogAdapter lock around each write, so concurrent logging through them is safe.

docs.text: Register an adapter and an exception handler, add a provider, then log. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Adapters; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Handlers; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Providers; public static class Program { public static void Main() { // Adapter used by ConsoleLogProvider. ServiceLocator.Register<IConsoleLogAdapter, StandardConsoleLogAdapter>(Lifetime.Singleton); // Must be registered before the first LogConsumer call. ServiceLocator.Register<IExceptionHandler, NullExceptionHandler>(Lifetime.Singleton); LogConsumer.AddProvider<ConsoleLogProvider>().SetLevel(LogLevel.All); LogConsumer.Info("Hello world Crispy Waffle"); LogConsumer.Debug("Current time: {0:HH:mm:ss}", DateTime.Now); LogConsumer.Warning("Press any key to close the program!"); Console.ReadKey(); } }

docs.text: public sealed class RollingTextFileLogAdapter : ITextFileLogAdapter — writes entries to files in a folder, starting a new file when a message count or size limit is reached. Files are named LogFile-{fileNameSeed}-[{n}].txt (or .json ). On start and on each roll, n is increased until the name does not collide with an existing file. Before each write the adapter checks the current file: when it holds maxMessageCount messages or its length has reached maxFileSize , it closes it and opens the next one, so a file can exceed the size limit by one entry. Writes are serialized with a lock per instance. Use one instance per seed; two instances with the same seed and folder write to different numbers but may race on creating them. Each entry is a LogMessage . In LogFileType.Text files, entries are separated by a ---------- line and each property is written as Name: value ( N.A. for empty values). In LogFileType.Json files, the file is kept as a valid JSON array of entries. Exceptions are written as [MainException][Type]: message followed by one [InnerException][Type]: message line per inner exception, without stack traces. The default category is N.A. . Member Description RollingTextFileLogAdapter(string folderPath, string fileNameSeed, int maxMessageCount, (Unit unit, uint size) maxFileSize, LogFileType fileType = LogFileType.Text) Constructor. Creates the first file immediately. Throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException when maxFileSize is under 1 KB or over 10 GB, or maxMessageCount is less than 1. Throws DirectoryNotFoundException when folderPath does not exist. Starts at LogLevel.Production . SetLevel(LogLevel level) Changes the level, then writes a "Level updated" warning. Debug(string message) , Trace(string message) , Info , Warning , Error , Fatal Write an entry at that level with the default category. Trace(Exception exception) / Trace(string message, Exception exception) Write exception details (and the message as a separate entry) at Trace level. Debug(string content, string fileName) Writes content as a Debug entry in the current log file, with MessageIdentifier set to fileName . No separate file is created. Debug<T>(T content, string identifier, SerializerFormat customFormat = SerializerFormat.None) Serializes content and writes it as a Debug entry with MessageIdentifier set to identifier . CategorizedFatal , CategorizedError , CategorizedWarning , CategorizedInfo , CategorizedTrace , CategorizedDebug(category, message) , CategorizedDebug<T>(...) Same as the uncategorized methods, with Category set to category . CategorizedDebug(string category, string content, string identifier) Writes content with MessageIdentifier set to identifier . Note: the entry is written at Fatal level, not Debug. Dispose() Closes the current file stream. Also called from the finalizer.

docs.text: Use the default handler, write exception messages to the console and full details to text files, and hook process-wide unhandled exceptions. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Adapters; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Handlers; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Providers; ServiceLocator.Register<IConsoleLogAdapter, StandardConsoleLogAdapter>(Lifetime.Singleton); ServiceLocator.Register<ITextFileLogAdapter>( () => new RollingTextFileLogAdapter("Logs", "app", 1000, (Unit.MByte, 5), LogFileType.Json), Lifetime.Singleton); ServiceLocator.Register<IExceptionHandler, DefaultExceptionHandler>(Lifetime.Singleton); DefaultExceptionHandler.TryAddConsoleLogProvider(); DefaultExceptionHandler.TryAddTextFileLogProvider(); AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException += LogConsumer.Handle; try { throw new InvalidOperationException("Something failed"); } catch (Exception e) { LogConsumer.Handle(e); } The Logs folder must exist before the adapter is created.

docs.text: Scheduler (cron jobs) The scheduler module runs in-process actions on a recurring schedule written as a CRON-like expression. You register one or more jobs with a JobManager , start it, and each job's delegate runs on its own thread whenever the current minute matches its expression. Use it for lightweight periodic work inside a long-running process, such as cleanup, polling or cache refresh. This module is a minimal minute-resolution timer that lives in the core package. For queued, retried or persisted background work, use the separate BackgroundJobs package instead. Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.Scheduler How it works Timer. JobManager owns a System.Timers.Timer with a fixed 30-second interval. On each tick it compares the current minute ( DateTime.Now.Minute ) with the minute of the last run. If the minute has changed, it records the new run time and calls Execute(DateTime.Now) on every registered JobRunner , in the order they were added. The last-run time is initialized when the JobManager is constructed, so the minute in which you create the manager never triggers jobs. All times are local ( DateTime.Now ). Matching. Each JobRunner holds a CronScheduler built from its expression. Execute checks CronScheduler.IsTime(dateTime) ; if the time does not match, nothing happens. Threading. When the time matches, the runner starts a new Thread for the delegate, unless the previous run of the same job is still in the Running or WaitSleepJoin state, in which case the run is skipped. Runs of the same job never overlap; different jobs run concurrently. Calls to Execute are serialized with a lock per runner. The job threads are ordinary foreground threads and nothing catches exceptions thrown by the delegate: an unhandled exception in a job terminates the process. Wrap the body of each job in try / catch . Stopping. Stop() stops the timer, so no new runs start. Jobs already running are not interrupted. JobManager does not implement IDisposable . CRON syntax CronScheduler supports five fields, in this order. There is no seconds field and no year field. Position Field Values * expands to 1 Minute 0-59 0-59 2 Hour 0-23 0-23 3 Day of month 1-31 1-31 4 Month 1-12 1-12 5 Day of week 0-6, 0 = Sunday 0-6 Fields are found by pattern matching, not by splitting on spaces. The expression is scanned with CronSchedulerValidations.ValidationRegex , and each successive match becomes the next field. Any character that is not part of a match acts as a separator. Fields that are missing at the end default to * , so 10 is the same as 10 * * * * and * */3 is the same as * */3 * * * . Matches after the fifth are ignored. Each field can use exactly one of these forms: Form Example Meaning * * Every value in the field's range. */n */15 Every value in the field's range that is divisible by n ( value % n == 0 ). a-b 10-15 Every value from a to b , inclusive. a-b/n 10-30/2 Every value from a to b , inclusive, that is divisible by n . a 5 A single value. a,b,c 0,6 A list of single values. All conditions are combined with AND: a time matches only if the minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week all match. This differs from standard cron, where a restricted day of month and a restricted day of week are combined with OR. Behaviors to be aware of: Steps are divisibility tests, not offsets from the start. */5 in the day-of-month field yields 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 (not 1, 6, 11, ...). 1-10/3 in the minute field yields 3, 6, 9 (not 1, 4, 7, 10). */2 in the month field yields 2, 4, ..., 12. Not supported: names ( MON , JAN ), ? , L , W , # , 7 for Sunday, steps on a single value ( 5/10 ), lists that contain ranges ( 1-5,10 ), and macros such as @daily . Unsupported tokens are not rejected. They are skipped or split into extra matches, which shifts the remaining fields. For example, 0 0 * * MON has only four matches, so the day of week becomes * and the job runs every day at midnight. 1-5,10 * * * * yields six matches ( 1-5 , 10 , * , ...), so 10 becomes the hour. Values outside a field's range are accepted but never match (for example, minute 70 ). IsValid returns true if the expression contains at least one match, so it only rejects strings with no digits and no * at all. Expression Runs * Every minute. 10 At minute 10 of every hour. */10 At minutes 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 of every hour. 10 1 * * 0 At 01:10 every Sunday. 0 9-17 * * 1-5 On the hour from 09:00 to 17:00, Monday to Friday. */20 * 10,20,30 * * At minutes 0, 20 and 40 of every hour on days 10, 20 and 30 of each month. 0 0 1 * * At midnight on the first day of each month. Getting started using System; using System.Threading; using CrispyWaffle.Scheduler; var counter = 0; var jobManager = new JobManager(); jobManager.AddJob("* * * * *", () => Interlocked.Increment(ref counter)); jobManager.Start(); Thread.Sleep(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2)); jobManager.Stop(); Console.WriteLine(counter); // typically 1 or 2, depending on when the manager was created Reference JobManager public class JobManager : IJobManager — holds a list of jobs and triggers them from a 30-second timer, at most once per minute. Member Description JobManager() Creates the manager and its timer. The timer is not started. AddJob(string cronExpression, ThreadStart action) Creates a JobRunner for the expression and action and adds it. Throws ArgumentNullException if the expression is null or whitespace or the action is null, ArgumentOutOfRangeException if the expression is not valid. The job list is not thread-safe; add jobs before calling Start . Start() Starts the timer. Stop() Stops the timer. Running jobs continue to completion. IJobManager public interface IJobManager — contract for a component that schedules and runs jobs. Member Description AddJob(string cronExpression, ThreadStart action) Adds a job with a schedule and the delegate to run. Start() Begins running scheduled jobs. Stop() Stops triggering jobs until Start is called again. IJobRunner public interface IJobRunner — contract for a single scheduled job. Member Description Execute(DateTime dateTime) Runs the job if dateTime matches its schedule. JobRunner public class JobRunner : IJobRunner — runs one ThreadStart delegate on a new thread when a CronScheduler matches. You normally create these through JobManager.AddJob . Create one directly to drive a schedule from your own timer. Member Description JobRunner(string schedule, ThreadStart threadStart) Builds a CronScheduler from schedule . Throws ArgumentNullException if schedule is null or whitespace or threadStart is null, ArgumentOutOfRangeException if schedule is not a valid expression. Execute(DateTime dateTime) If dateTime matches the schedule and the previous run is not still running, starts the delegate on a new thread and returns immediately. Thread-safe. IScheduler public interface IScheduler — contract for an object that parses a schedule expression and tests dates against it. Member Description IsValid(string expression) Returns true if the expression is acceptable to the scheduler. IsTime(DateTime dateTime) Returns true if dateTime matches the schedule. Minutes ICollection<int> of matching minutes. Hours ICollection<int> of matching hours. DaysOfMonth ICollection<int> of matching days of the month. Months ICollection<int> of matching months. DaysOfWeek ICollection<int> of matching days of the week. In CronScheduler these use System.DayOfWeek numbering: 0 = Sunday through 6 = Saturday. CronScheduler public class CronScheduler : IScheduler — parses a five-field expression (see CRON syntax ) into sets of matching values. Member Description CronScheduler() Creates an instance with no expression. All collections are empty and IsTime always returns false . Useful only for calling IsValid . CronScheduler(string expression) Parses expression . Throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException if IsValid returns false , ArgumentNullException if expression is null. IsValid(string expression) Returns true if ValidationRegex finds at least one match in expression . This is a weak check; see CRON syntax . IsTime(DateTime dateTime) Returns true if the minute, hour, day, month and day of week of dateTime are all in their sets. Seconds are ignored. Minutes , Hours , DaysOfMonth , Months , DaysOfWeek The parsed sets, as ICollection<int> . They are the live internal sets; do not modify them. CronSchedulerValidations public static class CronSchedulerValidations — the regular expressions used to tokenize and classify CRON fields. All are public static readonly Regex , compiled, with a 5-second match timeout. Member Pattern Matches DividedRegex (\*/\d+) */n RangeRegex (\d+\-\d+)\/?(\d+)? a-b and a-b/n WildRegex (\*) * ListRegex (((\d+,)*\d+)+) a and a,b,c ValidationRegex The four above joined with \| , in that order Any single field. Used to split an expression into fields. When classifying a field, CronScheduler tests DividedRegex , then RangeRegex , then WildRegex , then ListRegex , and uses the first that matches. Examples Several jobs with error handling using System; using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Scheduler; var jobManager = new JobManager(); jobManager.AddJob("*/5", () => { try { PurgeExpiredSessions(); } catch (Exception ex) { LogConsumer.Handle(ex); } }); jobManager.AddJob("0 3 * * 0", () => { try { RebuildSearchIndex(); // 03:00 every Sunday } catch (Exception ex) { LogConsumer.Handle(ex); } }); jobManager.Start(); Inspecting a schedule using System; using CrispyWaffle.Scheduler; var scheduler = new CronScheduler("* 10-15 * * *"); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(",", scheduler.Hours)); // 10,11,12,13,14,15 var weekend = new CronScheduler("* * * * 0,6"); Console.WriteLine(weekend.IsTime(new DateTime(2020, 9, 5, 12, 0, 0))); // True (Saturday) Driving a runner from your own clock using System; using CrispyWaffle.Scheduler; IJobRunner runner = new JobRunner("0 * * * *", () => Console.WriteLine("top of the hour")); runner.Execute(new DateTime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0)); // starts the job runner.Execute(new DateTime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 1, 0)); // does nothing See also BackgroundJobs Logging

Member Pattern Matches DividedRegex (\*/\d+) */n RangeRegex (\d+\-\d+)\/?(\d+)? a-b and a-b/n WildRegex (\*) * ListRegex (((\d+,)*\d+)+) a and a,b,c ValidationRegex The four above joined with \| , in that order Any single field. Used to split an expression into fields. When classifying a field, CronScheduler tests DividedRegex , then RangeRegex , then WildRegex , then ListRegex , and uses the first that matches.

docs.text: Serialization The serialization module converts objects to and from JSON, XML, YAML and TOML. You mark a class with [Serializer] to pick a format, then call GetSerializer() on an instance to get a SerializerConverter<T> . The converter can turn the object into a string, an XmlDocument , a JToken or a stream, and it can deserialize, load from a file or save to a file. You can also use the adapters ( NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter , JsonSerializerAdapter , XmlSerializerAdapter , YamlSerializerAdapter , TomlSerializerAdapter ) on their own, without the attribute or the factory. Package CrispyWaffle Namespace CrispyWaffle.Serialization , CrispyWaffle.Serialization.Adapters , CrispyWaffle.Serialization.NewtonsoftJson , CrispyWaffle.Serialization.SystemTextJson How it works SerializerFactory.GetSerializer(obj) reads the SerializerAttribute from the runtime type of obj and wraps the object in a SerializerConverter<T> with an adapter for that format: Attribute Adapter used [Serializer] or [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Xml)] XmlSerializerAdapter , resolved through ServiceLocator.Resolve<XmlSerializerAdapter>() [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Json)] (strict, the default) NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter , resolved through ServiceLocator.Resolve<NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter>() [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Json, false)] (not strict) A new NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter with MissingMemberHandling.Ignore [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Yaml)] YamlSerializerAdapter , resolved through ServiceLocator.Resolve<YamlSerializerAdapter>() [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Toml)] TomlSerializerAdapter , resolved through ServiceLocator.Resolve<TomlSerializerAdapter>() SerializerFormat.None Throws InvalidOperationException The factory always uses Newtonsoft.Json for JSON. The System.Text.Json adapter ( JsonSerializerAdapter ) is only used if you create it yourself. Attribute lookup rules: The attribute is read from the object's runtime type. SerializerAttribute is declared with Inherited = false , so a derived class needs its own [Serializer] . For an array, the attribute is read from the element type ( Customer[] uses the attribute on Customer ). For any other IEnumerable , the attribute is read from the first generic argument ( List<Customer> uses the attribute on Customer ). If no attribute is found, GetSerializer throws InvalidOperationException with the message The CrispyWaffle.Serialization.SerializerAttribute attribute was not found in the object of type ... . Strict and non-strict JSON differ only when you deserialize. Strict mode uses MissingMemberHandling.Error , so a JSON property with no matching .NET member throws. Non-strict mode uses MissingMemberHandling.Ignore . Both modes use the pt-BR culture, NullValueHandling.Ignore and the Newtonsoft NotNullObserverConverter . XmlSerializerAdapter , NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter , YamlSerializerAdapter and TomlSerializerAdapter have no constructor dependencies, so the service locator can create them without registration. Not-null observer NotNullObserver is an empty marker class. Use it as the type of a property that you expect to always be null or empty in incoming JSON, such as a field a third-party API documents but never fills. Both JSON adapters register a matching converter by default. When the JSON has a real value for that property, the converter throws NotNullObserverException , and the adapter wraps it in a second NotNullObserverException that names the target type. This lets you detect when the upstream payload changes. The two converters accept different "empty" values: JSON value Newtonsoft converter System.Text.Json converter null Returns null Returns null "" or whitespace string Returns null Returns null [] Returns null Throws JsonException (see note) {} Returns null Returns null Non-empty object Throws NotNullObserverException Throws NotNullObserverException Non-empty string, number, boolean, non-empty array Throws NotNullObserverException Throws JsonException (see note) Note: the System.Text.Json converter calls JsonElement.EnumerateObject() before it checks the value kind. That call throws InvalidOperationException for any value that is not an object, and System.Text.Json wraps it in a JsonException ("The JSON value could not be converted to CrispyWaffle.Serialization.NotNullObserver"). In those cases you get JsonException instead of NotNullObserverException . Getting started using System; using CrispyWaffle.Serialization; var customer = new Customer { Id = 1, Name = "Jane Doe" }; // Serialize to a JSON string (Newtonsoft.Json, indented). var json = (string)customer.GetSerializer(); // Deserialize back into a new instance. Customer copy = SerializerFactory.GetSerializer<Customer>().Deserialize(json); Console.WriteLine(copy.Name); [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Json)] public class Customer { public int Id { get; set; } public string Name { get; set; } } Reference SerializerFactory public static class SerializerFactory — creates SerializerConverter<T> instances from the [Serializer] attribute or from an explicit format. Member Description GetSerializer<T>(this T obj) Extension method. Reads the SerializerAttribute from the runtime type of obj (or its element / first generic argument for collections) and returns a converter that wraps obj . Throws InvalidOperationException when no attribute is found or the format is None . T : class . GetSerializer<T>() Creates a new T with Activator.CreateInstance<T>() and returns a converter for it. Use it when you only want to deserialize. T needs a public parameterless constructor. GetCustomSerializer<T>(this T obj, SerializerFormat format) Extension method. Ignores any attribute and returns a converter for format . JSON is always strict here. Throws InvalidOperationException for SerializerFormat.None . GetCustomSerializer<T>(SerializerFormat format) Same as above, for a new T created with Activator.CreateInstance<T>() . SerializerConverter<T> public sealed class SerializerConverter<T> where T : class — wraps an object and an ISerializerAdapter , and exposes conversion operators and file helpers. Methods that deserialize or load replace the wrapped object and return it. Member Description SerializerConverter(T obj, ISerializerAdapter formatter) Constructor. Wraps obj with the given adapter. Serialize(out Stream stream) Serializes the wrapped object with the adapter. The stream is positioned at 0. Deserialize(object deserialized) Deserializes deserialized with the adapter, stores the result and returns it. JSON adapters expect a string . The XML adapter accepts a string or an XmlDocument . DeserializeFromStream(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Deserializes from a stream (UTF-8 when encoding is null ), stores the result and returns it. Load(string file) Reads the file as UTF-8, deserializes it, stores the result and returns it. See BaseSerializerAdapter.Load<T> for exceptions. Save(string file) Serializes the wrapped object to file , replacing it if it exists. implicit operator XmlDocument(SerializerConverter<T>) Serializes to an XmlDocument . Returns null when the converter is null or its adapter is not XmlSerializerAdapter . An InvalidOperationException during serialization is logged through LogConsumer.Handle and an empty document is returned. implicit operator JToken(SerializerConverter<T>) Serializes to a Newtonsoft JToken : a JArray when the object is IEnumerable , otherwise a JObject . Returns null when the adapter is not NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter , or after logging an InvalidOperationException . explicit operator string(SerializerConverter<T>) XML adapter: indented XML without the XML declaration. Newtonsoft adapter: indented JSON. Any IStringSerializerAdapter (such as YamlSerializerAdapter or TomlSerializerAdapter ): the result of SerializeToString . Throws InvalidOperationException for any other adapter (including JsonSerializerAdapter ). implicit operator SerializerConverter<T>(XmlDocument xml) Creates a converter with the XML adapter and deserializes xml.InnerXml into T . implicit operator SerializerConverter<T>(JObject json) Creates a converter with the Newtonsoft adapter and deserializes json into T . implicit operator T(SerializerConverter<T>) Returns the wrapped object. ISerializerAdapter public interface ISerializerAdapter — contract for a format-specific serializer. All methods have the constraint T : class . Member Description DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Deserializes a stream. null encoding means UTF-8. Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Deserializes a serialized representation (usually a string ). Load<T>(string file) Reads a file and deserializes its content. Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Serializes an object into a new stream. Save<T>(string file, T deserialized) Serializes an object and writes it to a file. IStringSerializerAdapter public interface IStringSerializerAdapter : ISerializerAdapter — an adapter that can serialize directly to a string. SerializerConverter<T> uses it for the explicit string conversion. Member Description SerializeToString<T>(T deserialized) Serializes an object to its string representation. T : class . BaseSerializerAdapter public abstract class BaseSerializerAdapter : ISerializerAdapter — base class with file handling. Subclass it to add a format. Member Description virtual DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Throws NotImplementedException . Override it. virtual Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Throws NotImplementedException . Override it. virtual Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Throws NotImplementedException . Override it. virtual Load<T>(string file) Reads the whole file as UTF-8 and passes the string to Deserialize<T> . Throws ArgumentNullException when file is null or whitespace or has no file name part. Throws LocalFileNotFoundException when the file does not exist. virtual Save<T>(string file, T deserialized) Throws ArgumentNullException when file is null or whitespace. Deletes an existing file, then calls Serialize<T> and copies the stream into a new file. NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter public sealed class NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter : BaseSerializerAdapter — JSON adapter based on Newtonsoft.Json. The factory uses it for all JSON. Member Description NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter() Constructor. Uses JsonSerializerSettings with NotNullObserverConverter (Newtonsoft), culture pt-BR , MissingMemberHandling.Error and NullValueHandling.Ignore . NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter(JsonSerializerSettings settings) Constructor. Uses your settings for deserialization. DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Reads the stream to the end and calls JsonConvert.DeserializeObject<T> with the settings. Wraps NotNullObserverException in a new NotNullObserverException(typeof(T), e) . Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Casts serialized to string and deserializes it with the settings. Same exception wrapping. Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Writes indented JSON as UTF-8 into a new MemoryStream positioned at 0. This method uses a default JsonSerializer and does not apply the configured settings, so null properties are written. JsonSerializerAdapter public sealed class JsonSerializerAdapter : BaseSerializerAdapter — JSON adapter based on System.Text.Json. The factory never selects it; create it directly. Member Description JsonSerializerAdapter() Constructor. Uses JsonSerializerOptions with WriteIndented = true , PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true , DefaultIgnoreCondition = WhenWritingNull and the System.Text.Json NotNullObserverConverter . JsonSerializerAdapter(JsonSerializerOptions settings) Constructor. Uses your options. DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Throws ArgumentNullException when stream is null. Reads the stream to the end and calls JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T> . Wraps NotNullObserverException in a new NotNullObserverException(typeof(T), e) . Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Casts serialized to string and deserializes it. Same exception wrapping. Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Writes JSON with a Utf8JsonWriter (indented when WriteIndented is set) into a new MemoryStream positioned at 0. When deserialized is null , the stream is empty. XmlSerializerAdapter public sealed class XmlSerializerAdapter : BaseSerializerAdapter — XML adapter based on System.Xml.Serialization.XmlSerializer . Member Description DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Deserializes with new XmlSerializer(typeof(T)) . Returns null if the result is not a T . Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Accepts an XmlDocument (uses OuterXml ) or a string . Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Serializes with new XmlSerializer(deserialized.GetType()) into a MemoryStream positioned at 0. Output is indented UTF-8, keeps the XML declaration, and has no xsi / xsd namespace declarations. YamlSerializerAdapter public sealed class YamlSerializerAdapter : BaseSerializerAdapter, IStringSerializerAdapter — YAML adapter based on YamlDotNet . Property names use camel case ( ApplicationName becomes applicationName ). Member Description DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Throws ArgumentNullException when stream is null. Reads the stream (UTF-8 when encoding is null , byte order marks detected) and deserializes it. The stream is left open. Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Throws ArgumentNullException when serialized is null and ArgumentException when it is not a string . Duplicate keys throw YamlDotNet.Core.YamlException . Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Writes YAML as UTF-8 into a new MemoryStream positioned at 0. When deserialized is null , the stream is empty. SerializeToString<T>(T deserialized) Returns the YAML string, or an empty string when deserialized is null . TomlSerializerAdapter public sealed class TomlSerializerAdapter : BaseSerializerAdapter, IStringSerializerAdapter — TOML adapter based on Tomlyn . Property names use camel case ( ApplicationName becomes applicationName ). Member Description DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Throws ArgumentNullException when stream is null. Reads the stream (UTF-8 when encoding is null , byte order marks detected) and deserializes it. The stream is left open. Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Throws ArgumentNullException when serialized is null and ArgumentException when it is not a string . Invalid TOML, including duplicate keys, throws Tomlyn.TomlException . Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Writes TOML as UTF-8 into a new MemoryStream positioned at 0. When deserialized is null , the stream is empty. SerializeToString<T>(T deserialized) Returns the TOML string, or an empty string when deserialized is null . SerializerAttribute public sealed class SerializerAttribute : Attribute — selects the format the factory uses for a class or interface. Declared with AttributeTargets.Class | AttributeTargets.Interface , Inherited = false , AllowMultiple = true . The factory reads it with Attribute.GetCustomAttribute , which throws AmbiguousMatchException if the attribute is applied more than once, so apply it only once per type. Member Description SerializerAttribute(SerializerFormat format = SerializerFormat.Xml, bool isStrict = true) Constructor. Default is strict XML. Format The SerializerFormat . IsStrict For JSON: true fails on unknown JSON members during deserialization, false ignores them. Has no effect on XML, YAML or TOML. SerializerFormat public enum SerializerFormat — output format. Each value has a [HumanReadable] label. Value Description None (0) No format. The factory throws InvalidOperationException for it. Label None . Json JSON through Newtonsoft.Json. Label JSON . Xml XML through XmlSerializer . Label XML . Yaml YAML through YamlDotNet. Label YAML . Toml TOML through Tomlyn. Label TOML . NotNullObserver public class NotNullObserver — empty marker type for properties that should never receive a value. See Not-null observer . CrispyWaffle.Serialization.NewtonsoftJson.NotNullObserverConverter public sealed class NotNullObserverConverter : JsonConverter (Newtonsoft) — enforces NotNullObserver properties during Newtonsoft deserialization. Member Description CanConvert(Type objectType) Returns true only for NotNullObserver . ReadJson(JsonReader reader, Type objectType, object existingValue, JsonSerializer serializer) Returns null for null , a null/whitespace string, or an empty array or object. Otherwise throws NotNullObserverException with the token type, value and JSON path. WriteJson(JsonWriter writer, object value, JsonSerializer serializer) Writes value with serializer.Serialize . CrispyWaffle.Serialization.NewtonsoftJson.NotNullObserverException public class NotNullObserverException : Exception — thrown by the Newtonsoft converter and adapter when a NotNullObserver property has a value. Member Description NotNullObserverException(JsonToken type, object value, string path) Message: Not null observer found a not null value in path {path} of type {type}: {value} . Thrown by the converter. NotNullObserverException(Type parentType, Exception innerException) Message: Unable to serialize type {parentType.FullName}. Constraints: Not null observer . Thrown by NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter around the converter's exception. protected NotNullObserverException(SerializationInfo info, StreamingContext context) Serialization constructor. CrispyWaffle.Serialization.SystemTextJson.NotNullObserverConverter public sealed class NotNullObserverConverter : JsonConverter<NotNullObserver> (System.Text.Json) — enforces NotNullObserver properties during System.Text.Json deserialization. Member Description Read(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options) Returns null for null , a null/whitespace string, or {} . Throws NotNullObserverException for a non-empty object. Throws InvalidOperationException for other non-null values, which System.Text.Json surfaces as a JsonException (see the note under Not-null observer ). Write(Utf8JsonWriter writer, NotNullObserver value, JsonSerializerOptions options) Writes value with JsonSerializer.Serialize . CrispyWaffle.Serialization.SystemTextJson.NotNullObserverException public class NotNullObserverException : Exception — thrown by the System.Text.Json converter and adapter when a NotNullObserver property has a value. Member Description NotNullObserverException(JsonTokenType type, object value) Message: Not null observer found a not null value of type {type}: {value} . Thrown by the converter. NotNullObserverException(Type parentType, Exception innerException) Message: Unable to serialize type {parentType.FullName}. Constraints: Not null observer . Thrown by JsonSerializerAdapter around the converter's exception. protected NotNullObserverException(SerializationInfo info, StreamingContext context) Serialization constructor. The two exception classes have the same name in different namespaces. Catch the one that matches the adapter you use. LocalFileNotFoundException public class LocalFileNotFoundException : Exception (namespace CrispyWaffle.Serialization.Adapters ) — thrown by BaseSerializerAdapter.Load<T> when the file does not exist. Member Description LocalFileNotFoundException(string file, string fullPath) Message: Unable to find the file {file} in the directory {fullPath} . fullPath is the directory of the absolute path. protected LocalFileNotFoundException(SerializationInfo info, StreamingContext context) Serialization constructor. Examples XML round trip [Serializer] with no arguments selects XML. using CrispyWaffle.Serialization; var order = new Order { Code = 42, Description = "Sample" }; var xml = (string)order.GetSerializer(); Order copy = SerializerFactory.GetSerializer<Order>().Deserialize(xml); [Serializer] public class Order { public int Code { get; set; } public string Description { get; set; } } Collections Arrays and generic collections use the attribute of their element type. using System.Collections.Generic; using CrispyWaffle.Serialization; var items = new List<Customer> { new() { Id = 1, Name = "Jane" }, new() { Id = 2, Name = "John" }, }; var json = (string)items.GetSerializer(); List<Customer> copy = new List<Customer>().GetSerializer().Deserialize(json); [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Json)] public class Customer { public int Id { get; set; } public string Name { get; set; } } Save to and load from a file using CrispyWaffle.Serialization; var settings = new AppSettings { Endpoint = "https://example.com" }; settings.GetSerializer().Save("settings.json"); AppSettings loaded = SerializerFactory.GetSerializer<AppSettings>().Load("settings.json"); [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Json, false)] public class AppSettings { public string Endpoint { get; set; } } Force a format without an attribute GetCustomSerializer ignores the attribute, so it also works for types without one. using CrispyWaffle.Serialization; using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq; var point = new Point { X = 1, Y = 2 }; JToken token = point.GetCustomSerializer(SerializerFormat.Json); public class Point { public int X { get; set; } public int Y { get; set; } } YAML round trip [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Yaml)] selects YAML. Property names are written in camel case. using CrispyWaffle.Serialization; var settings = new AppSettings { ApplicationName = "Crispy Waffle", RetryCount = 3 }; // applicationName: Crispy Waffle // retryCount: 3 var yaml = (string)settings.GetSerializer(); AppSettings copy = SerializerFactory.GetSerializer<AppSettings>().Deserialize(yaml); settings.GetSerializer().Save("settings.yaml"); AppSettings loaded = SerializerFactory.GetSerializer<AppSettings>().Load("settings.yaml"); [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Yaml)] public class AppSettings { public string ApplicationName { get; set; } public int RetryCount { get; set; } } To use YAML for a type whose attribute selects another format, call GetCustomSerializer(SerializerFormat.Yaml) . TOML round trip [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Toml)] selects TOML. Property names are written in camel case. using CrispyWaffle.Serialization; var settings = new AppSettings { ApplicationName = "Crispy Waffle", RetryCount = 3 }; // applicationName = "Crispy Waffle" // retryCount = 3 var toml = (string)settings.GetSerializer(); AppSettings copy = SerializerFactory.GetSerializer<AppSettings>().Deserialize(toml); settings.GetSerializer().Save("settings.toml"); AppSettings loaded = SerializerFactory.GetSerializer<AppSettings>().Load("settings.toml"); [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Toml)] public class AppSettings { public string ApplicationName { get; set; } public int RetryCount { get; set; } } To use TOML for a type whose attribute selects another format, call GetCustomSerializer(SerializerFormat.Toml) . Use the System.Text.Json adapter directly using System.IO; using CrispyWaffle.Serialization.Adapters; var adapter = new JsonSerializerAdapter(); adapter.Serialize(new Point { X = 1, Y = 2 }, out Stream stream); var json = new StreamReader(stream).ReadToEnd(); Point copy = adapter.Deserialize<Point>(json); public class Point { public int X { get; set; } public int Y { get; set; } } Detect an unexpected value LegacyField is expected to always be empty. When it is not, deserialization fails. using System; using CrispyWaffle.Serialization; using CrispyWaffle.Serialization.Adapters; using CrispyWaffle.Serialization.NewtonsoftJson; var adapter = new NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter(); try { adapter.Deserialize<Payload>("{\"Id\":1,\"LegacyField\":\"surprise\"}"); } catch (NotNullObserverException e) { // "Unable to serialize type Payload. Constraints: Not null observer" Console.WriteLine(e.Message); Console.WriteLine(e.InnerException?.Message); } public class Payload { public int Id { get; set; } public NotNullObserver LegacyField { get; set; } } See also Service locator Attributes Logging

Member Description DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Deserializes a stream. null encoding means UTF-8. Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Deserializes a serialized representation (usually a string ). Load<T>(string file) Reads a file and deserializes its content. Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Serializes an object into a new stream. Save<T>(string file, T deserialized) Serializes an object and writes it to a file.
docs.title: ISerializerAdapter

docs.text: public interface IStringSerializerAdapter : ISerializerAdapter — an adapter that can serialize directly to a string. SerializerConverter<T> uses it for the explicit string conversion. Member Description SerializeToString<T>(T deserialized) Serializes an object to its string representation. T : class .
docs.title: IStringSerializerAdapter

docs.text: public abstract class BaseSerializerAdapter : ISerializerAdapter — base class with file handling. Subclass it to add a format. Member Description virtual DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Throws NotImplementedException . Override it. virtual Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Throws NotImplementedException . Override it. virtual Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Throws NotImplementedException . Override it. virtual Load<T>(string file) Reads the whole file as UTF-8 and passes the string to Deserialize<T> . Throws ArgumentNullException when file is null or whitespace or has no file name part. Throws LocalFileNotFoundException when the file does not exist. virtual Save<T>(string file, T deserialized) Throws ArgumentNullException when file is null or whitespace. Deletes an existing file, then calls Serialize<T> and copies the stream into a new file.
docs.title: BaseSerializerAdapter

docs.text: public sealed class NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter : BaseSerializerAdapter — JSON adapter based on Newtonsoft.Json. The factory uses it for all JSON. Member Description NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter() Constructor. Uses JsonSerializerSettings with NotNullObserverConverter (Newtonsoft), culture pt-BR , MissingMemberHandling.Error and NullValueHandling.Ignore . NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter(JsonSerializerSettings settings) Constructor. Uses your settings for deserialization. DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Reads the stream to the end and calls JsonConvert.DeserializeObject<T> with the settings. Wraps NotNullObserverException in a new NotNullObserverException(typeof(T), e) . Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Casts serialized to string and deserializes it with the settings. Same exception wrapping. Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Writes indented JSON as UTF-8 into a new MemoryStream positioned at 0. This method uses a default JsonSerializer and does not apply the configured settings, so null properties are written.
docs.title: NewtonsoftJsonSerializerAdapter

docs.text: public sealed class JsonSerializerAdapter : BaseSerializerAdapter — JSON adapter based on System.Text.Json. The factory never selects it; create it directly. Member Description JsonSerializerAdapter() Constructor. Uses JsonSerializerOptions with WriteIndented = true , PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true , DefaultIgnoreCondition = WhenWritingNull and the System.Text.Json NotNullObserverConverter . JsonSerializerAdapter(JsonSerializerOptions settings) Constructor. Uses your options. DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Throws ArgumentNullException when stream is null. Reads the stream to the end and calls JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T> . Wraps NotNullObserverException in a new NotNullObserverException(typeof(T), e) . Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Casts serialized to string and deserializes it. Same exception wrapping. Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Writes JSON with a Utf8JsonWriter (indented when WriteIndented is set) into a new MemoryStream positioned at 0. When deserialized is null , the stream is empty.
docs.title: JsonSerializerAdapter

docs.text: public sealed class XmlSerializerAdapter : BaseSerializerAdapter — XML adapter based on System.Xml.Serialization.XmlSerializer . Member Description DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Deserializes with new XmlSerializer(typeof(T)) . Returns null if the result is not a T . Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Accepts an XmlDocument (uses OuterXml ) or a string . Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Serializes with new XmlSerializer(deserialized.GetType()) into a MemoryStream positioned at 0. Output is indented UTF-8, keeps the XML declaration, and has no xsi / xsd namespace declarations.
docs.title: XmlSerializerAdapter

docs.text: public sealed class YamlSerializerAdapter : BaseSerializerAdapter, IStringSerializerAdapter — YAML adapter based on YamlDotNet . Property names use camel case ( ApplicationName becomes applicationName ). Member Description DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Throws ArgumentNullException when stream is null. Reads the stream (UTF-8 when encoding is null , byte order marks detected) and deserializes it. The stream is left open. Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Throws ArgumentNullException when serialized is null and ArgumentException when it is not a string . Duplicate keys throw YamlDotNet.Core.YamlException . Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Writes YAML as UTF-8 into a new MemoryStream positioned at 0. When deserialized is null , the stream is empty. SerializeToString<T>(T deserialized) Returns the YAML string, or an empty string when deserialized is null .
docs.title: YamlSerializerAdapter

Property names use camel case ( ApplicationName becomes applicationName ). Member Description DeserializeFromStream<T>(Stream stream, Encoding encoding = null) Throws ArgumentNullException when stream is null. Reads the stream (UTF-8 when encoding is null , byte order marks detected) and deserializes it. The stream is left open. Deserialize<T>(object serialized) Throws ArgumentNullException when serialized is null and ArgumentException when it is not a string . Invalid TOML, including duplicate keys, throws Tomlyn.TomlException . Serialize<T>(T deserialized, out Stream stream) Writes TOML as UTF-8 into a new MemoryStream positioned at 0. When deserialized is null , the stream is empty. SerializeToString<T>(T deserialized) Returns the TOML string, or an empty string when deserialized is null .

docs.text: public sealed class SerializerAttribute : Attribute — selects the format the factory uses for a class or interface. Declared with AttributeTargets.Class | AttributeTargets.Interface , Inherited = false , AllowMultiple = true . The factory reads it with Attribute.GetCustomAttribute , which throws AmbiguousMatchException if the attribute is applied more than once, so apply it only once per type. Member Description SerializerAttribute(SerializerFormat format = SerializerFormat.Xml, bool isStrict = true) Constructor. Default is strict XML. Format The SerializerFormat . IsStrict For JSON: true fails on unknown JSON members during deserialization, false ignores them. Has no effect on XML, YAML or TOML.

Label None . Json JSON through Newtonsoft.Json. Label JSON . Xml XML through XmlSerializer . Label XML . Yaml YAML through YamlDotNet. Label YAML . Toml TOML through Tomlyn. Label TOML .
