docs.text: CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs runs fire-and-forget and delayed jobs inside an ASP.NET Core application. You register typed handlers under a name, enqueue a job with that name and a payload, and a hosted worker picks it up, runs the handler in its own DI scope, and retries it with exponential backoff when it fails. Jobs are kept in an in-memory store by default, or in a database through Entity Framework Core. The package is standalone: it does not reference the core CrispyWaffle package. It is built on Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting ( BackgroundService ) and Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection . It is a different thing from the core package's cron scheduler : that one runs in-process actions on cron expressions through JobManager , while this package queues persisted, retryable jobs that carry a payload. The CronJobService base class in this package does not parse cron expressions (see Recurring work ). Package CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs Namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Abstractions , CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core , CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Extensions , CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Persistence , CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Scheduling , CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Monitoring , CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Exceptions Install Not yet published to NuGet (it is not in the release workflow's package list). Reference the project: dotnet add reference Src/CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs/CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.csproj Target framework net10.0 only Depends on No CrispyWaffle packages. Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Abstractions , Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Abstractions (for IStartupFilter and the middleware), Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore and Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Relational How it works Registration AddCrispyBackgroundJobs registers, all as singletons unless noted: Service Implementation JobOptions The instance built from your configureOptions callback IJobHandlerRegistry JobHandlerRegistry JobDispatcher JobDispatcher JobMetrics JobMetrics IJobScheduler DelayedJobScheduler IJobStore InMemoryJobStore (default), or EfCoreJobStore as scoped when useEfCoreStore: true BackgroundJobQueue Only in the default (in-memory) mode Hosted service BackgroundWorker IJobStore and BackgroundJobQueue are added with TryAdd , so a store you register before the call wins. AddJobHandler<THandler, TData>(name) registers THandler as scoped and adds an IStartupFilter that calls IJobHandlerRegistry.Register<THandler, TData>(name) when the ASP.NET Core request pipeline is built. This means AddJobHandler only populates the registry in an ASP.NET Core host. In a generic host (worker service) the filter never runs; register the handler type in DI yourself and call Register on the registry after building the host (see Use a generic host ). Enqueueing JobDispatcher.EnqueueAsync (or IJobScheduler.EnqueueAsync ) creates a JobEntity with Status = Pending , the handler name, the priority, MaxAttempt , and the payload serialized with System.Text.Json default options, then saves it with IJobStore.SaveAsync . ScheduleAsync does the same with ScheduledAt = UtcNow + delay ; the job stays in the store until it is due. Only when no IJobStore is registered does the dispatcher fall back to the BackgroundJobQueue : EnqueueAsync pushes the job onto the queue, and ScheduleAsync waits for the delay in a background Task and then pushes it. With AddCrispyBackgroundJobs a store is always registered, so this path is not used. Worker loop BackgroundWorker starts JobOptions.WorkerCount loops (default: one per processor). Each loop: Calls IJobStore.FetchNextAsync , which returns the oldest due Pending job with the highest priority ( High before Normal before Low , then by CreatedAt ) and marks it Processing . If nothing is due, the loop sleeps for JobOptions.PollingInterval (default 2 seconds). If the job's ScheduledAt is still in the future, puts it back ( MarkRetryAsync with the same time) and moves on. Creates a DI scope, looks up the handler type and payload type in IJobHandlerRegistry , deserializes the payload into the payload type, resolves the handler from the scope, and calls its HandleAsync . Records the outcome in the store (see below). An unexpected error in the loop itself is logged and the loop waits 1 second before continuing. The handler is invoked by reflection: the worker looks up a public method named HandleAsync on the concrete handler type. Implement IBackgroundJobHandler<TData>.HandleAsync as a normal public method, not as an explicit interface implementation, and do not add other HandleAsync overloads; otherwise the call throws and the job is retried as described below. Lifecycle and retries Outcome What happens Handler returns JobResult.Ok() MarkCompletedAsync : status Completed . Handler returns JobResult.Fail(message, retry: true) and Attempt + 1 < MaxAttempt Attempt is incremented and MarkRetryAsync sets status Pending with ScheduledAt = UtcNow + backoff . Handler returns Fail with retry: false , or attempts are used up MarkFailedAsync : status Failed , LastError = message (or "Job failed" when the message is null ). No handler registered under the job's name MarkFailedAsync with "No handler registered for '<name>'" . Not retried. Handler type cannot be resolved from DI MarkFailedAsync with "Handler type <type> not resolved from DI" . Not retried. Handler throws, or the payload cannot be deserialized Logged, Attempt incremented, rescheduled with backoff. MaxAttempt is not checked on this path, so a job that always throws is retried indefinitely (every 300 seconds once the cap is reached). The backoff is min(2^min(Attempt, 10), 300) seconds, where Attempt is the already incremented count: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, then 300 seconds. The cap is hard-coded; JobOptions.MaxBackoffSeconds is not read. JobEntity.RetryDelaySeconds is also not read. MaxAttempt counts total executions. With the default of 3, a handler that keeps returning Fail(..., retry: true) runs three times and is then marked Failed . On shutdown, a job interrupted by the stopping token is normally caught by the "handler throws" path and rescheduled with backoff. The JobStatus.Dead value is never assigned by the library. Job stores In-memory (default). InMemoryJobStore keeps jobs in a ConcurrentDictionary . Jobs are lost when the process stops, and completed and failed jobs are never removed. FetchNextAsync selects and marks a job in two separate steps without a lock, so with more than one worker the same job can occasionally be picked by two loops. Set WorkerCount = 1 if handlers must not run twice. EF Core. Pass useEfCoreStore: true and register JobDbContext yourself with your database provider, for example services.AddDbContext<JobDbContext>(o => o.UseSqlServer(connectionString)) . You must also create the Jobs table, for example with db.Database.EnsureCreated() or with migrations generated against JobDbContext (migrations need a MigrationsAssembly in your project, since the context lives in this package). The EF Core mode has wiring problems you need to work around: JobDispatcher takes a BackgroundJobQueue constructor parameter, but the queue is only registered in in-memory mode. Without services.AddSingleton<BackgroundJobQueue>() , resolving JobDispatcher or IJobScheduler fails. EfCoreJobStore is scoped, but the singleton BackgroundWorker and JobDispatcher resolve it from the root provider. With scope validation enabled (the default in the Development environment) the host fails to start with a "Cannot consume scoped service" error. With validation disabled, a single JobDbContext instance is shared by every worker loop and every caller of the dispatcher. DbContext is not thread-safe, so keep WorkerCount = 1 and avoid enqueueing while the worker is running, or register your own IJobStore that creates a context per call. No concurrency token is configured on JobEntity , so FetchNextAsync does not prevent two processes from claiming the same job. Treat the EF Core store as experimental until these are fixed. Monitoring JobMetrics is a singleton dictionary of named counters. The library registers it but does not increment any counter itself, so you record the values you care about, for example from your handlers. MonitoringMiddleware serves JobMetrics.Snapshot() as a JSON object ( {"counter": value} ) for any request whose path starts with the segment /jobs/metrics , and passes every other request on. There is no UseXxx extension; add it with app.UseMiddleware<MonitoringMiddleware>() . The endpoint has no authentication of its own. Recurring work CronJobService is an abstract BackgroundService that calls ExecuteOnce in a loop with a fixed one-minute delay after each run. Despite the file name ( CronJobScheduler.cs ), it does not accept or parse a cron expression, and it is not registered by AddCrispyBackgroundJobs . Register a subclass with AddHostedService . For real cron expressions, use the core scheduler , or enqueue jobs from your subclass. Getting started using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Abstractions; using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core; using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Extensions; var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); builder.Services.AddCrispyBackgroundJobs(o => o.WorkerCount = 2); builder.Services.AddJobHandler<SendEmailHandler, SendEmailData>("send-email"); var app = builder.Build(); app.MapPost( "/signup", async (string email, IJobScheduler jobs) => { await jobs.EnqueueAsync("send-email", new SendEmailData(email, "Welcome!")); return Results.Accepted(); } ); app.Run(); public sealed record SendEmailData(string To, string Subject); public sealed class SendEmailHandler(ILogger<SendEmailHandler> logger) : IBackgroundJobHandler<SendEmailData> { public async Task<JobResult> HandleAsync(SendEmailData data, CancellationToken cancellationToken) { try { logger.LogInformation("Sending '{Subject}' to {To}", data.Subject, data.To); await Task.Delay(100, cancellationToken); // send the email here return JobResult.Ok(); } catch (HttpRequestException ex) { return JobResult.Fail(ex.Message, retry: true); } } } Reference ServiceCollectionExtensions public static class ServiceCollectionExtensions — registration entry points (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Extensions ). Member Description AddCrispyBackgroundJobs(this IServiceCollection services, Action<JobOptions>? configureOptions = null, bool useEfCoreStore = false) Registers the services listed in Registration and the BackgroundWorker hosted service. With useEfCoreStore: true , registers EfCoreJobStore as scoped IJobStore ; you must register JobDbContext (and, see Job stores , BackgroundJobQueue ). Returns services . AddJobHandler<THandler, TData>(this IServiceCollection services, string handlerName) Constraint: THandler : class, IBackgroundJobHandler<TData> . Registers THandler as scoped and an IStartupFilter that adds handlerName to the registry when the ASP.NET Core pipeline is built. Has no effect on the registry in a non-web host. Returns services . IJobScheduler public interface IJobScheduler — the injectable API for adding jobs (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Abstractions ). Member Description EnqueueAsync(string handlerName, object payload, int maxAttempts = 3, JobPriority priority = JobPriority.Normal) Adds a job that is due immediately. Returns Task (the job id is not exposed; use JobDispatcher to get it). ScheduleAsync(string handlerName, object payload, TimeSpan delay, int maxAttempts = 3, JobPriority priority = JobPriority.Normal) Adds a job that becomes due after delay . Returns Task . Because maxAttempts defaults to 3 here and is always passed on, JobOptions.DefaultMaxAttempt has no effect for jobs added through IJobScheduler . DelayedJobScheduler public class DelayedJobScheduler : IJobScheduler — default IJobScheduler ; forwards both methods to JobDispatcher (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Scheduling ). Member Description DelayedJobScheduler(IServiceProvider provider) Constructor. JobDispatcher is resolved from provider on every call. EnqueueAsync(...) / ScheduleAsync(...) See IJobScheduler . JobDispatcher public class JobDispatcher — creates JobEntity records and hands them to the store or the queue (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core ). Member Description JobDispatcher(IServiceProvider provider, BackgroundJobQueue? queue, IJobStore? store, JobOptions options) Constructor. Despite the nullable annotations, the DI container requires both BackgroundJobQueue and IJobStore to be registered. EnqueueAsync(string handlerName, object payload, int? maxAttempts = null, JobPriority priority = JobPriority.Normal) Creates a pending job ( MaxAttempt = maxAttempts ?? options.DefaultMaxAttempt ) and saves it to the store, or enqueues it when there is no store. Returns Task<Guid> , the job id. ScheduleAsync(string handlerName, object payload, TimeSpan delay, int? maxAttempts = null, JobPriority priority = JobPriority.Normal) Same, with ScheduledAt = UtcNow + delay . Without a store, waits delay in a background task before enqueueing (lost if the process stops). Returns Task . IBackgroundJobHandler<TData> public interface IBackgroundJobHandler<TData> — implement this to handle one kind of job (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Abstractions ). Handlers are resolved from a new DI scope per job, so they can depend on scoped services. Member Description HandleAsync(TData data, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Runs the job. data is the payload deserialized with System.Text.Json default options ( null / default when the payload is empty). The token is the host's stopping token. Return JobResult.Ok() or JobResult.Fail(...) . Must be a public method on the handler class (see Worker loop ). IBackgroundJob public interface IBackgroundJob — a payload-less job abstraction (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Abstractions ). Nothing in the package executes it; the worker only runs IBackgroundJobHandler<TData> handlers. Member Description ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken) Returns Task<JobResult> . JobResult public sealed record JobResult(bool Success, bool Retry = false, string? ErrorMessage = null) — the outcome returned by a handler (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core ). Member Description Success true when the job succeeded. Retry When Success is false , whether the worker should retry (subject to MaxAttempt ). ErrorMessage Stored in JobEntity.LastError when the job ends as Failed . Ok() Static. Returns a successful result. Fail(string message, bool retry = false) Static. Returns a failed result. Note that retry defaults to false , so a plain Fail("...") is not retried. IJobHandlerRegistry public interface IJobHandlerRegistry — maps handler names to handler and payload types (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core ). Member Description Register<THandler, TData>(string handlerName) Constraint: THandler : class, IBackgroundJobHandler<TData> . Adds or replaces the mapping for handlerName . TryGet(string handlerName, out Type? handlerType, out Type? dataType) Returns true and the two types when handlerName is registered. JobHandlerRegistry public class JobHandlerRegistry : IJobHandlerRegistry — thread-safe default registry backed by a ConcurrentDictionary . Member Description Register<THandler, TData>(string handlerName) Throws ArgumentException when handlerName is null, empty or whitespace. Names are case-sensitive. TryGet(string handlerName, out Type? handlerType, out Type? dataType) Returns false for a null or unknown name. IJobStore public interface IJobStore — persistence for jobs (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Abstractions ). Implement it to use another storage; register your implementation before calling AddCrispyBackgroundJobs . Member Description SaveAsync(JobEntity job, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Stores a new job. FetchNextAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Returns the next due Pending job ( ScheduledAt null or not after now) and marks it Processing , or null . Implementations should claim the job atomically. MarkCompletedAsync(Guid jobId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Sets status Completed . MarkFailedAsync(Guid jobId, string error, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Sets status Failed and LastError . MarkRetryAsync(Guid jobId, DateTimeOffset? nextAttemptAt, int attemptCount, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Sets status Pending , ScheduledAt = nextAttemptAt and Attempt = attemptCount . InMemoryJobStore public class InMemoryJobStore : IJobStore — default store, process-local (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Persistence ). Implements every IJobStore member; all methods complete synchronously and ignore the token. Unknown ids are ignored. See Job stores for its limits. EfCoreJobStore public class EfCoreJobStore : IJobStore — store backed by JobDbContext (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Persistence ). Member Description EfCoreJobStore(JobDbContext db) Constructor. SaveAsync(...) Sets UpdatedAt , adds the job and calls SaveChangesAsync . FetchNextAsync(...) Queries the first due pending job id ordered by priority then CreatedAt , loads it, sets Processing and saves. Returns null if nothing is due or if SaveChangesAsync throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException . MarkCompletedAsync(...) / MarkFailedAsync(...) / MarkRetryAsync(...) Load the job, update it as described in IJobStore , and save. Unknown ids are ignored. JobDbContext public class JobDbContext : DbContext — EF Core context for the EfCoreJobStore (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Persistence ). Member Description JobDbContext(DbContextOptions<JobDbContext> options) Constructor, used by AddDbContext<JobDbContext> . Jobs DbSet<JobEntity> . OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder) Protected. Key Id ; HandlerName required, max length 256; Payload optional; Priority and Status stored as int ; CreatedAt and UpdatedAt required; database defaults MaxAttempt = 3 and Attempt = 0 . BackgroundWorker public class BackgroundWorker : BackgroundService — the hosted service that runs jobs (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core ). Registered by AddCrispyBackgroundJobs ; you do not use it directly. See Worker loop and Lifecycle and retries . Member Description BackgroundWorker(IServiceProvider provider, JobOptions options, ILogger<BackgroundWorker> logger) Constructor. Resolves BackgroundJobQueue and IJobStore (both optional) and IJobHandlerRegistry (required) from provider . Uses the store when one is registered, otherwise the queue. ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken) Protected override. Starts WorkerCount loops and completes when all of them stop. BackgroundJobQueue public class BackgroundJobQueue — in-memory priority queue used only when no IJobStore is registered (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core ). Member Description Enqueue(JobEntity job) Adds the job with its Priority (lower value first) and signals a waiting consumer. DequeueAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken) Waits for a signal and returns the highest-priority job. Returns null when cancelled. When the worker uses this queue, a job that is not yet due is dequeued and enqueued again in a tight loop until it is due. JobOptions public class JobOptions — worker settings, configured through AddCrispyBackgroundJobs (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core ). Registered as a plain singleton, not through IOptions<T> . Member Description WorkerCount int . Number of concurrent worker loops. Default Environment.ProcessorCount . DefaultMaxAttempt int . MaxAttempt for jobs added through JobDispatcher without maxAttempts . Default 3 . PollingInterval TimeSpan . Sleep between store polls when no job is due. Default 2 seconds. MaxBackoffSeconds int . Default 300 . Not used; the worker's 300-second cap is hard-coded. JobEntity public class JobEntity — a stored job (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Abstractions ). Member Description Id Guid . Default Guid.NewGuid() . HandlerName string . Name registered in IJobHandlerRegistry . Default empty. Payload string . JSON payload. Default empty. Priority JobPriority . Default Normal . Status JobStatus . Default Pending . ScheduledAt DateTimeOffset? . When the job becomes due; null means immediately. Attempt int . Number of failed executions so far. Default 0 . MaxAttempt int . Maximum executions for JobResult.Fail(..., retry: true) outcomes. Default 3 . LastError string? . Error recorded when the job is marked Failed . CreatedAt DateTimeOffset . Default UtcNow at construction. UpdatedAt DateTimeOffset . Updated by the stores on every change. RetryDelaySeconds int . Default 0 . Not used by the worker. JobPriority public enum JobPriority — lower values run first. Value Description High (0) Picked before Normal and Low . Normal (1) Default. Low (2) Picked last. JobStatus public enum JobStatus — job lifecycle state. Value Description Pending (0) Waiting to run, or waiting for a retry. Processing (1) Claimed by a worker. Completed (2) Handler returned success. Failed (3) Handler failed with no retries left, did not ask for a retry, or could not be found. Dead (4) Not used by the library. JobMetrics public class JobMetrics — thread-safe named counters, registered as a singleton (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Monitoring ). Nothing in the package increments them. Member Description Increment(string key) Adds 1 to key , creating it at 1. Get(string key) Returns the value of key , or 0 . Snapshot() Returns a copy of all counters as IDictionary<string, long> . MonitoringMiddleware public class MonitoringMiddleware — ASP.NET Core middleware that exposes JobMetrics (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Monitoring ). Member Description MonitoringMiddleware(RequestDelegate next, JobMetrics metrics) Constructor, called by UseMiddleware<MonitoringMiddleware>() . InvokeAsync(HttpContext context) For paths starting with /jobs/metrics , writes the snapshot as application/json and ends the request. Otherwise calls next . CronJobService public abstract class CronJobService : BackgroundService — base class for work that repeats every minute (namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Scheduling ). See Recurring work . Member Description CronJobService(ILogger logger) Protected constructor. ExecuteOnce(CancellationToken stoppingToken) Protected abstract. Your work. Exceptions are logged and the loop continues. ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken) Protected override. Calls ExecuteOnce , then waits one minute, until the host stops. JobFailedException public class JobFailedException : Exception — namespace CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Exceptions . Has one constructor, JobFailedException(string message) . The package never throws it; if a handler throws it, it is treated like any other exception (logged and retried). Examples Schedule a delayed, high-priority job JobDispatcher returns the job id; IJobScheduler does not. using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Abstractions; using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core; public sealed class ReminderService(JobDispatcher dispatcher) { public Task<Guid> RemindNowAsync(string email) => dispatcher.EnqueueAsync("send-email", new SendEmailData(email, "Reminder")); public Task RemindLaterAsync(string email) => dispatcher.ScheduleAsync( "send-email", new SendEmailData(email, "Your trial ends tomorrow"), TimeSpan.FromHours(1), maxAttempts: 5, priority: JobPriority.High ); } Expose metrics Increment counters from your handlers and map the middleware. using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Abstractions; using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core; using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Extensions; using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Monitoring; var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); builder.Services.AddCrispyBackgroundJobs(); builder.Services.AddJobHandler<ResizeImageHandler, ResizeImageData>("resize-image"); var app = builder.Build(); app.UseMiddleware<MonitoringMiddleware>(); // GET /jobs/metrics -> {"resize-image.ok":12} app.Run(); public sealed record ResizeImageData(string Path, int Width); public sealed class ResizeImageHandler(JobMetrics metrics) : IBackgroundJobHandler<ResizeImageData> { public Task<JobResult> HandleAsync(ResizeImageData data, CancellationToken cancellationToken) { // resize data.Path to data.Width here metrics.Increment("resize-image.ok"); return Task.FromResult(JobResult.Ok()); } } Use the EF Core store Register the context, the queue that JobDispatcher needs, and create the table at startup. Keep one worker because the store's DbContext is shared (see Job stores ), and disable scope validation, which otherwise rejects the scoped store inside singletons. using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core; using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Extensions; using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Persistence; using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore; var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); builder.Host.UseDefaultServiceProvider(o => { o.ValidateScopes = false; o.ValidateOnBuild = false; }); builder.Services.AddDbContext<JobDbContext>(o => o.UseSqlServer(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Jobs")) ); builder.Services.AddSingleton<BackgroundJobQueue>(); builder.Services.AddCrispyBackgroundJobs(o => o.WorkerCount = 1, useEfCoreStore: true); builder.Services.AddJobHandler<SendEmailHandler, SendEmailData>("send-email"); var app = builder.Build(); using (var scope = app.Services.CreateScope()) { scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<JobDbContext>().Database.EnsureCreated(); } app.Run(); UseSqlServer comes from the Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer package; use the provider for your database. Use a generic host AddJobHandler relies on an ASP.NET Core startup filter. In a worker service, register the handler in DI and in the registry yourself before the host starts. using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core; using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Extensions; var builder = Host.CreateApplicationBuilder(args); builder.Services.AddCrispyBackgroundJobs(); builder.Services.AddScoped<SendEmailHandler>(); var host = builder.Build(); host.Services.GetRequiredService<IJobHandlerRegistry>() .Register<SendEmailHandler, SendEmailData>("send-email"); host.Run(); Run work every minute using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Abstractions; using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Scheduling; public sealed class CleanupService(ILogger<CleanupService> logger, IJobScheduler jobs) : CronJobService(logger) { protected override Task ExecuteOnce(CancellationToken stoppingToken) => jobs.EnqueueAsync("cleanup", new { OlderThanDays = 30 }); } // builder.Services.AddHostedService<CleanupService>(); The anonymous payload is serialized as {"OlderThanDays":30} , so the cleanup handler's payload type needs a matching OlderThanDays property. See also Diagrams Scheduler for cron-based scheduling in the core package HTTP client , the other standalone Microsoft.Extensions based package

Records the outcome in the store (see below). An unexpected error in the loop itself is logged and the loop waits 1 second before continuing. The handler is invoked by reflection: the worker looks up a public method named HandleAsync on the concrete handler type. Implement IBackgroundJobHandler<TData>.HandleAsync as a normal public method, not as an explicit interface implementation, and do not add other HandleAsync overloads; otherwise the call throws and the job is retried as described below.
docs.title: Worker loop

docs.text: Outcome What happens Handler returns JobResult.Ok() MarkCompletedAsync : status Completed . Handler returns JobResult.Fail(message, retry: true) and Attempt + 1 < MaxAttempt Attempt is incremented and MarkRetryAsync sets status Pending with ScheduledAt = UtcNow + backoff . Handler returns Fail with retry: false , or attempts are used up MarkFailedAsync : status Failed , LastError = message (or "Job failed" when the message is null ). No handler registered under the job's name MarkFailedAsync with "No handler registered for '<name>'" . Not retried. Handler type cannot be resolved from DI MarkFailedAsync with "Handler type <type> not resolved from DI" . Not retried. Handler throws, or the payload cannot be deserialized Logged, Attempt incremented, rescheduled with backoff. MaxAttempt is not checked on this path, so a job that always throws is retried indefinitely (every 300 seconds once the cap is reached). The backoff is min(2^min(Attempt, 10), 300) seconds, where Attempt is the already incremented count: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, then 300 seconds. The cap is hard-coded; JobOptions.MaxBackoffSeconds is not read. JobEntity.RetryDelaySeconds is also not read. MaxAttempt counts total executions. With the default of 3, a handler that keeps returning Fail(..., retry: true) runs three times and is then marked Failed . On shutdown, a job interrupted by the stopping token is normally caught by the "handler throws" path and rescheduled with backoff. The JobStatus.Dead value is never assigned by the library.
docs.title: Lifecycle and retries

docs.text: In-memory (default). InMemoryJobStore keeps jobs in a ConcurrentDictionary . Jobs are lost when the process stops, and completed and failed jobs are never removed. FetchNextAsync selects and marks a job in two separate steps without a lock, so with more than one worker the same job can occasionally be picked by two loops. Set WorkerCount = 1 if handlers must not run twice. EF Core. Pass useEfCoreStore: true and register JobDbContext yourself with your database provider, for example services.AddDbContext<JobDbContext>(o => o.UseSqlServer(connectionString)) . You must also create the Jobs table, for example with db.Database.EnsureCreated() or with migrations generated against JobDbContext (migrations need a MigrationsAssembly in your project, since the context lives in this package). The EF Core mode has wiring problems you need to work around: JobDispatcher takes a BackgroundJobQueue constructor parameter, but the queue is only registered in in-memory mode. Without services.AddSingleton<BackgroundJobQueue>() , resolving JobDispatcher or IJobScheduler fails. EfCoreJobStore is scoped, but the singleton BackgroundWorker and JobDispatcher resolve it from the root provider. With scope validation enabled (the default in the Development environment) the host fails to start with a "Cannot consume scoped service" error. With validation disabled, a single JobDbContext instance is shared by every worker loop and every caller of the dispatcher. DbContext is not thread-safe, so keep WorkerCount = 1 and avoid enqueueing while the worker is running, or register your own IJobStore that creates a context per call. No concurrency token is configured on JobEntity , so FetchNextAsync does not prevent two processes from claiming the same job. Treat the EF Core store as experimental until these are fixed.
docs.title: Job stores

docs.text: JobMetrics is a singleton dictionary of named counters. The library registers it but does not increment any counter itself, so you record the values you care about, for example from your handlers. MonitoringMiddleware serves JobMetrics.Snapshot() as a JSON object ( {"counter": value} ) for any request whose path starts with the segment /jobs/metrics , and passes every other request on. There is no UseXxx extension; add it with app.UseMiddleware<MonitoringMiddleware>() . The endpoint has no authentication of its own.
docs.title: Monitoring

docs.text: CronJobService is an abstract BackgroundService that calls ExecuteOnce in a loop with a fixed one-minute delay after each run. Despite the file name ( CronJobScheduler.cs ), it does not accept or parse a cron expression, and it is not registered by AddCrispyBackgroundJobs . Register a subclass with AddHostedService . For real cron expressions, use the core scheduler , or enqueue jobs from your subclass.

docs.text: using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Abstractions; using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Core; using CrispyWaffle.BackgroundJobs.Extensions; var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); builder.Services.AddCrispyBackgroundJobs(o => o.WorkerCount = 2); builder.Services.AddJobHandler<SendEmailHandler, SendEmailData>("send-email"); var app = builder.Build(); app.MapPost( "/signup", async (string email, IJobScheduler jobs) => { await jobs.EnqueueAsync("send-email", new SendEmailData(email, "Welcome!")); return Results.Accepted(); } ); app.Run(); public sealed record SendEmailData(string To, string Subject); public sealed class SendEmailHandler(ILogger<SendEmailHandler> logger) : IBackgroundJobHandler<SendEmailData> { public async Task<JobResult> HandleAsync(SendEmailData data, CancellationToken cancellationToken) { try { logger.LogInformation("Sending '{Subject}' to {To}", data.Subject, data.To); await Task.Delay(100, cancellationToken); // send the email here return JobResult.Ok(); } catch (HttpRequestException ex) { return JobResult.Fail(ex.Message, retry: true); } } }

docs.text: CrispyWaffle.Configuration CrispyWaffle.Configuration holds the connection settings that the connector packages (Redis, CouchDB, Elasticsearch, RabbitMQ, SMTP) take. A Connection stores a host, a port and a set of credentials. When it is serialized, the password is encrypted, so you can keep connections in configuration files without writing passwords in plain text. Use this package whenever you create a connector from one of the other CrispyWaffle packages. You can also use it for your own connection settings. Package CrispyWaffle.Configuration Namespace CrispyWaffle.Configuration Install dotnet add package CrispyWaffle.Configuration Depends on CrispyWaffle How it works Connection implements IConnection , and its Credentials property holds an IConnectionCredential . The default constructor sets Credentials to a new Credentials instance, so you can use object-initializer syntax such as Credentials = { Username = "...", Password = "..." } without creating the credentials object yourself. Connectors read Host , Port , Credentials.Username and Credentials.Password from the connection in their constructors. They don't keep the connection after that, so changing a Connection after a connector has been created has no effect on that connector. Password encryption Credentials has two password properties: Password holds the plain-text value. It has [XmlIgnore] and both JsonIgnore attributes (Newtonsoft and System.Text.Json), so serializers never write it. PasswordInternal is the value that gets serialized, under the name Password (XML element, Newtonsoft JsonProperty and System.Text.Json JsonPropertyName ). When PasswordInternal is read, the plain-text password is encrypted with Security.Encrypt and a 32-character MD5 hash of the encrypted text is appended. When the password is empty or whitespace, the getter returns an empty string. When PasswordInternal is assigned, the setter does the reverse: If the last 32 characters match the MD5 hash of the rest of the value, the rest is decrypted and stored as the plain-text password. If they don't match, or the value is 32 characters or shorter, or decryption throws, the value is stored as the plain-text password. Because of this fallback, a configuration file can hold either an encrypted password or a plain-text one. The encryption keys come from an ISecureCredentialProvider that Credentials resolves through ServiceLocator.Resolve<ISecureCredentialProvider>() every time PasswordInternal is read or assigned. Register one before you serialize or deserialize credentials that have a password. The same keys must be used on both sides. Connection has the [Serializer] attribute, which uses XML as the default format. The Name property is written as an XML attribute, and the credentials are written through the hidden CredentialsInternal property as a Credentials element. Getting started using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Configuration; // Register the keys used to encrypt and decrypt serialized passwords. ServiceLocator.Register<ISecureCredentialProvider>( () => new SecureCredentialProvider { PasswordHash = "Cr1$PTVV@FE13", SaltKey = "y48H85nH21", IVKey = "HZEM7|Ne2YGS/F41", }, Lifetime.Singleton ); // Describe a connection. Credentials is created by the constructor. var connection = new Connection { Name = "Redis", Host = "localhost", Port = 6379, Credentials = { Username = "default", Password = "myP@ssw0rd" }, }; Pass the connection to a connector constructor, for example new RedisConnector(connection, serializer) . See CrispyWaffle.Redis , CrispyWaffle.CouchDB and CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch . Reference Connection public sealed class Connection : IConnection is the default implementation of IConnection , with XML serialization support. Member Description Connection() Constructor. Sets Credentials to a new Credentials instance. Name Connection name or identifier. Serialized as the XML attribute Name . Host Host name or address. Some connectors expect the URL scheme here (see the CouchDB page). Port Port number. Credentials The IConnectionCredential used to authenticate. Has [XmlIgnore] . CredentialsInternal Infrastructure property, hidden from IntelliSense. Casts Credentials to Credentials so the XML serializer can write it as the Credentials element. Reading it throws InvalidCastException if Credentials holds a different IConnectionCredential implementation. Don't use it directly. IConnection public interface IConnection is the contract that every connector constructor accepts. Member Description Name Connection name or identifier. Host Host name or address. Port Port number. Credentials Credentials used to authenticate. IConnectionCredential public interface IConnectionCredential is a username and password pair. Member Description Username User name. Password Plain-text password. ISecureCredentialProvider public interface ISecureCredentialProvider supplies the keys that Credentials uses to encrypt and decrypt serialized passwords. Credentials resolves it from ServiceLocator . Member Description PasswordHash Password used to derive the encryption key. SaltKey Salt used to derive the encryption key. IVKey Initialization vector. Credentials public sealed class Credentials : IConnectionCredential, INotifyPropertyChanged is the default credential implementation. It encrypts the password when serialized. Member Description Username User name. Raises PropertyChanged when set. Password Plain-text password. Never serialized. Raises PropertyChanged when set. PasswordInternal Infrastructure property, hidden from IntelliSense, serialized as Password . The getter returns the encrypted password followed by its MD5 hash, or an empty string when there is no password. The setter decrypts a value in that format, or stores any other value as plain text. Both resolve ISecureCredentialProvider from ServiceLocator when there is a value to process. Raises PropertyChanged with the name PasswordInternal . PropertyChanged Event raised when Username , Password or PasswordInternal is set. SecureCredentialProvider public class SecureCredentialProvider : ISecureCredentialProvider is a plain implementation of ISecureCredentialProvider with settable properties. Member Description PasswordHash Password used to derive the encryption key. SaltKey Salt used to derive the encryption key. IVKey Initialization vector. ConnectionNameAttribute public sealed class ConnectionNameAttribute : Attribute is a marker that records which named connection a connector class expects. You can apply it to a class more than once. The connectors in the CrispyWaffle packages use it to declare their expected names: "Redis" , "RedisMaster" and "RedisSlave" , "CouchDB" , "ElasticSearch" , "RabbitMQ" and "SMTP" . No code in the CrispyWaffle packages reads the attribute. It's metadata for your own configuration-loading code. Member Description ConnectionNameAttribute(string name) Constructor. Sets Name . Name The connection name. Order Ordering hint for when a class needs more than one connection, such as MasterSlaveConfiguration . Defaults to 0 . Examples Round-trip credentials through JSON The serialized output contains the encrypted password under Password . Assigning that value to PasswordInternal restores the plain-text password. using CrispyWaffle.Configuration; using CrispyWaffle.Serialization; using CrispyWaffle.Utilities; // Requires an ISecureCredentialProvider registered in ServiceLocator. var credential = new Credentials { Password = "EchoFoxPapa" }; var json = (string)credential.GetCustomSerializer(SerializerFormat.Json); dynamic deserialized = SerializerFactory .GetCustomSerializer<DynamicSerialization>(SerializerFormat.Json) .Deserialize(json); var restored = new Credentials { PasswordInternal = (string)deserialized.Password }; // restored.Password == "EchoFoxPapa" Mark a custom connector with its connection name using CrispyWaffle.Configuration; [ConnectionName("Billing")] public sealed class BillingApiConnector { public BillingApiConnector(IConnection connection) { BaseUrl = $"https://{connection.Host}:{connection.Port}"; ApiUser = connection.Credentials.Username; } public string BaseUrl { get; } public string ApiUser { get; } } See also CrispyWaffle.Redis CrispyWaffle.CouchDB CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch CrispyWaffle.RabbitMQ Cryptography Serialization Service locator

It has [XmlIgnore] and both JsonIgnore attributes (Newtonsoft and System.Text.Json), so serializers never write it. PasswordInternal is the value that gets serialized, under the name Password (XML element, Newtonsoft JsonProperty and System.Text.Json JsonPropertyName ). When PasswordInternal is read, the plain-text password is encrypted with Security.Encrypt and a 32-character MD5 hash of the encrypted text is appended. When the password is empty or whitespace, the getter returns an empty string. When PasswordInternal is assigned, the setter does the reverse: If the last 32 characters match the MD5 hash of the rest of the value, the rest is decrypted and stored as the plain-text password. If they don't match, or the value is 32 characters or shorter, or decryption throws, the value is stored as the plain-text password. Because of this fallback, a configuration file can hold either an encrypted password or a plain-text one. The encryption keys come from an ISecureCredentialProvider that Credentials resolves through ServiceLocator.Resolve<ISecureCredentialProvider>() every time PasswordInternal is read or assigned. Register one before you serialize or deserialize credentials that have a password. The same keys must be used on both sides. Connection has the [Serializer] attribute, which uses XML as the default format. The Name property is written as an XML attribute, and the credentials are written through the hidden CredentialsInternal property as a Credentials element.

docs.text: using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Configuration; // Register the keys used to encrypt and decrypt serialized passwords. ServiceLocator.Register<ISecureCredentialProvider>( () => new SecureCredentialProvider { PasswordHash = "Cr1$PTVV@FE13", SaltKey = "y48H85nH21", IVKey = "HZEM7|Ne2YGS/F41", }, Lifetime.Singleton ); // Describe a connection. Credentials is created by the constructor. var connection = new Connection { Name = "Redis", Host = "localhost", Port = 6379, Credentials = { Username = "default", Password = "myP@ssw0rd" }, }; Pass the connection to a connector constructor, for example new RedisConnector(connection, serializer) . docs.text: CrispyWaffle.CouchDB CrispyWaffle.CouchDB provides a cache repository that stores documents in Apache CouchDB , using the CouchDB.NET driver. Use it when cached data should survive restarts and be readable from any process that can reach the CouchDB server, and when the cached values are documents rather than plain strings or numbers. Package CrispyWaffle.CouchDB Namespace CrispyWaffle.CouchDB.Cache , CrispyWaffle.CouchDB.Utils.Communications Install Not yet published to NuGet (it is not in the release workflow's package list). Reference the project: dotnet add reference Src/CrispyWaffle.CouchDB/CrispyWaffle.CouchDB.csproj Depends on CrispyWaffle , CrispyWaffle.Configuration , CouchDB.NET How it works Connecting CouchDBConnector creates a CouchDB.NET CouchClient from an IConnection . The client URL is "{Host}:{Port}" , so Host must include the scheme, for example http://localhost . The client always uses basic authentication with Credentials.Username and Credentials.Password . You can also pass a CouchClient that you have configured yourself. Documents and databases Only types derived from CouchDBCacheDocument can be stored. CouchDBCacheDocument.Key is the CouchDB document ID, so one key holds at most one document. SubKey is an ordinary document field that the sub-key overloads use as an extra filter. The repository picks a database from the document type: the type name in lowercase followed by s . For example, CouchDBCacheDocument maps to couchdbcachedocuments and a Car subclass maps to cars . If that database isn't in the server's database list, it's created. If it's already there, the repository opens it with CouchClient.GetDatabase<T>() . There are two groups of methods: The ICacheRepository methods ( SetAsync , GetAsync , TryGetAsync , RemoveAsync , TTLAsync , Clear ) always use the database of the base CouchDBCacheDocument type. SetAsync<T> returns without storing anything when T doesn't derive from CouchDBCacheDocument , and GetAsync<T> returns default . Values are read back as CouchDBCacheDocument and then cast to T . The *Specific* methods ( SetSpecificAsync<T> , GetSpecificAsync<T> , RemoveSpecificAsync<T> , Clear<T> , GetDocCount<T> ) use the database of T . Use them for your own document subclasses. Expiration SetSpecificAsync(value, key, ttl) stores ttl in TTL and DateTime.UtcNow + ttl in ExpiresAt . CouchDB doesn't expire documents itself. Expiration is checked when a document is read: If ExpiresAt is set and in the past, the read deletes the document and returns default . The sub-key SetAsync and SetSpecificAsync overloads don't set a TTL. TTLAsync returns the stored TTL value, which is the original lifetime, not the time remaining. Errors ShouldPropagateExceptions defaults to false . When it's false : Most failures are passed to LogConsumer.Handle and the method returns normally. The Remove* methods and TTLAsync also log through LogConsumer.Error . GetSpecificAsync throws InvalidOperationException after logging a suppressed error. In both modes: A document that doesn't exist is returned as null , not as an error. OperationCanceledException is logged as a warning and rethrown by most methods. The exception is TryGetAsync<T>(key) , which returns (false, default) on cancellation. Dispose() disposes the CouchDBConnector , which disposes the CouchClient . Getting started Start CouchDB locally. The repository's docker-compose.yml runs couchdb:latest on port 5984 with the user Admin and the password myP@ssw0rd . using CrispyWaffle.Cache; using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Configuration; using CrispyWaffle.CouchDB.Cache; using CrispyWaffle.CouchDB.Utils.Communications; var connection = new Connection { Host = "http://localhost", // include the scheme Port = 5984, Credentials = { Username = "Admin", Password = "myP@ssw0rd" }, }; ServiceLocator.Register(() => new CouchDBConnector(connection), Lifetime.Singleton); ServiceLocator.Register( () => new CouchDBCacheRepository(ServiceLocator.Resolve<CouchDBConnector>()), Lifetime.Singleton ); CacheManager.AddRepository<CouchDBCacheRepository>(); // Use the repository directly for typed documents. var repository = ServiceLocator.Resolve<CouchDBCacheRepository>(); var doc = new CouchDBCacheDocument(); await repository.SetAsync(doc, Guid.NewGuid().ToString()); var stored = await repository.GetAsync<CouchDBCacheDocument>(doc.Key); Reference CouchDBCacheRepository public class CouchDBCacheRepository : ICacheRepository, IDisposable is a cache repository that stores CouchDBCacheDocument instances in CouchDB. Member Description CouchDBCacheRepository(CouchDBConnector connector) Constructor. ShouldPropagateExceptions When true , CouchDB errors are rethrown. When false (default), they are logged and suppressed. SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, TimeSpan? ttl = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) When T derives from CouchDBCacheDocument , calls SetSpecificAsync with value cast to CouchDBCacheDocument , so it's stored in the base document database. Does nothing for other types. Returns ValueTask . SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Same as above, but sets Key and SubKey (trimmed) and calls CreateOrUpdateAsync . Suppressed errors are logged with LogConsumer.Error . GetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Reads document key from the base document database and casts it to T . Returns default when T doesn't derive from CouchDBCacheDocument , or when the document is missing or expired. Returns ValueTask<T> . GetAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Same, but matches on both Key and SubKey . TryGetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Returns (true, value) when a document is found, otherwise (false, default) . Returns (false, default) on cancellation instead of throwing. TryGetAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Same, matching on Key and SubKey . Rethrows OperationCanceledException . RemoveAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) / RemoveAsync(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Removes a document from the base document database. See RemoveSpecificAsync . TTLAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Returns the TTL stored on document key , or TimeSpan.Zero when there is no document or a suppressed error occurred. Clear() / Clear<T>() Deletes every document in the base document database, or in the database of T . Blocks until all deletes finish. GetDocCount<T>() Returns the number of documents with a non-null ID in the database of T . T : CouchDBCacheDocument . SetSpecificAsync<T>(T value, string key, TimeSpan? ttl = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Sets value.Key , sets TTL and ExpiresAt when ttl is given, and creates the document in the database of T with CreateAsync . T : CouchDBCacheDocument . Returns Task . SetSpecificAsync<T>(T value, string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Sets Key and SubKey (trimmed) and calls CreateOrUpdateAsync in the database of T . GetSpecificAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Finds document key in the database of T . Returns null when it doesn't exist. Deletes it and returns null when it has expired. Throws InvalidOperationException after a suppressed error. GetSpecificAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Same, matching on Key and SubKey . RemoveSpecificAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Deletes document key from the database of T . Logs at info level whether the document was found. Throws ArgumentException when key is null, empty or whitespace. RemoveSpecificAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Same, matching on Key and SubKey . Dispose() Disposes the connector. CouchDBConnector public class CouchDBConnector : IDisposable holds the CouchDB.NET client. It has the [ConnectionName("CouchDB")] attribute. Member Description CouchDBConnector(IConnection connection) Creates a CouchClient for "{connection.Host}:{connection.Port}" with basic authentication from connection.Credentials . CouchDBConnector(CouchClient client) Wraps an existing client. CouchDBClient The CouchClient instance. Use it for operations the repository doesn't cover. Dispose() Disposes the client. Dispose(bool disposing) Protected virtual. Disposes CouchDBClient when disposing is true . Override it in subclasses to release extra resources. CouchDBCacheDocument public class CouchDBCacheDocument : CouchDocument is the base class for everything stored by CouchDBCacheRepository . Derive from it to add your own fields. Id and Rev come from CouchDB.NET's CouchDocument . Member Description Key The cache key. Reads and writes the document Id . SubKey Optional secondary key, stored as a field. ExpiresAt UTC time after which the document is treated as expired. default means it never expires. TTL The lifetime the document was stored with. Examples Store a custom document type in its own database Documents of type Car go to the cars database. using CrispyWaffle.CouchDB.Cache; public class Car : CouchDBCacheDocument { public Car(string maker) => Maker = maker; public string Maker { get; set; } } var car = new Car("MakerOne"); await repository.SetSpecificAsync(car, Guid.NewGuid().ToString()); var fromDb = await repository.GetSpecificAsync<Car>(car.Key); await repository.RemoveSpecificAsync<Car>(car.Key); Store a document that expires var key = Guid.NewGuid().ToString(); await repository.SetAsync(new CouchDBCacheDocument(), key, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)); await Task.Delay(6000); var expired = await repository.GetAsync<CouchDBCacheDocument>(key); // null; the document was deleted Clear a database and count documents await repository.Clear(); var remaining = await repository.GetDocCount<CouchDBCacheDocument>(); // 0 See also Caching CrispyWaffle.Configuration CrispyWaffle.Redis

docs.text: CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch connects CrispyWaffle to Elasticsearch through the official Elastic.Clients.Elasticsearch client. It provides: A log provider that indexes every log message as a document and deletes old log documents once, shortly after startup. A small wrapper for reading and writing documents. Index helpers that derive index names from your types. Use it when you want CrispyWaffle logs searchable in Elasticsearch or Kibana, or when you need simple document storage without writing client code yourself. Package CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch Namespace CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch.Log , CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch.Helpers , CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch.Utils.Communications Install dotnet add package CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch Depends on CrispyWaffle , CrispyWaffle.Configuration , Elastic.Clients.Elasticsearch How it works Connecting ElasticConnector builds an ElasticsearchClient from an IConnection : The scheme is https when Port is 443 , and http otherwise. Basic authentication is added only when Credentials isn't null and Credentials.Username isn't blank. The client's default index is the defaultIndexName constructor argument. When you don't pass one, it's logs-{EnvironmentHelper.ApplicationName}-{EnvironmentHelper.Version} . Register the connector as a singleton. ElasticWrapper and ElasticSearchLogProvider take it in their constructors. The static Extensions class resolves it from ServiceLocator . Log provider ElasticSearchLogProvider is an ILogProvider . Each logging call that passes the level check builds a LogMessage and indexes it in the connector's default index. The LogMessage carries: The application name, date, host name and process ID. The local and remote IP addresses. The operation, user agent, thread ID and thread name. Indexing calls are started but not awaited. Logging never blocks, and indexing errors aren't reported back to the caller. The provider's level starts with no flags set, so call SetLevel after adding it. Ten seconds after it's constructed, the provider runs a single delete-by-query against the default index. The query removes LogMessage documents whose Date is older than logRetentionDays days. This cleanup runs once per provider instance, not on a schedule. AbortGarbageCollector() and Dispose() cancel the cleanup if it hasn't run yet. Index names Extensions.GetIndexName<T>() decides which index a type belongs to: If the type has an [IndexName] attribute, that name is used. Otherwise, the type name in lowercase is used (with spaces replaced by - ). ElasticWrapper 's *WithResolver methods and the Extensions methods use this name. Types used with them must implement the marker interface IIndexable . Getting started Start Elasticsearch locally. The repository's docker-compose.yml runs elasticsearch:8.8.0 as a single node on port 9200 with security disabled. using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Configuration; using CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch.Log; using CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch.Utils.Communications; using CrispyWaffle.Log; var connection = new Connection { Host = "localhost", Port = 9200 }; var connector = new ElasticConnector(connection, "logs-my-app"); ServiceLocator.Register(connector); // Index log messages and delete log documents older than 30 days. LogConsumer .AddProvider(new ElasticSearchLogProvider(connector, 30)) .SetLevel(LogLevel.Production); LogConsumer.Info("Application started"); Reference ElasticConnector public sealed class ElasticConnector creates and holds the ElasticsearchClient . It has the [ConnectionName("ElasticSearch")] attribute. Member Description ElasticConnector(IConnection connection) Uses logs-{EnvironmentHelper.ApplicationName}-{EnvironmentHelper.Version} as the default index. ElasticConnector(IConnection connection, string defaultIndexName) Builds the client for connection.Host:connection.Port with defaultIndexName as the default index. Throws ArgumentNullException when connection is null . Client The ElasticsearchClient . Use it for anything the wrapper doesn't cover. DefaultIndexName The default index name passed to the client. ElasticSearchLogProvider public class ElasticSearchLogProvider : ILogProvider, IDisposable indexes log messages in Elasticsearch. Member Description ElasticSearchLogProvider(ElasticConnector elastic, int logRetentionDays) Constructor. Uses elastic.Client and elastic.DefaultIndexName , and schedules the one-time retention cleanup to run 10 seconds later. SetLevel(LogLevel level) Sets which levels are indexed. Nothing is indexed until this is called. Fatal(category, message) / Error(category, message) / Warning(category, message) / Info(category, message) / Debug(category, message) Indexes a message at that level when the level is enabled. docs.text: ElasticConnector builds an ElasticsearchClient from an IConnection : The scheme is https when Port is 443 , and http otherwise. Basic authentication is added only when Credentials isn't null and Credentials.Username isn't blank. The client's default index is the defaultIndexName constructor argument. When you don't pass one, it's logs-{EnvironmentHelper.ApplicationName}-{EnvironmentHelper.Version} . Register the connector as a singleton. ElasticWrapper and ElasticSearchLogProvider take it in their constructors. The static Extensions class resolves it from ServiceLocator .
docs.title: Connecting

docs.text: ElasticSearchLogProvider is an ILogProvider . Each logging call that passes the level check builds a LogMessage and indexes it in the connector's default index. The LogMessage carries: The application name, date, host name and process ID. The local and remote IP addresses. The operation, user agent, thread ID and thread name. Indexing calls are started but not awaited. Logging never blocks, and indexing errors aren't reported back to the caller. The provider's level starts with no flags set, so call SetLevel after adding it. Ten seconds after it's constructed, the provider runs a single delete-by-query against the default index. The query removes LogMessage documents whose Date is older than logRetentionDays days. This cleanup runs once per provider instance, not on a schedule. AbortGarbageCollector() and Dispose() cancel the cleanup if it hasn't run yet.

docs.text: Extensions.GetIndexName<T>() decides which index a type belongs to: If the type has an [IndexName] attribute, that name is used. Otherwise, the type name in lowercase is used (with spaces replaced by - ). ElasticWrapper 's *WithResolver methods and the Extensions methods use this name. Types used with them must implement the marker interface IIndexable .

docs.text: Start Elasticsearch locally. The repository's docker-compose.yml runs elasticsearch:8.8.0 as a single node on port 9200 with security disabled. using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Configuration; using CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch.Log; using CrispyWaffle.ElasticSearch.Utils.Communications; using CrispyWaffle.Log; var connection = new Connection { Host = "localhost", Port = 9200 }; var connector = new ElasticConnector(connection, "logs-my-app"); ServiceLocator.Register(connector); // Index log messages and delete log documents older than 30 days. LogConsumer .AddProvider(new ElasticSearchLogProvider(connector, 30)) .SetLevel(LogLevel.Production); LogConsumer.Info("Application started");

docs.text: CrispyWaffle.Elmah CrispyWaffle.Elmah provides an exception handler that sends exceptions handled by CrispyWaffle to ELMAH, through the ElmahCore library for ASP.NET Core. Use it when your web application already uses ElmahCore and you want exceptions passed to LogConsumer.Handle to show up in the ELMAH error log. Package CrispyWaffle.Elmah Namespace CrispyWaffle.Elmah Install dotnet add package CrispyWaffle.Elmah Depends on CrispyWaffle , ElmahCore How it works ElmahExceptionHandler implements IExceptionHandler . Set it as the handler with LogConsumer.SetHandler ; after that, every LogConsumer.Handle(...) call goes to it. For each exception the handler: Works out a category by walking the call stack and taking the full name of the first declaring type whose namespace does not start with CrispyWaffle . Builds one text block with the message, type name and stack trace of the exception and of each inner exception. While doing so, it calls Error(category, message) on every provider added with ExceptionLogType.Message , once per exception in the chain. Writes the combined messages with Error(category, ...) to every provider added with ExceptionLogType.Full . Calls ElmahCore's ElmahExtensions.RaiseError(exception) . ElmahCore must be configured in your host ( services.AddElmah(...) and app.UseElmah() , following the ElmahCore documentation) for the raised errors to be stored. The list of additional providers is static. Providers added through one ElmahExceptionHandler instance are used by every instance, and there is no way to remove them. Getting started using CrispyWaffle.Elmah; using CrispyWaffle.Log; using ElmahCore.Mvc; var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); builder.Services.AddElmah(); var app = builder.Build(); app.UseElmah(); LogConsumer.SetHandler(new ElmahExceptionHandler()); app.MapGet("/fail", () => { try { throw new InvalidOperationException("Something failed"); } catch (Exception e) { LogConsumer.Handle(e); return Results.Problem(); } }); app.Run(); Reference ElmahExceptionHandler public sealed class ElmahExceptionHandler : IExceptionHandler — exception handler that raises exceptions in ELMAH and optionally copies them to other log providers. Member Description ElmahExceptionHandler() Implicit parameterless constructor. Handle(Exception exception) Processes exception as described in How it works. Handle(object sender, UnhandledExceptionEventArgs args) Casts args.ExceptionObject to Exception and processes it. Suitable for AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException . Handle(object sender, ThreadExceptionEventArgs args) Processes args.Exception . AddLogProvider<TLogProvider>(ExceptionLogType type) Resolves TLogProvider through ServiceLocator.Resolve<TLogProvider>() , adds it to the shared provider list with type , and returns it. TLogProvider must implement ILogProvider . ExceptionLogType is defined in the core package ( CrispyWaffle.Log.Handlers ): Message and Full . See Logging . Examples Copy exceptions to a text file log Exceptions still go to ELMAH, and the full exception text is also written to the text file provider. TextFileLogProvider and its adapter must be resolvable through ServiceLocator . using CrispyWaffle.Elmah; using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Handlers; using CrispyWaffle.Log.Providers; var handler = new ElmahExceptionHandler(); handler.AddLogProvider<TextFileLogProvider>(ExceptionLogType.Full).SetLevel(LogLevel.All); LogConsumer.SetHandler(handler); AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException += handler.Handle; See also Logging Service locator CrispyWaffle.Log4Net

docs.text: CrispyWaffle.EventLog CrispyWaffle.EventLog writes CrispyWaffle log messages to the Windows Event Log. Use it for Windows services and desktop applications whose operators read logs in Event Viewer. The package uses System.Diagnostics.EventLog , which only works on Windows. The library targets .NET Standard and .NET and has no platform annotation, so it builds anywhere, but on Linux and macOS the System.Diagnostics.EventLog calls throw PlatformNotSupportedException . Package CrispyWaffle.EventLog Namespace CrispyWaffle.EventLog.Log.Providers , CrispyWaffle.EventLog.Log.Adapters Install dotnet add package CrispyWaffle.EventLog Depends on CrispyWaffle , System.Diagnostics.EventLog How it works EventLogProvider is the ILogProvider you register with LogConsumer . It forwards every call to an EventLogAdapter , which writes entries to a System.Diagnostics.EventLog . The category argument is not used. Log and source. The adapter writes to the log named by logName , or to Application when logName is null, empty or whitespace. The source name is cut to 212 characters and < and > are replaced by _ . Source registration. Creating an event source requires administrator rights. By default ( manageEventSource: false ) the adapter only sets the source name; register the source beforehand, for example during installation with EventLog.CreateEventSource . With manageEventSource: true the adapter creates the source when it does not exist. If the source exists in a different log, the adapter deletes it from that log and writes a warning entry, under a helper source named serilog-{logName} , saying that a restart may be required before entries appear in the new log. Levels and entry types. The adapter starts with no level enabled; call SetLevel after you register the provider. Levels map to entry types as follows: LogLevel EventLogEntryType Fatal , Error Error Warning Warning Info , Trace , Debug Information Message size. Messages longer than 31,839 characters are truncated. Exceptions are written as one entry that contains the message and stack trace of the exception and of each inner exception, separated by \r\n . Event IDs. Each entry gets an event ID from an IEventIdProvider . The default EventIdProvider hashes the message text into a 16-bit number, so the same message always gets the same ID. Getting started using CrispyWaffle.EventLog.Log.Providers; using CrispyWaffle.Log; LogConsumer.AddProvider(new EventLogProvider("my-service")).SetLevel(LogLevel.Production); LogConsumer.Info("Service started"); Reference EventLogProvider public sealed class EventLogProvider : ILogProvider — log provider that writes to the Windows Event Log through an EventLogAdapter . Member Description EventLogProvider() Constructor. Uses source crispy-waffle , the Application log, the local machine, no source management, and EventIdProvider . EventLogProvider(string source) Constructor. Uses source , the Application log, the local machine, no source management, and EventIdProvider . EventLogProvider(string source, string logName) Constructor. Same as above with the given log name. EventLogProvider(string source, string logName, string machineName, bool manageEventSource, IEventIdProvider eventIdProvider) Constructor. Uses EventIdProvider when eventIdProvider is null . Throws ArgumentNullException when source is null . SetLevel(LogLevel level) Sets the enabled levels on the adapter. Fatal(category, message) / Error(category, message) / Warning(category, message) / Info(category, message) Writes message at that level. Trace(category, message) Writes message at trace level. Trace(category, message, exception) Writes message , then the exception details, as two entries at trace level. Trace(category, exception) Writes the exception details as one entry at trace level. Debug(category, message) Writes message at debug level. Debug(category, content, identifier) Writes "{identifier}: {content}" at debug level. Debug<T>(string category, T content, string identifier, SerializerFormat customFormat = SerializerFormat.None) Serializes content with its [Serializer] format (or with customFormat when it is not None ) and writes "{identifier}: {serialized}" at debug level. T must be class, new() . IEventIdProvider public interface IEventIdProvider — computes the event ID for a log entry. Implement it to control event IDs, for example to map known messages to fixed IDs. Member Description ushort ComputeEventId(string message) Returns the event ID for message . EventIdProvider public class EventIdProvider : IEventIdProvider — default implementation that hashes the message. Member Description ComputeEventId(string message) Returns a 16-bit hash of message (a Jenkins one-at-a-time hash truncated to ushort ). Throws ArgumentNullException when message is null . EventLogAdapter public sealed class EventLogAdapter : ILogAdapter — writes to a System.Diagnostics.EventLog . EventLogProvider creates one internally; use it directly only if you build your own provider. Member Description EventLogAdapter(string source, string logName, string machineName, bool manageEventSource, IEventIdProvider eventIdProvider) Constructor. Normalizes the source name, opens the log ( Application when logName is null or whitespace) and either registers the source ( manageEventSource: true ) or only sets it. Throws ArgumentNullException when source or eventIdProvider is null . SetLevel(LogLevel level) Sets the enabled levels. Fatal(message) / Error(message) / Warning(message) / Info(message) Writes message at that level. Trace(message) Writes message at trace level. Trace(message, exception) Writes message , then the exception details, as two entries at trace level. Trace(exception) Writes the exception details as one entry at trace level. Debug(message) Writes message at debug level. Debug(string content, string fileName) Writes "{fileName}: {content}" at debug level. Debug<T>(T content, string identifier, SerializerFormat customFormat = SerializerFormat.None) Serializes content and writes "{identifier}: {serialized}" at debug level. T must be a class. Dispose() Does nothing. The underlying EventLog is not disposed. Examples Write to a custom log with source management Run once with administrator rights so the source can be created in the MyCompany log. using System; using CrispyWaffle.EventLog.Log.Providers; using CrispyWaffle.Log; var provider = new EventLogProvider( "billing-service", "MyCompany", Environment.MachineName, manageEventSource: true, eventIdProvider: null ); LogConsumer.AddProvider(provider).SetLevel(LogLevel.All); LogConsumer.Warning("Invoice queue is above {0} items", 1000); Use fixed event IDs Return the same event ID for every entry from a source. using System; using CrispyWaffle.EventLog.Log.Providers; var provider = new EventLogProvider( "billing-service", "Application", Environment.MachineName, false, new FixedEventIdProvider() ); public sealed class FixedEventIdProvider : IEventIdProvider { public ushort ComputeEventId(string message) => 1000; } See also Logging CrispyWaffle.Log4Net
