docs.text: CrispyWaffle.HttpClient CrispyWaffle.HttpClient is a small wrapper around IHttpClientFactory that sends JSON requests, retries transient failures with exponential backoff, and returns every result as an HttpResponse<T> instead of throwing (unless you ask it to throw). Use it when you want typed JSON calls with retries and a uniform result object, without adding Polly. The package is standalone: it does not reference the core CrispyWaffle package and does not use ServiceLocator . It is wired up through Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection and consumed by injecting IHttpClientWrapper . Package CrispyWaffle.HttpClient Namespace CrispyWaffle.HttpClient , CrispyWaffle.HttpClient.Serialization , CrispyWaffle.HttpClient.Exceptions Install Not yet published to NuGet (it is not in the release workflow's package list). Reference the project: dotnet add reference Src/CrispyWaffle.HttpClient/CrispyWaffle.HttpClient.csproj Target framework net10.0 only Depends on No CrispyWaffle packages. Microsoft.Extensions.Http (which brings Microsoft.Extensions.Options , Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions and DI abstractions) How it works Registration AddCrispyWaffleHttpClient calls services.AddHttpClient() , binds HttpRequestOptions through services.Configure , and registers two singletons: IJsonSerializer as SystemTextJsonSerializer and IHttpClientWrapper as HttpClientWrapper . The wrapper also takes an optional ILogger<HttpClientWrapper> ; if logging is registered, it logs header, read and deserialization problems. Request flow For each call, the wrapper: Merges the registered default options with the per-request HttpRequestOptions , if any (see Per-request options ). Picks the serializer: options.Serializer if set, otherwise the IJsonSerializer from DI. Creates a client from IHttpClientFactory ( CreateClient(NamedHttpClient) when NamedHttpClient is set, otherwise CreateClient() ), then: sets BaseAddress from the options only if the client has no base address yet; sets Timeout to max(1, TimeoutSeconds) seconds, overwriting any timeout configured on a named client; adds each DefaultRequestHeaders entry to the client's default headers (invalid headers are skipped and logged as warnings); adds Accept: application/json if the client has no Accept header. Builds a new HttpRequestMessage for every attempt. If a body is present, it is serialized with the chosen serializer and sent as UTF-8 StringContent with content type application/json (or text/plain when UseJsonContentType is false ). The headers are also copied onto the message with TryAddWithoutValidation . Sends with HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead through the retry policy below. Reads the body as a string, collects response and content headers into Headers , and builds the result: 2xx : deserializes the body into T (an empty or whitespace body gives default(T) ). A deserialization error gives a failed result with the error "DeserializationFailed: <message>" . Any other status : a failed result whose Errors holds "HTTP <code> <reason>" and, if non-empty, the raw body. No response after retries : a failed result with StatusCode = null and one error (the last exception message, or "Unknown error" ). When ThrowOnError is true , each of the failure cases above throws HttpClientException instead of returning a failed result. Duration covers all attempts and retry delays, up to the arrival of the final response headers (it does not include reading the body). Retry policy Retries are handled by an internal policy (no Polly dependency). With the default RetryCount = 3 , a call makes up to 4 attempts. What is retried: Trigger Retried Status code >= 500 Yes 408 Request Timeout Yes 429 Too Many Requests Yes, honoring Retry-After Any other status (including all other 4xx) No. Returned immediately HttpRequestException Yes OperationCanceledException (including TaskCanceledException from HttpClient.Timeout ) Yes TimeoutException Yes Any other exception No. It propagates out of the call unwrapped Delay before the next attempt, where attempt is 0 for the first try: capped = min(RetryBaseDelayMs * 2^min(attempt, 10), MaxRetryDelayMs) delay = max(0, capped + capped * 0.2 * (random[0,1) - 0.5)) // jitter of +/-10% With the defaults ( RetryBaseDelayMs = 200 , MaxRetryDelayMs = 10000 ) the waits are about 200 ms, 400 ms and 800 ms. For a 429 response with a Retry-After header (delta seconds or an HTTP date, read from response or content headers), the delay becomes min(Retry-After, MaxRetryDelayMs) with no jitter. Edge cases to be aware of: If the last attempt still returns a retryable status, the policy waits one more delay and then reports "no response". The result has StatusCode = null and no body, so the final 5xx / 429 status is not visible to the caller. If RetryCount <= 0 , the request is sent once and any exception is captured into a failed result (or an HttpClientException when ThrowOnError is true ), rather than propagating. Cancelling the CancellationToken while a retry is pending throws TaskCanceledException from the delay. If cancellation hits the final attempt, the call returns a failed "no response" result instead. A Retry-After date in the past produces a negative delay, and Task.Delay throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException . Per-request options When you pass an HttpRequestOptions to a call, it is merged with the registered defaults like this: Property Merge rule BaseAddress , NamedHttpClient , Serializer Per-request value if not null , else default TimeoutSeconds , RetryCount , RetryBaseDelayMs , MaxRetryDelayMs Per-request value if not 0 , else default ThrowOnError , UseJsonContentType Always the per-request value DefaultRequestHeaders Union of both; per-request keys win (case-insensitive) Because a new HttpRequestOptions already has non-zero numeric defaults (30, 3, 200, 10000) and ThrowOnError = false , passing one replaces your registered values for those properties with the class defaults unless you set them again. Setting RetryCount = 0 per request does not disable retries; it falls back to the registered default. To disable retries, set RetryCount = 0 in the registered options. Naming conflicts HttpRequestOptions also exists as System.Net.Http.HttpRequestOptions . Projects with ImplicitUsings enabled import System.Net.Http globally, so naming the type alone gives error CS0104 (ambiguous reference). Add an alias: using HttpRequestOptions = CrispyWaffle.HttpClient.HttpRequestOptions; . The examples on this page do this. Inside a namespace that starts with CrispyWaffle , the name HttpClient resolves to the CrispyWaffle.HttpClient namespace, not System.Net.Http.HttpClient . Use the fully qualified name or an alias if you need the BCL type there. Getting started using CrispyWaffle.HttpClient; using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; var services = new ServiceCollection(); services.AddLogging(); services.AddCrispyWaffleHttpClient(o => { o.BaseAddress = "https://api.example.com/"; o.TimeoutSeconds = 10; o.RetryCount = 2; }); using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(); var http = provider.GetRequiredService<IHttpClientWrapper>(); HttpResponse<Todo> response = await http.GetAsync<Todo>("todos/1"); if (response.IsSuccess) { Console.WriteLine($"{response.Data!.Title} ({response.Duration.TotalMilliseconds} ms)"); } else { Console.WriteLine($"Failed: {response.StatusCode} {string.Join("; ", response.Errors ?? [])}"); } public sealed record Todo(int Id, string Title, bool Completed); Reference ServiceCollectionExtensions public static class ServiceCollectionExtensions — DI registration for the wrapper (namespace CrispyWaffle.HttpClient ). Member Description AddCrispyWaffleHttpClient(this IServiceCollection services, Action<HttpRequestOptions>? configureOptions = null) Calls AddHttpClient() , configures HttpRequestOptions with configureOptions (or an empty configuration), and registers IJsonSerializer -> SystemTextJsonSerializer and IHttpClientWrapper -> HttpClientWrapper , both as singletons. Returns services . To use a different serializer, register your own IJsonSerializer after this call so it replaces the default. IHttpClientWrapper public interface IHttpClientWrapper — the high-level HTTP API. Inject this. Member Description GetAsync<T>(string url, HttpRequestOptions? options = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Sends GET and deserializes a 2xx body into T . Returns Task<HttpResponse<T>> . PostAsync<TRequest, TResponse>(string url, TRequest? body = default, HttpRequestOptions? options = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Sends POST with body serialized as JSON (no content when body is null ). Returns Task<HttpResponse<TResponse>> . PutAsync<TRequest, TResponse>(string url, TRequest? body = default, HttpRequestOptions? options = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Same as PostAsync with PUT . DeleteAsync(string url, HttpRequestOptions? options = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Sends DELETE . Returns Task<HttpResponse<object?>> ; a JSON body is deserialized as object (a JsonElement with the default serializer). Get<T>(url, options) / Post<TRequest, TResponse>(url, body, options) / Put<TRequest, TResponse>(url, body, options) / Delete(url, options) Synchronous versions that block on the async methods with GetAwaiter().GetResult() . No cancellation token. They can deadlock under a synchronization context; prefer the async methods. url is either absolute or relative to BaseAddress . A relative URL with no base address throws InvalidOperationException from HttpClient , which is not retried and propagates (when RetryCount > 0 ). HttpClientWrapper public class HttpClientWrapper : IHttpClientWrapper — the default implementation described in How it works . Member Description HttpClientWrapper(IHttpClientFactory httpClientFactory, IOptions<HttpRequestOptions> options, IJsonSerializer? serializer = null, ILogger<HttpClientWrapper>? logger = null) Constructor. Throws ArgumentNullException when httpClientFactory is null . Uses new HttpRequestOptions() when options or its value is null , and new SystemTextJsonSerializer() when serializer is null . All IHttpClientWrapper members See above. HttpRequestOptions public class HttpRequestOptions — registered defaults (through IOptions<HttpRequestOptions> ) and per-request overrides. Member Description BaseAddress string? . Base URL for the created client. Only applied if the client has no base address already. Default null . TimeoutSeconds int . Per-attempt timeout; values below 1 become 1. Default 30 . RetryCount int . Number of retries after the first attempt. 0 or less means a single attempt. Default 3 . RetryBaseDelayMs int . Base delay for exponential backoff. Default 200 . MaxRetryDelayMs int . Upper bound for one retry delay, including Retry-After . Default 10000 . ThrowOnError bool . Throw HttpClientException on failure instead of returning a failed HttpResponse<T> . Default false . DefaultRequestHeaders IDictionary<string, string>? . Headers added to every request. Default null . NamedHttpClient string? . Name passed to IHttpClientFactory.CreateClient(name) . Default null (unnamed client). UseJsonContentType bool . Send request bodies as application/json ; when false , text/plain . The body is serialized with the JSON serializer either way. Default true . Serializer IJsonSerializer? . Serializer override. Default null (use the one from DI). HttpResponse<T> public class HttpResponse<T> — the result of every wrapper call. Member Description IsSuccess true for a 2xx response whose body deserialized without error. StatusCode HttpStatusCode? . null when no response was received. Data T? . The deserialized body; default on failure or empty body. RawContent string? . The response body as text. Errors IList<string>? . Failure messages; null on success. Headers IDictionary<string, IEnumerable<string>>? . Response and content headers. null when no response was received. Duration TimeSpan . Time spent on all attempts and retry delays, up to the final response headers. Success(T? data, HttpStatusCode statusCode, string? rawContent, IDictionary<string, IEnumerable<string>>? headers, TimeSpan duration) Static factory for a successful result. Failure(HttpStatusCode? statusCode, string? rawContent, IList<string>? errors, IDictionary<string, IEnumerable<string>>? headers, TimeSpan duration) Static factory for a failed result. IJsonSerializer public interface IJsonSerializer — pluggable serializer (namespace CrispyWaffle.HttpClient.Serialization ). Implementations must be thread-safe because the registered instance is a singleton. Member Description Serialize<T>(T value) Returns the JSON string for value . Used for request bodies. Deserialize<T>(string json) Returns json as T . Used for response bodies. Deserialize(string json, Type type) Non-generic form. Not used by the wrapper. SystemTextJsonSerializer public class SystemTextJsonSerializer : IJsonSerializer — the default serializer, based on System.Text.Json . Member Description SystemTextJsonSerializer(JsonSerializerOptions? options = null) Constructor. When options is null , uses camelCase property names, case-insensitive property matching, and DefaultIgnoreCondition = WhenWritingNull . Serialize<T>(T value) JsonSerializer.Serialize(value, options) . Deserialize<T>(string json) Returns default for null or whitespace input, otherwise JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T> . Deserialize(string json, Type type) Returns null for null or whitespace input, otherwise JsonSerializer.Deserialize(json, type, options) . HttpClientException public class HttpClientException : Exception — thrown on failure when ThrowOnError is true (namespace CrispyWaffle.HttpClient.Exceptions ). Member Description HttpClientException(string message, HttpStatusCode? statusCode = null, string? responseContent = null, Exception? inner = null) Constructor. StatusCode HttpStatusCode? . Status of the failed response; null when no response was received. ResponseContent string? . Response body, when available. Thrown with these messages: Message Situation StatusCode InnerException HTTP request failed after retries No usable response after all attempts null Last exception, if any Failed to read response content Reading the body threw Response status The read exception Failed to deserialize response to <T> 2xx body could not be deserialized Response status The deserialization exception HTTP request failed with <code> Non-2xx, non-retryable status Response status null Examples Post a body and throw on failure Set ThrowOnError per request to get exceptions instead of a failed result. Remember that a per-request options object also resets the numeric settings to their class defaults. using CrispyWaffle.HttpClient; using CrispyWaffle.HttpClient.Exceptions; using HttpRequestOptions = CrispyWaffle.HttpClient.HttpRequestOptions; public sealed class OrdersClient(IHttpClientWrapper http) { public async Task<OrderCreated?> CreateAsync(NewOrder order, CancellationToken ct) { try { var response = await http.PostAsync<NewOrder, OrderCreated>( "orders", order, new HttpRequestOptions { ThrowOnError = true, TimeoutSeconds = 5 }, ct ); return response.Data; } catch (HttpClientException ex) { Console.WriteLine($"Order API failed: {ex.StatusCode} {ex.ResponseContent}"); return null; } } } public sealed record NewOrder(string Sku, int Quantity); public sealed record OrderCreated(Guid Id); Use a named client and per-request headers Configure the named client with AddHttpClient , then point the wrapper at it. The base address from the named client is kept; TimeoutSeconds from the options still overrides its timeout. using CrispyWaffle.HttpClient; using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using HttpRequestOptions = CrispyWaffle.HttpClient.HttpRequestOptions; var services = new ServiceCollection(); services.AddHttpClient("github", c => { c.BaseAddress = new Uri("https://api.github.com/"); c.DefaultRequestHeaders.UserAgent.ParseAdd("crispy-waffle-sample"); }); services.AddCrispyWaffleHttpClient(o => o.NamedHttpClient = "github"); using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(); var http = provider.GetRequiredService<IHttpClientWrapper>(); var response = await http.GetAsync<Repo>( "repos/guibranco/CrispyWaffle", new HttpRequestOptions { DefaultRequestHeaders = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["X-GitHub-Api-Version"] = "2022-11-28", }, } ); Console.WriteLine(response.Data?.FullName); public sealed record Repo(string FullName, int StargazersCount); Use custom JSON settings Register your own IJsonSerializer after AddCrispyWaffleHttpClient to replace the default for every call, or set HttpRequestOptions.Serializer for a single call. using System.Text.Json; using CrispyWaffle.HttpClient; using CrispyWaffle.HttpClient.Serialization; using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; var services = new ServiceCollection(); services.AddCrispyWaffleHttpClient(); services.AddSingleton<IJsonSerializer>( new SystemTextJsonSerializer( new JsonSerializerOptions { PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower } ) ); See also Diagrams Serialization for the core package's serializers Background jobs , the other standalone Microsoft.Extensions based package

docs.text: Set ThrowOnError per request to get exceptions instead of a failed result. Remember that a per-request options object also resets the numeric settings to their class defaults. using CrispyWaffle.HttpClient; using CrispyWaffle.HttpClient.Exceptions; using HttpRequestOptions = CrispyWaffle.HttpClient.HttpRequestOptions; public sealed class OrdersClient(IHttpClientWrapper http) { public async Task<OrderCreated?> CreateAsync(NewOrder order, CancellationToken ct) { try { var response = await http.PostAsync<NewOrder, OrderCreated>( "orders", order, new HttpRequestOptions { ThrowOnError = true, TimeoutSeconds = 5 }, ct ); return response.Data; } catch (HttpClientException ex) { Console.WriteLine($"Order API failed: {ex.StatusCode} {ex.ResponseContent}"); return null; } } } public sealed record NewOrder(string Sku, int Quantity); public sealed record OrderCreated(Guid Id);

docs.text: CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr adds string extension methods for Brazilian data: parsing Brazilian phone numbers and formatting CPF/CNPJ documents and CEP zip codes. Use it when you receive these values as free text (with or without punctuation) and need a normalized value or a display format. Package CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr Namespace CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr Install dotnet add package CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr Depends on CrispyWaffle (no third-party package) How it works All methods remove non-digit characters from the input before working on it, so (11) 98765-4321 , 11 98765 4321 and 11987654321 are equivalent. Phone numbers TryParseBrazilianPhoneNumber applies these rules to the digits: If the digits start with 55 and there are 12 to 14 of them, the 55 country code is removed. If fewer than 10 or more than 12 digits remain, parsing fails. The area code (DDD) is the first two digits, or digits two and three when the number starts with 0 and has 11 or 12 digits (a trunk prefix such as 011 ). If the ninth digit from the end is 9 , the number is the last nine digits (mobile number with the extra 9). Otherwise it is the last eight digits. Rule 4 also applies to 10-digit input, where the ninth digit from the end is the second digit of the area code. A landline in an area code ending in 9 (for example 19 3234-5678 ) is therefore parsed as the nine-digit number 932345678 . The result is a PhoneNumber (from the core package, namespace CrispyWaffle.Utilities ) with CountryCode 55, RegionCode set to the area code and Number set to the subscriber number. PhoneNumber.IsNinthDigit is true when the number has nine digits. ParseBrazilianPhoneNumber does the same but throws InvalidTelephoneNumberException (namespace CrispyWaffle.GoodPractices ) when parsing fails. The exception message contains the digits only, for example The value '123456' isn't a valid telephone number. for the input abc123def456 . Documents and zip codes FormatBrazilianDocument picks the pattern from the length of the input string as given (not of its digits): 14 characters use the CNPJ pattern 00.000.000/0000-00 , any other length uses the CPF pattern 000.000.000-00 . Pass unformatted digits. The digits are converted to a number, so leading zeros are restored by the pattern ( 01234567890 becomes 012.345.678-90 ). FormatBrazilianZipCode removes non-digits and rewrites every run of eight digits as 00000-000 . For a normal CEP that is the whole value; extra digits are left as they are. Getting started using CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr; var phone = "5511987654321".ParseBrazilianPhoneNumber(); // phone.CountryCode == 55, phone.RegionCode == 11, phone.Number == 987654321, phone.IsNinthDigit == true var cpf = "12345678900".FormatBrazilianDocument(); // "123.456.789-00" var cnpj = "12345678901234".FormatBrazilianDocument(); // "12.345.678/9012-34" var cep = "01310100".FormatBrazilianZipCode(); // "01310-100" Reference ConversionExtensions public static class ConversionExtensions — extension methods on string for Brazilian phone numbers, documents and zip codes. Member Description ParseBrazilianPhoneNumber(this string number) Parses number with the rules in How it works and returns a PhoneNumber . Throws InvalidTelephoneNumberException with the digits of number when it is not a valid Brazilian phone number. TryParseBrazilianPhoneNumber(this string number, ref PhoneNumber result) Parses number and stores the result in result . Returns true on success and false when the number of digits is invalid; result is unchanged on failure. Throws NullReferenceException when number is null . FormatBrazilianDocument(this string document) Formats document as a CNPJ ( 00.000.000/0000-00 ) when the input is 14 characters long, otherwise as a CPF ( 000.000.000-00 ). Returns "Invalid document" when document is null, empty or whitespace. FormatBrazilianZipCode(this string zipCode) Removes non-digits and formats each run of eight digits as 00000-000 . Returns "Invalid zipcode" when zipCode is null, empty or whitespace. Fewer than eight digits are returned unformatted. Examples Parse phone numbers in different formats Outputs match the package's unit tests. using CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr; var a = "5511987654321".ParseBrazilianPhoneNumber(); // 55, 11, 987654321, IsNinthDigit: true var b = "551187654321".ParseBrazilianPhoneNumber(); // 55, 11, 87654321, IsNinthDigit: false var c = "11987654321".ParseBrazilianPhoneNumber(); // 55, 11, 987654321, IsNinthDigit: true var d = "1187654321".ParseBrazilianPhoneNumber(); // 55, 11, 87654321, IsNinthDigit: false Validate user input without exceptions TryParseBrazilianPhoneNumber takes the result by ref , so initialize it first. using CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr; using CrispyWaffle.Utilities; var phone = new PhoneNumber(0, 0, 0); if ("(11) 98765-4321".TryParseBrazilianPhoneNumber(ref phone)) { // phone.ToString() == "5511987654321" } var valid = "190".TryParseBrazilianPhoneNumber(ref phone); // false Handle an invalid phone number using CrispyWaffle.GoodPractices; using CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr; try { "abc123def456".ParseBrazilianPhoneNumber(); } catch (InvalidTelephoneNumberException e) { // e.Message == "The value '123456' isn't a valid telephone number." } Format documents using CrispyWaffle.I18n.PtBr; "12345678900".FormatBrazilianDocument(); // "123.456.789-00" "12345678901234".FormatBrazilianDocument(); // "12.345.678/9012-34" string.Empty.FormatBrazilianDocument(); // "Invalid document" See also Utilities Extensions Validations

docs.text: CrispyWaffle.Log4Net CrispyWaffle.Log4Net is a bridge that sends CrispyWaffle log calls to an Apache log4net logger. Use it when your application already configures log4net appenders and you want messages written through LogConsumer to go to the same destinations. Package CrispyWaffle.Log4Net Namespace CrispyWaffle.Log4Net Install dotnet add package CrispyWaffle.Log4Net Depends on CrispyWaffle , log4net How it works Log4NetLogProvider implements ILogProvider and wraps a log4net ILog . You configure log4net (appenders, layouts, thresholds) as usual, get an ILog from LogManager , and register the provider with LogConsumer . The provider filters calls by its own CrispyWaffle LogLevel first. It starts with no level enabled, so call SetLevel after you register it. Calls that pass the filter go to the log4net method shown below. log4net then applies its own level thresholds. CrispyWaffle call log4net call Fatal ILog.Fatal Error ILog.Error Warning ILog.Warn Info ILog.Info Trace (all overloads) ILog.Info Debug (all overloads) ILog.Debug The category argument is not forwarded; log4net uses the logger name of the ILog you pass in. Exceptions are not passed to log4net as exception objects. The provider writes the message and stack trace of the exception and of each inner exception as separate Info entries. Getting started using System.IO; using System.Reflection; using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Log4Net; using log4net; using log4net.Config; var repository = LogManager.GetRepository(Assembly.GetEntryAssembly()); XmlConfigurator.Configure(repository, new FileInfo("log4net.config")); var log = LogManager.GetLogger(typeof(Program)); LogConsumer.AddProvider(new Log4NetLogProvider(log)).SetLevel(LogLevel.All); LogConsumer.Info("Application started"); Reference Log4NetLogProvider public sealed class Log4NetLogProvider : ILogProvider — log provider that writes to a log4net ILog . Member Description Log4NetLogProvider(ILog adapter) Constructor. The argument is not checked for null . SetLevel(LogLevel level) Sets the enabled levels. Calls for levels that are not enabled are ignored. Fatal(category, message) Writes message with ILog.Fatal . Error(category, message) Writes message with ILog.Error . Warning(category, message) Writes message with ILog.Warn . Info(category, message) Writes message with ILog.Info . Trace(category, message) Writes message with ILog.Info . Trace(category, message, exception) Writes message , then the message and stack trace of exception and each inner exception, with ILog.Info . Trace(category, exception) Writes the message and stack trace of exception and each inner exception with ILog.Info . Debug(category, message) Writes message with ILog.Debug . Debug(category, content, identifier) Writes identifier , then content , as two ILog.Debug entries. Debug<T>(string category, T content, string identifier, SerializerFormat customFormat = SerializerFormat.None) Writes identifier , then content serialized with its [Serializer] format (or with customFormat when it is not None ), as two ILog.Debug entries. T must be class, new() . Examples Use a named logger and a narrower level Only errors and fatal messages reach log4net. using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Log4Net; using log4net; var provider = new Log4NetLogProvider(LogManager.GetLogger("CrispyWaffle")); provider.SetLevel(LogLevel.Fatal | LogLevel.Error); LogConsumer.AddProvider(provider); LogConsumer.Error("Payment gateway returned {0}", 503); See also Logging CrispyWaffle.EventLog CrispyWaffle.Elmah

docs.text: CrispyWaffle.RabbitMQ CrispyWaffle.RabbitMQ sends and receives messages through a RabbitMQ broker and provides a log provider that publishes CrispyWaffle log messages to a RabbitMQ exchange. Use it when you want to publish typed messages to a queue or an exchange with a few lines of code, consume them through an event, or ship your application logs to RabbitMQ. Package CrispyWaffle.RabbitMQ Namespace CrispyWaffle.RabbitMQ.Utils.Communications , CrispyWaffle.RabbitMQ.Helpers , CrispyWaffle.RabbitMQ.Log Install dotnet add package CrispyWaffle.RabbitMQ Depends on CrispyWaffle , CrispyWaffle.Configuration , RabbitMQ.Client How it works RabbitMQConnector turns an IConnection (host, port, credentials) into a RabbitMQ.Client IConnectionFactory and stores a default exchange name. Every other type in the package takes a connector. Message types are plain classes that: implement the marker interface IQueuing , have a public parameterless constructor (the methods use the class, IQueuing, new() constraint), carry a [Serializer] attribute, because the body is produced with GetSerializer() . With [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Json)] the body is JSON; with the attribute's default format the body is XML. Without the attribute, sending throws InvalidOperationException . The target name comes from the message type: [QueueName("...")] sets the queue name and [ExchangeName("...")] sets the exchange name. Without the attribute, the name is the class name in lowercase (for example OrderCreated becomes ordercreated ). Sending RabbitMQWrapper opens a new connection and channel for every call and disposes them when the call ends. Messages are published as persistent and UTF-8 encoded. SendToQueueAsync publishes to the default exchange with the queue name as routing key. By default it first declares the queue as durable, non-exclusive and not auto-deleted. SendToExchangeAsync publishes to the named exchange with an empty routing key. It declares the exchange (durable, not auto-deleted) only when you pass an exchange type such as ExchangeType.Fanout . After each send the wrapper writes a trace entry through LogConsumer with the target name and the serialized body. Receiving MessageReceiver starts a background task for each ReceiveFromQueue<T> or ReceiveFromExchange<T> call and returns immediately. The task keeps its connection and channel open until the CancellationToken is canceled. ReceiveFromQueue<T> consumes from the queue named by T . It does not declare the queue, so the queue must already exist. ReceiveFromExchange<T> declares a server-named queue, binds it to the exchange named by T with an empty routing key, and consumes from it. The exchange must already exist. Each delivery is decoded as UTF-8 and raised through the MessageReceived event as a MessageReceivedArgs (queue name and body). The body is the raw string; deserialize it yourself. The event handler runs on the RabbitMQ consumer thread. The receiver has no API to acknowledge messages. Pass autoAck: true unless you only want to peek: with autoAck: false messages stay unacknowledged and are redelivered when the channel closes. Deliveries that arrive while no handler is subscribed to MessageReceived are ignored. Exceptions in the background task (for example a failed connection) are not surfaced to the caller. Log provider RabbitMQLogProvider implements ILogProvider . Its constructor connects synchronously, opens a channel and declares the connector's DefaultExchangeName as a durable fanout exchange. Log calls build a LogMessage (application, host, IP addresses, level, thread, and so on), serialize it as JSON and put it in an in-memory queue. A dedicated worker thread publishes the queued messages to the exchange with an empty routing key. Publish failures are written to LogConsumer.Trace and the message is dropped. The worker thread is a foreground thread that only stops after the CancellationToken passed to the constructor is canceled, so cancel that token when your application shuts down or the process will not exit. The provider starts with no level enabled; call SetLevel before it writes anything. Getting started using System; using System.Threading.Tasks; using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Configuration; using CrispyWaffle.RabbitMQ.Helpers; using CrispyWaffle.RabbitMQ.Utils.Communications; using CrispyWaffle.Serialization; [QueueName("orders")] [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Json)] public class OrderCreated : IQueuing { public Guid Id { get; set; } public string Customer { get; set; } } public static class Program { public static async Task Main() { var connection = new Connection { Host = "localhost", Port = 5672, Credentials = { Username = "guest", Password = "guest" }, }; ServiceLocator.Register(new RabbitMQConnector(connection)); var wrapper = ServiceLocator.Resolve<RabbitMQWrapper>(); await wrapper.SendToQueueAsync(new OrderCreated { Id = Guid.NewGuid(), Customer = "ACME" }); } } Reference RabbitMQWrapper public class RabbitMQWrapper — publishes serialized messages to RabbitMQ queues and exchanges. Member Description RabbitMQWrapper(RabbitMQConnector connector) Constructor. Throws ArgumentNullException when connector is null . SendToExchangeAsync<T>(T item, string exchangeDeclareType = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Serializes item and publishes it as a persistent message to the exchange named by T (see ExchangeNameAttribute ), with an empty routing key. When exchangeDeclareType is not null or whitespace, declares the exchange first with that type, durable and not auto-deleted. Returns Task . T must be class, IQueuing, new() . SendToQueueAsync<T>(T item, bool queueDeclare = true, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Serializes item and publishes it as a persistent message to the queue named by T (see QueueNameAttribute ) through the default exchange. When queueDeclare is true , declares the queue first as durable, non-exclusive and not auto-deleted. Returns Task . T must be class, IQueuing, new() . MessageReceiver public class MessageReceiver — consumes messages from a queue or an exchange in the background and raises an event for each one. Member Description MessageReceiver(RabbitMQConnector connector) Constructor. Throws ArgumentNullException when connector is null . MessageReceivedHandler Nested delegate: public delegate void MessageReceivedHandler(object sender, MessageReceivedArgs e) . MessageReceived event MessageReceivedHandler . Raised for each delivery with the queue name and the UTF-8 decoded body. ReceiveFromQueue<T>(bool autoAck, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Starts a background consumer on the existing queue named by T . Returns immediately. The consumer stops when cancellationToken is canceled. ReceiveFromExchange<T>(bool autoAck, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Declares a server-named queue, binds it to the existing exchange named by T with an empty routing key, and starts a background consumer on it. Use it when you want to publish typed messages to a queue or an exchange with a few lines of code, consume them through an event, or ship your application logs to RabbitMQ. docs.text: RabbitMQConnector turns an IConnection (host, port, credentials) into a RabbitMQ.Client IConnectionFactory and stores a default exchange name. Every other type in the package takes a connector. Message types are plain classes that: implement the marker interface IQueuing , have a public parameterless constructor (the methods use the class, IQueuing, new() constraint), carry a [Serializer] attribute, because the body is produced with GetSerializer() . With [Serializer(SerializerFormat.Json)] the body is JSON; with the attribute's default format the body is XML. Without the attribute, sending throws InvalidOperationException . The target name comes from the message type: [QueueName("...")] sets the queue name and [ExchangeName("...")] sets the exchange name. Without the attribute, the name is the class name in lowercase (for example OrderCreated becomes ordercreated ).
docs.title: How it works

docs.text: RabbitMQWrapper opens a new connection and channel for every call and disposes them when the call ends. Messages are published as persistent and UTF-8 encoded. SendToQueueAsync publishes to the default exchange with the queue name as routing key. By default it first declares the queue as durable, non-exclusive and not auto-deleted. SendToExchangeAsync publishes to the named exchange with an empty routing key. It declares the exchange (durable, not auto-deleted) only when you pass an exchange type such as ExchangeType.Fanout . After each send the wrapper writes a trace entry through LogConsumer with the target name and the serialized body.
docs.title: Sending

docs.text: MessageReceiver starts a background task for each ReceiveFromQueue<T> or ReceiveFromExchange<T> call and returns immediately. The task keeps its connection and channel open until the CancellationToken is canceled. ReceiveFromQueue<T> consumes from the queue named by T . It does not declare the queue, so the queue must already exist. ReceiveFromExchange<T> declares a server-named queue, binds it to the exchange named by T with an empty routing key, and consumes from it. The exchange must already exist. Each delivery is decoded as UTF-8 and raised through the MessageReceived event as a MessageReceivedArgs (queue name and body). The body is the raw string; deserialize it yourself. The event handler runs on the RabbitMQ consumer thread. The receiver has no API to acknowledge messages. Pass autoAck: true unless you only want to peek: with autoAck: false messages stay unacknowledged and are redelivered when the channel closes. Deliveries that arrive while no handler is subscribed to MessageReceived are ignored. Exceptions in the background task (for example a failed connection) are not surfaced to the caller.
docs.title: Receiving

docs.text: RabbitMQLogProvider implements ILogProvider . Its constructor connects synchronously, opens a channel and declares the connector's DefaultExchangeName as a durable fanout exchange. Log calls build a LogMessage (application, host, IP addresses, level, thread, and so on), serialize it as JSON and put it in an in-memory queue. A dedicated worker thread publishes the queued messages to the exchange with an empty routing key. Publish failures are written to LogConsumer.Trace and the message is dropped. The worker thread is a foreground thread that only stops after the CancellationToken passed to the constructor is canceled, so cancel that token when your application shuts down or the process will not exit. The provider starts with no level enabled; call SetLevel before it writes anything.
docs.title: Log provider

docs.text: CrispyWaffle.Redis CrispyWaffle.Redis connects CrispyWaffle to Redis . It has four parts: A cache repository for CacheManager . A log provider that publishes log messages to Redis Pub/Sub channels. A telemetry client that stores hits, events and metrics in Redis. Helpers for master/replica setups and quick counter operations. Use it when several processes or machines need a shared cache, when you want log messages streamed to listeners in real time, or when you want lightweight counters stored in Redis. Package CrispyWaffle.Redis Namespace CrispyWaffle.Redis.Cache , CrispyWaffle.Redis.Log , CrispyWaffle.Redis.Log.PropagationStrategy , CrispyWaffle.Redis.Telemetry , CrispyWaffle.Redis.Utils , CrispyWaffle.Redis.Utils.Communications Install dotnet add package CrispyWaffle.Redis Depends on CrispyWaffle , CrispyWaffle.Configuration , StackExchange.Redis , StackExchange.Redis.Extensions.Core How it works The connector Everything in this package goes through a RedisConnector . The connector builds a StackExchange.Redis.Extensions RedisConfiguration with these settings: AbortOnConnectFail = false and AllowAdmin = true . A server enumeration strategy of All servers, Any role, and Throw on unreachable servers. A host list parsed from a comma-separated string of host[:port] entries. The port defaults to 6379 when it's missing. From that configuration, the connector creates a RedisConnectionPoolManager and a RedisClient . Every connector needs an ISerializer from StackExchange.Redis.Extensions.Core . That serializer converts cached values to and from bytes. The package doesn't include an implementation, so either reference a serializer package such as StackExchange.Redis.Extensions.System.Text.Json or write your own (see Getting started ). You can create a connector in several ways: From an IConnection ( Host , Port and Credentials.Password are used; the username is ignored). From a host and a port. From a raw host list. From a MasterSlaveConfiguration , which combines two connections. From an existing IRedisClient and IRedisConnectionPoolManager . Register the connector as a singleton, because it owns the connection pool. QueuePrefix defaults to "crispy-waffle" . The Pub/Sub log provider uses it to name channels. The overloads that take a queuePrefix throw ArgumentNullException when it's null . Cache repository RedisCacheRepository implements ICacheRepository , so you can add it to CacheManager alongside other repositories. The ICacheRepository methods always use database 0 ( IRedisClient.Db0 ) and the connector's serializer. Sub-key entries are stored as Redis hashes. SetAsync(value, key, subKey) reads the whole hash, sets one field, and writes the hash back with FireAndForget . SetToDatabase , GetFromDatabase , TryGetFromDatabase and RemoveFromDatabase work with any database number and call the connector serializer directly. Errors depend on ShouldPropagateExceptions , which defaults to false : When it's false , failures are logged instead of thrown. Exceptions whose message contains "timeout" go to LogConsumer.Trace ; all others go to LogConsumer.Handle . OperationCanceledException and argument-validation exceptions are always rethrown. GetAsync throws InvalidOperationException when the key is missing. It also throws InvalidOperationException after logging a suppressed error, so a missing key and a failed call look the same to the caller. The TryGetAsync overloads return (false, default) in both of those cases instead. Dispose() disposes the underlying RedisConnector . If several components share one connector, don't dispose the repository until all of them are done. Pub/Sub log provider PubSubRedisLogProvider is an ILogProvider . Each logging call that passes the level check builds a LogMessage , serializes it to JSON, and adds it to an in-memory ConcurrentQueue<string> . The LogMessage carries: The date, host name and process ID. The local and remote IP addresses. The operation, user agent, thread ID and thread name. A new GUID as the message Id . The constructor starts a dedicated worker thread named "Message queue Redis log provider worker". The thread waits one second and then loops. Each pass drains the queue and hands every message to the configured IPropagationStrategy . When the queue is empty and the CancellationToken passed to the constructor has been cancelled, the worker exits. The worker is a foreground thread and doesn't sleep between passes. Cancel the token when your application shuts down, or the thread keeps the process alive. If publishing a message throws, the worker logs the exception through LogConsumer.Debug and moves on to the next message. The provider's log level starts at no levels, so it records nothing until you call SetLevel . Each propagation strategy publishes two messages: The queue name to the channel {QueuePrefix}-queues , so listeners can discover which channels are active. The serialized log message to {QueuePrefix}-{queue name} . Strategy Queue name GeneralPropagation general OperationPropagationStrategy EnvironmentHelper.Operation (set with EnvironmentHelper.SetOperation ) ProcessPropagation EnvironmentHelper.ProcessId Telemetry client RedisTelemetryClient implements ITelemetryClient : Hits are string counters in database HitDatabase . Metrics are hash counters in database MetricDatabase , with one hash per metric and one field per variation. Events are serialized strings stored in the database whose number is the event's Category , under the event's Name . Exceptions and dependencies are counted in the hashes Exceptions_{suffix} and Dependencies_{suffix} in MetricDatabase . Writes use CommandFlags.FireAndForget , and reads use CommandFlags.PreferReplica . Getting started Start Redis locally. The repository's docker-compose.yml runs redis:6.2-alpine on port 6379 with the password myP@ssw0rd . Then create a serializer, a connection and a connector, and register them: using System.Text.Json; using System.Threading; using CrispyWaffle.Cache; using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Configuration; using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Redis.Cache; using CrispyWaffle.Redis.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Redis.Log.PropagationStrategy; using CrispyWaffle.Redis.Telemetry; using CrispyWaffle.Redis.Utils.Communications; using CrispyWaffle.Telemetry; using StackExchange.Redis.Extensions.Core; public sealed class SystemTextJsonRedisSerializer : ISerializer { private readonly JsonSerializerOptions _options = new(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web); public byte[] Serialize<T>(T item) => JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes(item, _options); public T Deserialize<T>(byte[] serializedObject) => JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>(serializedObject, _options); } public static class RedisBootstrap { public static void Configure(CancellationToken shutdownToken) { var connection = new Connection { Host = "localhost", Port = 6379, Credentials = { Password = "myP@ssw0rd" }, }; var connector = new RedisConnector( connection, new SystemTextJsonRedisSerializer(), "my-app" ); // One connector per process: it owns the connection pool. ServiceLocator.Register(connector); // Cache CacheManager.AddRepository(new RedisCacheRepository(connector)); // Logging LogConsumer .AddProvider( new PubSubRedisLogProvider(connector, new GeneralPropagation(), shutdownToken) ) .SetLevel(LogLevel.Production); // Telemetry TelemetryAnalytics.AddClient(new RedisTelemetryClient(connector, "my-app")); } } After that, await CacheManager.SetAsync("value", "my-key") , LogConsumer.Info("...") and TelemetryAnalytics.TrackHit("home") all reach Redis. Reference RedisConnector public class RedisConnector : IDisposable owns the Redis connection pool and the IRedisClient that every other type in this package uses. It has the [ConnectionName("Redis")] attribute. Member Description RedisConnector(IConnection connection, ISerializer serializer) / RedisConnector(IConnection connection, ISerializer serializer, string queuePrefix) Connects to connection.Host:connection.Port with connection.Credentials.Password . The queuePrefix overload throws ArgumentNullException when queuePrefix is null . RedisConnector(string host, int port, string password, ISerializer serializer) / RedisConnector(string host, int port, string password, ISerializer serializer, string queuePrefix) Connects to a single host and port. RedisConnector(string hostsList, string password, ISerializer serializer) / RedisConnector(string hostsList, string password, ISerializer serializer, string queuePrefix) Connects to a comma-separated list of host[:port] entries (default port 6379 ). All other constructors except the IRedisClient one end up here. RedisConnector(MasterSlaveConfiguration configuration, ISerializer serializer) / RedisConnector(MasterSlaveConfiguration configuration, ISerializer serializer, string queuePrefix) Connects using configuration.HostsList and configuration.Password . RedisConnector(IRedisClient client, IRedisConnectionPoolManager connectionPoolManager, ISerializer serializer, string queuePrefix) Wraps an existing client and pool manager, for example in tests or when you configure StackExchange.Redis.Extensions yourself. queuePrefix isn't validated. Serializer The ISerializer passed to the constructor. Cache The IRedisClient (StackExchange.Redis.Extensions) used by RedisCacheRepository . Subscriber An ISubscriber from a pooled connection. Used to publish and subscribe to channels. DefaultDatabase The default IDatabase of a pooled connection. QueuePrefix Prefix for Pub/Sub channel names. Defaults to "crispy-waffle" . GetDatabase(int databaseNumber, object asyncState = null) Returns the IDatabase with the given number from a pooled connection. GetDefaultServer() Returns the IServer for the first configured endpoint. Dispose() Disposes the connection pool manager. Calling it again has no effect. RedisCacheRepository public class RedisCacheRepository : ICacheRepository, IDisposable is a cache repository backed by Redis. It reads and writes database 0, except for the *Database methods. Member Description RedisCacheRepository(RedisConnector connector) Constructor. Uses connector.Cache for the ICacheRepository operations. ShouldPropagateExceptions When true , Redis errors are rethrown. When false (default), they are logged and suppressed. SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, TimeSpan? ttl = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Stores value under key , with an optional expiry. When the token can be canceled, it waits for the write or the cancellation, whichever comes first, and throws OperationCanceledException on cancellation. Returns ValueTask . SetAsync<T>(T value, string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Stores value as field subKey of the hash key . Throws ArgumentException when key or subKey is null or empty, and ArgumentNullException when value is null for a reference type. Returns ValueTask . GetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Returns the value stored under key . Throws ArgumentException for an empty key, and InvalidOperationException ("Unable to get the item with key ...") when the key doesn't exist or a suppressed error occurred. Returns ValueTask<T> . GetAsync<T>(string key, string subKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Currently ignores subKey and behaves like GetAsync<T>(key) . Because sub-key values are stored as hashes, reading them this way fails. Use TryGetAsync<T>(key, subKey) to read a hash field. TryGetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Returns (true, value) when key exists. Returns (false, default) when it doesn't, or when an error is suppressed. docs.text: CrispyWaffle.Redis connects CrispyWaffle to Redis . It has four parts: A cache repository for CacheManager . A log provider that publishes log messages to Redis Pub/Sub channels. A telemetry client that stores hits, events and metrics in Redis. Helpers for master/replica setups and quick counter operations. Use it when several processes or machines need a shared cache, when you want log messages streamed to listeners in real time, or when you want lightweight counters stored in Redis. docs.text: Everything in this package goes through a RedisConnector . The connector builds a StackExchange.Redis.Extensions RedisConfiguration with these settings: AbortOnConnectFail = false and AllowAdmin = true . A server enumeration strategy of All servers, Any role, and Throw on unreachable servers. A host list parsed from a comma-separated string of host[:port] entries. The port defaults to 6379 when it's missing. From that configuration, the connector creates a RedisConnectionPoolManager and a RedisClient . Every connector needs an ISerializer from StackExchange.Redis.Extensions.Core . That serializer converts cached values to and from bytes. The package doesn't include an implementation, so either reference a serializer package such as StackExchange.Redis.Extensions.System.Text.Json or write your own (see Getting started ). You can create a connector in several ways: From an IConnection ( Host , Port and Credentials.Password are used; the username is ignored). From a host and a port. From a raw host list. From a MasterSlaveConfiguration , which combines two connections. From an existing IRedisClient and IRedisConnectionPoolManager . Register the connector as a singleton, because it owns the connection pool. QueuePrefix defaults to "crispy-waffle" . The Pub/Sub log provider uses it to name channels. The overloads that take a queuePrefix throw ArgumentNullException when it's null .
docs.title: The connector

docs.text: RedisCacheRepository implements ICacheRepository , so you can add it to CacheManager alongside other repositories. The ICacheRepository methods always use database 0 ( IRedisClient.Db0 ) and the connector's serializer. Sub-key entries are stored as Redis hashes. SetAsync(value, key, subKey) reads the whole hash, sets one field, and writes the hash back with FireAndForget . SetToDatabase , GetFromDatabase , TryGetFromDatabase and RemoveFromDatabase work with any database number and call the connector serializer directly. Errors depend on ShouldPropagateExceptions , which defaults to false : When it's false , failures are logged instead of thrown. Exceptions whose message contains "timeout" go to LogConsumer.Trace ; all others go to LogConsumer.Handle . OperationCanceledException and argument-validation exceptions are always rethrown. GetAsync throws InvalidOperationException when the key is missing. It also throws InvalidOperationException after logging a suppressed error, so a missing key and a failed call look the same to the caller. The TryGetAsync overloads return (false, default) in both of those cases instead. Dispose() disposes the underlying RedisConnector . If several components share one connector, don't dispose the repository until all of them are done.
docs.title: Cache repository

docs.text: PubSubRedisLogProvider is an ILogProvider . Each logging call that passes the level check builds a LogMessage , serializes it to JSON, and adds it to an in-memory ConcurrentQueue<string> . The LogMessage carries: The date, host name and process ID. The local and remote IP addresses. The operation, user agent, thread ID and thread name. A new GUID as the message Id . The constructor starts a dedicated worker thread named "Message queue Redis log provider worker". The thread waits one second and then loops. Each pass drains the queue and hands every message to the configured IPropagationStrategy . When the queue is empty and the CancellationToken passed to the constructor has been cancelled, the worker exits. The worker is a foreground thread and doesn't sleep between passes. Cancel the token when your application shuts down, or the thread keeps the process alive. If publishing a message throws, the worker logs the exception through LogConsumer.Debug and moves on to the next message. The provider's log level starts at no levels, so it records nothing until you call SetLevel . Each propagation strategy publishes two messages: The queue name to the channel {QueuePrefix}-queues , so listeners can discover which channels are active. The serialized log message to {QueuePrefix}-{queue name} . Strategy Queue name GeneralPropagation general OperationPropagationStrategy EnvironmentHelper.Operation (set with EnvironmentHelper.SetOperation ) ProcessPropagation EnvironmentHelper.ProcessId

docs.text: RedisTelemetryClient implements ITelemetryClient : Hits are string counters in database HitDatabase . Metrics are hash counters in database MetricDatabase , with one hash per metric and one field per variation. Events are serialized strings stored in the database whose number is the event's Category , under the event's Name . Exceptions and dependencies are counted in the hashes Exceptions_{suffix} and Dependencies_{suffix} in MetricDatabase . Writes use CommandFlags.FireAndForget , and reads use CommandFlags.PreferReplica .

docs.text: Start Redis locally. The repository's docker-compose.yml runs redis:6.2-alpine on port 6379 with the password myP@ssw0rd . Then create a serializer, a connection and a connector, and register them: using System.Text.Json; using System.Threading; using CrispyWaffle.Cache; using CrispyWaffle.Composition; using CrispyWaffle.Configuration; using CrispyWaffle.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Redis.Cache; using CrispyWaffle.Redis.Log; using CrispyWaffle.Redis.Log.PropagationStrategy; using CrispyWaffle.Redis.Telemetry; using CrispyWaffle.Redis.Utils.Communications; using CrispyWaffle.Telemetry; using StackExchange.Redis.Extensions.Core; public sealed class SystemTextJsonRedisSerializer : ISerializer { private readonly JsonSerializerOptions _options = new(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web); public byte[] Serialize<T>(T item) => JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes(item, _options); public T Deserialize<T>(byte[] serializedObject) => JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>(serializedObject, _options); } public static class RedisBootstrap { public static void Configure(CancellationToken shutdownToken) { var connection = new Connection { Host = "localhost", Port = 6379, Credentials = { Password = "myP@ssw0rd" }, }; var connector = new RedisConnector( connection, new SystemTextJsonRedisSerializer(), "my-app" ); // One connector per process: it owns the connection pool. ServiceLocator.Register(connector); // Cache CacheManager.AddRepository(new RedisCacheRepository(connector)); // Logging LogConsumer .AddProvider( new PubSubRedisLogProvider(connector, new GeneralPropagation(), shutdownToken) ) .SetLevel(LogLevel.Production); // Telemetry TelemetryAnalytics.AddClient(new RedisTelemetryClient(connector, "my-app")); } } After that, await CacheManager.SetAsync("value", "my-key") , LogConsumer.Info("...") and TelemetryAnalytics.TrackHit("home") all reach Redis.

CrispyWaffle.Utils CrispyWaffle.Utils contains communication helpers: an FTP client for uploading files and managing a remote directory, and an SMTP mailer for sending plain-text and HTML e-mail with attachments. It also has an extension that renders a MailMessage as raw EML and the exceptions these helpers throw. SmtpMailer currently sends only when the application runs on .NET Framework (through the netstandard2.0 build). On .NET (Core) SendAsync throws before sending; see SMTP mailer . Package CrispyWaffle.Utils Namespace CrispyWaffle.Utils.Communications , CrispyWaffle.Utils.Extensions , CrispyWaffle.Utils.GoodPractices Install dotnet add package CrispyWaffle.Utils Depends on CrispyWaffle , CrispyWaffle.Configuration (no third-party package; uses System.Net FTP and SMTP classes) How it works FTP client FtpClient works on one remote directory, set in the constructor. A trailing / on the directory is removed. Every URL is built as ftp://{host}:{port}/{remoteDirectory}/{path} . Requests use FtpWebRequest in passive mode with the configured credentials. Public methods take a lock, so one instance can be shared between threads, but calls run one at a time. Whether a path is treated as a file or a directory depends on whether it has a file extension. A path with an extension is uploaded or deleted as a file; a path without one is created or removed as a directory. Upload creates the remote directory if it does not exist, deletes an existing file with the same name, and then uploads the bytes. ClearDirectory deletes every entry listed in the remote directory, removes the directory, and creates it again empty. FTP errors are wrapped in FtpClientException . An existence check that fails with a WebException is treated as "does not exist". FtpWebRequest is marked obsolete in .NET 6 and later, and Microsoft recommends a third-party FTP library for new development. SMTP mailer SmtpMailer wraps one SmtpClient and one MailMessage . Create one instance per e-mail and dispose it after sending. The client always uses SSL and a timeout of 300 seconds. The sender comes from SmtpMailerOptions.FromAddress and FromName . Build the message in this order: SetSubject , SetRecipients , SetReplyTo , SetReadNotificationTo , SetPriority in any order. SetMessageBody once. A second call throws MessageException . AddAttachment , only after SetMessageBody with an HTML body; otherwise it throws (see the reference below). SendAsync . The plain-text body is the main body. When an HTML body is given, it is added as a text/html alternate view, so mail clients that support HTML show it instead. SendAsync behaves as follows: It first renders the message with MailMessageExtensions.RawMessage , even when debug is off. That method only works on .NET Framework (see its reference entry), so on .NET (Core) SendAsync throws NullReferenceException before anything is sent. When SmtpMailerOptions.EnableDebug is true , the raw message is written as an .eml file through LogConsumer.DebugTo , named {subject} {timestamp}.{guid}.eml . When SmtpMailerOptions.IsSandbox is true , nothing is sent. A trace entry is written and the method returns. Otherwise the message is sent with SmtpClient.SendMailAsync . Send errors are tracked with TelemetryAnalytics.TrackMetric("SMTPError", message) and then handled by type: Socket errors (an inner-inner SocketException ) and SMTP replies containing 4.7.1 or 5.0.3 store a flag in CacheManager for 15 minutes, keyed by the calling method. While the flag exists, SendAsync calls from the same method skip sending without an error. The exception is not rethrown. This only works when a cache repository is registered with CacheManager . Replies containing 4.4.2 or 4.7.0 are rethrown. Any other exception is passed to LogConsumer.Handle and not rethrown. In other words, SendAsync completing does not mean the e-mail was delivered. Getting started using System.Collections.Generic; using CrispyWaffle.Utils.Communications; using var mailer = new SmtpMailer( "smtp.example.com", 587, "user@example.com", "password", "Example App", "no-reply@example.com" ); mailer.SetSubject("Welcome"); mailer.SetRecipients(new Dictionary { ["Jane Doe"] = "jane@example.com" }); mailer.SetMessageBody("Welcome to Example App.", "

Welcome to Example App.

"); await mailer.SendAsync(); Reference SmtpMailer public class SmtpMailer : IMailer — builds and sends one e-mail through an SMTP server. The class has [ConnectionName("SMTP")] . Member Description SmtpMailer(IConnection connection, SmtpMailerOptions options) Constructor. Takes host, port, user name and password from connection . Throws ArgumentNullException when connection or options is null . SmtpMailer(string host, int port, string userName, string password, string senderDisplayName, string senderEmailAddress) Constructor. Builds a Connection and an SmtpMailerOptions (sandbox and debug off) from the arguments. SetSubject(string subject) Sets the subject, UTF-8 encoded. SetRecipients(Dictionary recipients) Adds a To address for each entry. The key is the display name and the value is the address. Does nothing when recipients is null . Throws ArgumentNullException when an address is null or whitespace. SetMessageBody(string plainTextMessage, string htmlMessage) Sets the plain-text body (UTF-8) and, when htmlMessage is not null or whitespace, adds it as a text/html alternate view. Throws MessageException when called a second time. AddAttachment(Attachment attachment) Adds an attachment. Throws NullMessageException when SetMessageBody was not called. The attachment is skipped silently when the HTML body is longer than 150,000 characters. Errors while adding are passed to LogConsumer.Handle . The HTML-length check dereferences the HTML body, so when SetMessageBody was called without an HTML body this method throws NullReferenceException . SetReplyTo(string name, string emailAddress) Adds a reply-to address and a Return-path header. SetReadNotificationTo(string name, string emailAddress) Adds a Disposition-Notification-To header (read receipt request). SetPriority(MailPriority priority) Sets the message priority. SendAsync() Sends the message, honoring IsSandbox and EnableDebug . See How it works for error handling. Returns Task . Dispose() Disposes the message and the SMTP client. Dispose(bool disposing) protected virtual . Override to release extra resources in a subclass. IMailer public interface IMailer : IDisposable — contract for a mailer. SmtpMailer is the only implementation in the package. Member Description SetSubject(string subject) Sets the subject. SetRecipients(Dictionary recipients) Adds recipients (name to address). SetMessageBody(string plainTextMessage, string htmlMessage) Sets the plain-text and HTML bodies. SetReadNotificationTo(string name, string emailAddress) Requests a read receipt. SetPriority(MailPriority priority) Sets the priority. SetReplyTo(string name, string emailAddress) Sets the reply-to address. AddAttachment(Attachment attachment) Adds an attachment. SendAsync() Sends the message. Returns Task . SmtpMailerOptions public class SmtpMailerOptions — sender and behavior settings for SmtpMailer . Member Description FromAddress Sender e-mail address. FromName Sender display name. IsSandbox When true , SendAsync does not send. Default false . EnableDebug When true , SendAsync writes the raw message as an .eml file through TextFileLogProvider . Default false . FtpClient public class FtpClient — uploads files to and manages one directory on an FTP server. Member Description FtpClient(IConnection connection, string remoteDirectory) Constructor. Takes host, port (21 when connection is null ), user name and password from connection . FtpClient(string host, int port, string userName, string password, string remoteDirectory) Constructor. Removes a trailing / from remoteDirectory . Throws ArgumentNullException when remoteDirectory is null or whitespace. Upload(string fileName, byte[] bytes) Creates the remote directory when it does not exist, deletes an existing fileName , and uploads bytes . Returns true when the server confirms the upload. Throws ArgumentNullException when an argument is null , and FtpClientException when the upload fails. CreateDirectory(string name) Creates the subdirectory name under the remote directory. Returns true when the server confirms it. Throws FtpClientException on failure. Remove(string path) Deletes path under the remote directory: a file when it has an extension, otherwise a directory. Throws FtpClientException when the server does not answer with FileActionOK or the request fails. ClearDirectory() Deletes every entry listed in the remote directory, removes the directory, and creates it again. MailMessageExtensions public static class MailMessageExtensions — extension methods for System.Net.Mail.MailMessage . Member Description RawMessage(this MailMessage self) Returns a MemoryStream with the message in RFC 822 (EML) format, positioned at the start. It calls internal System.Net.Mail members through reflection and looks for a MailWriter(Stream) constructor, which exists only on .NET Framework. On .NET (Core) the constructor is MailWriter(Stream, bool) , so the method throws NullReferenceException . FtpClientException public class FtpClientException : Exception — thrown by FtpClient when an FTP operation fails. Marked [Serializable] . Member Description FtpClientException() Constructor with the default message. FtpClientException(string message) Constructor with a message. FtpClientException(string message, Exception innerException) Constructor with a message and inner exception. FtpClientException(string path, string action, FtpStatusCode responseCode) Message: Unable to {action} the path/file {path} in the FtpClient host. Status code: {responseCode} . FtpClientException(string path, string action, Exception innerException) Same message with status code 0 , and the inner exception. Used when the request throws a WebException . FtpClientException(SerializationInfo info, StreamingContext context) protected . Deserialization constructor. MessageException public class MessageException : Exception — thrown by SmtpMailer.SetMessageBody when the body was already set. Message: The message cannot be set more than once for the same instance of Email class . Marked [Serializable] . Member Description MessageException() Constructor with the default message. MessageException(SerializationInfo info, StreamingContext context) protected . Deserialization constructor. NullMessageException public class NullMessageException : Exception — thrown by SmtpMailer.AddAttachment when the body has not been set. Message: Unable to set the attachment of message before the message itself . Marked [Serializable] . Member Description NullMessageException() Constructor with the default message. NullMessageException(SerializationInfo info, StreamingContext context) protected . Deserialization constructor. Examples Send an e-mail with a stored connection and an attachment Use a Connection from configuration and SmtpMailerOptions to keep sending off in test environments. using System.Collections.Generic; using System.IO; using System.Net.Mail; using System.Text; using CrispyWaffle.Configuration; using CrispyWaffle.Utils.Communications; var connection = new Connection { Host = "smtp.example.com", Port = 587, Credentials = { Username = "user@example.com", Password = "password" }, }; var options = new SmtpMailerOptions { FromAddress = "reports@example.com", FromName = "Reports", IsSandbox = false, }; using var mailer = new SmtpMailer(connection, options); mailer.SetSubject("Daily report"); mailer.SetRecipients(new Dictionary { ["Ops"] = "ops@example.com" }); mailer.SetReplyTo("Support", "support@example.com"); mailer.SetPriority(MailPriority.High); mailer.SetMessageBody("The daily report is attached.", "

The daily report is attached.

"); var csv = new MemoryStream(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("date,total\n2024-01-01,10\n")); mailer.AddAttachment(new Attachment(csv, "report.csv", "text/csv")); await mailer.SendAsync(); Upload a file over FTP Upload a file to /exports on the server, replacing any file with the same name. using System.IO; using CrispyWaffle.Utils.Communications; using CrispyWaffle.Utils.GoodPractices; var ftp = new FtpClient("ftp.example.com", 21, "user", "password", "exports/"); try { var uploaded = ftp.Upload("report.csv", File.ReadAllBytes("report.csv")); } catch (FtpClientException e) { // e.Message: "Unable to create the path/file report.csv in the FtpClient host. Status code: 0" } Save a message as an EML file RawMessage returns the message exactly as it would be sent. This works on .NET Framework only. using System.IO; using System.Net.Mail; using CrispyWaffle.Utils.Extensions; using var message = new MailMessage("from@example.com", "to@example.com", "Subject", "Body"); using var raw = message.RawMessage(); using var file = File.Create("message.eml"); raw.CopyTo(file); See also CrispyWaffle.Configuration Logging Caching Telemetry
